openQuestions: Were any of the 30-plus candidate oxides proposed by Stanev, Oses, Kusne, Rodriguez, Paglione, Curtarolo and Takeuchi in 2018 ever synthesized and measured? Searches surfaced no follow-up experimental paper testing them, and the review by Tran and colleagues states generally that ML-predicted superconductors have rarely been confirmed — but an explicit negative result, or a named compound that was tested and failed, would be much stronger than an absence of evidence. Worth checking the citing literature of the npj paper directly.

The exact record counts and cleaning rules for each SuperCon release are inconsistent across sources (roughly 16,400 versus 26,323 versus about 32,000 entries in different descriptions). Any number quoted in the book should be tied to a specific named release (e.g. a dated MDR SuperCon Datasheet DOI), not to 'SuperCon' generically.

The frequently repeated claim that the La(1-x)Sr(x)CuO4 family has about 550 SuperCon entries containing visible outliers against the known doping dependence of Tc came from a search summary, not from a source read end to end. The primary paper making that specific argument should be located and cited directly before the LSCO example is used.

No open, stable URL was found for the original 1950 Ginzburg-Landau paper; the Springer reprint chapter is paywalled. A book citation will need either the Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 20, 1064 reference given without a link, or a substitute such as Ginzburg's 2004 Nobel Lecture or Gor'kov's 1959 microscopic derivation of Ginzburg-Landau from BCS (which was not researched here).

Affiliations for several author teams (Hamidieh; Roter and Dordevic; Lee, Hattrick-Simpers, Kim and von Lilienfeld; Tran and colleagues; Li, Hsu and Huang; the full Meredig author list) were inferred from search summaries rather than read off the papers. Each should be checked against the published title page before print.

Whether the Zr-In-Ni superconductor reported by Pogue and colleagues has been independently reproduced by another group is unknown from this research. If the book presents it as the one clear ML discovery success, independent confirmation matters.

The current status of the H3S and LaH10 dispute as of 2026 was not established. The Hirsch-Marsiglio objections, the Minkov Nature Communications author correction, and later flux-trapping exchanges are an active back-and-forth; the book should state the position as of a specific date rather than declaring the matter settled either way.

verdicts.claim: BCS theory: Bardeen, Cooper, Schrieffer, Physical Review 108, 1175-1204 (1957), DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175, Dept. of Physics, University of Illinois, Urbana; gap Delta(T) closes continuously at Tc.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: J. Bardeen; L. N. Cooper; J. R. Schrieffer, 'Theory of Superconductivity', Phys. Rev. 108(5), 1175-1204 (1 Dec 1957), DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175. URL resolves to that exact work. Caveat on framing, not fact: the phrase 'order parameter' is Ginzburg-Landau/Gor'kov language and does not appear as such in BCS 1957 — BCS derives Delta(T) vanishing continuously at Tc and the specific-heat jump. Safer phrasing: 'BCS supplies the microscopic content, a gap Delta(T) that closes continuously at Tc; the identification of that gap with a Ginzburg-Landau order parameter is Gor'kov's 1959 result.' The trailing editorial sentence ('the theoretical object every Tc-prediction model is implicitly approximating') is the author's interpretation, not a claim of the 1957 paper.

verdicts.claim: Ginzburg 2004 Nobel Lecture, Reviews of Modern Physics 76, 981-998, DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.76.981; original Ginzburg-Landau paper Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 20, 1064 (1950); Lebedev Institute.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: Vitaly L. Ginzburg, 'Nobel Lecture: On superconductivity and superfluidity (what I have and have not managed to do) as well as on the "physical minimum" at the beginning of the XXI century', Rev. Mod. Phys. 76(3), 981-998 (2004). DOI resolves correctly. The Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 20, 1064 (1950) reference for the original V. L. Ginzburg and L. D. Landau paper is the standard, correct citation; the statement that no stable open DOI was located is accurate as of this check.

verdicts.claim: SuperCon provenance: NIMS, traceable to a national 'Multi-Core' project begun in 1987 after the 1986 cuprate discovery; distributed via MatNavi; web GUI decommissioned 2021; now MDR SuperCon Datasheet under CC-BY with a new DOI per revision; record counts vary (~16,400 / 26,323 / ~32,000).
verdicts.correction: All verifiable elements check out. The 'Multi-Core' project was launched in 1987 at the then Science and Technology Agency (now MEXT) following the 1986 discovery of high-Tc oxide superconductors; the SuperCon web GUI was decommissioned in 2021 (NIMS/DICE notice, December 2021) and the data re-released via MDR from December 2022. The MDR collection page at https://mdr.nims.go.jp/collections/5712mb227 resolves, is titled 'MDR SuperCon Datasheet', carries CC-BY 4.0, and states DOIs are issued per revision (collection DOI https://doi.org/10.48505/nims.3837). The 26,323 figure is attested for the cleaned MDR SuperCon release; the ~16,400 figure traces to Stanev et al. 2018's own extraction, not to a NIMS release — worth saying so explicitly. The dossier's own caution about pinning any number to a dated release DOI is correct and should be followed.

verdicts.claim: SuperCon2 / Grobid-superconductors: Foppiano, Baptista de Castro, Ortiz Suarez, Terashima, Takano, Ishii, STAM: Methods 3, 2153633 (2023), arXiv Oct 2022; 40,324 records from 37,700 papers; co-authors at Inria/Sorbonne for Ortiz Suarez.
verdicts.correction: Citation and numbers are right; one affiliation is wrong. Correct: Luca Foppiano, Pedro Baptista de Castro, Pedro Ortiz Suarez, Kensei Terashima, Yoshihiko Takano, Masashi Ishii, 'Automatic extraction of materials and properties from superconductors scientific literature', Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods 3(1), 2153633 (2023), DOI 10.1080/27660400.2022.2153633; arXiv:2210.15600, submitted 26 October 2022. 40,324 records from 37,700 papers, captured fields (name, formula, class, shape, doping, substitution variables, substrate, Tc, applied pressure, measurement method) all confirmed. CORRECTION: Ortiz Suarez's affiliation in the publisher metadata is University of Mannheim, not Inria/Sorbonne. Also note the publisher renders the second author as 'Pedro Baptista Castro' while arXiv renders 'Pedro Baptista de Castro' — use the published journal form if citing the journal version. URL https://doi.org/10.1080/27660400.2022.2153633 resolves to this exact work.

verdicts.claim: 3DSC: Sommer, Willa, Schmalian, Friederich, Scientific Data 10, 816 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41597-023-02721-y, arXiv Dec 2022; augments SuperCon with approximate 3D crystal structures and shows structural information improves Tc prediction.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: '3DSC - a dataset of superconductors including crystal structures', Timo Sommer, Roland Willa, Jörg Schmalian, Pascal Friederich, Scientific Data 10(1), article 816 (21 Nov 2023). arXiv:2212.06071, submitted 12 December 2022, titled '3DSC - A New Dataset of Superconductors Including Crystal Structures'. The abstract states verbatim that they 'perform a statistical analysis and machine learning experiments to show that access to this structural information improves the prediction of the critical temperature', so the claim does not overstate. Affiliation (KIT) is consistent with the paper.

verdicts.claim: Stanev, Oses, Kusne, Rodriguez, Paglione, Curtarolo, Takeuchi, npj Computational Materials 4, 29 (2018), arXiv:1709.02727 submitted 8 Sept 2017; ~92% out-of-sample accuracy classifying above/below 10 K; SuperCon 12,000+ entries; more than 30 non-cuprate, non-iron-based oxide candidates from ICSD.
verdicts.correction: Fully verified. Title 'Machine learning modeling of superconducting critical temperature'; author list and order exactly as given; npj Comput. Mater. 4, article 29 (2018); DOI 10.1038/s41524-018-0085-8 resolves to this work; arXiv:1709.02727 submitted 8 September 2017. The abstract states '12,000+ known superconductors available via the SuperCon database' and ~92% accuracy; the body says the final candidate set 'has 35 members' and describes 'more than 30 non-cuprate and non-iron-based oxides as candidate materials'. One precision note for the book: the ~16,400 figure sometimes quoted for this paper is its raw SuperCon extraction, while ~12,000 is the modelled set — do not use them interchangeably.

verdicts.claim: Hamidieh, Computational Materials Science 154, 346-354 (2018), arXiv:1803.10260 March 2018; RMSE about 9.5 K; model predicts Tc only for assumed superconductors and does not say whether a compound superconducts; feature table became the UCI 'Superconductivity Data' set. Affiliation University of Pennsylvania.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: Kam Hamidieh, 'A data-driven statistical model for predicting the critical temperature of a superconductor', Computational Materials Science 154, 346-354 (November 2018), DOI 10.1016/j.commatsci.2018.07.052. arXiv:1803.10260 submitted 4 March 2018. The stated limitation is verbatim in the abstract: 'our model does not predict whether a material is a superconductor or not, it only gives predictions for superconductors', and the ±9.5 K RMSE is exact. Affiliation: University of Pennsylvania (Wharton Statistics) is supported by secondary sources but Crossref carries no affiliation field for this record — verify against the printed title page before print, as the dossier already flags. Note the dossier cites the arXiv URL; for a journal citation add DOI 10.1016/j.commatsci.2018.07.052.

verdicts.claim: Roter and Dordevic, Physica C 575, 1353689 (2020), arXiv:2002.07266 Feb 2020; element vectors learned from SuperCon compositions then Tc regression, R^2 about 0.93, new high-Tc candidates proposed. Affiliation University of Akron.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: B. Roter and S. V. Dordevic, Physica C: Superconductivity and its Applications 575, 1353689 (August 2020), DOI 10.1016/j.physc.2020.1353689; arXiv:2002.07266 submitted 17 February 2020; abstract states R^2 ≈ 0.93 and only chemical composition used. Benjamin Roter and Sasa V. Dordevic, Department of Physics, The University of Akron — confirmed. One citation nuance: the published journal title is 'Predicting new superconductors and their critical temperatures using machine learning', while the arXiv preprint title reads '...using unsupervised machine learning'. If the book calls this an 'unsupervised' approach, cite the arXiv title or note the discrepancy; the published version dropped the word.

verdicts.claim: Meredig, Antono, Church, Hutchinson, Ling, Paradiso, Blaiszik, Foster, Gibbons, Hattrick-Simpers, Mehta, Ward, Molecular Systems Design & Engineering 3, 819-825 (2018); random k-fold CV overestimates discovery usefulness; introduces leave-one-cluster-out CV plus a nearest-neighbour benchmark; superconductor Tc is the worked example.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms the full 12-author list in exactly the order given, 'Can machine learning identify the next high-temperature superconductor? Examining extrapolation performance for materials discovery', Mol. Syst. Des. Eng. 3(5), 819-825 (2018), DOI 10.1039/C8ME00012C — URL resolves. The LOCO CV plus nearest-neighbour benchmark description is accurate. Affiliation mapping (Citrine Informatics; University of Chicago / Argonne; NIST; SLAC) is consistent with the listed authors but was not read off the printed title page — check before print, as the dossier flags.

verdicts.claim: Jung, Jung, Cole, Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling 64(19), 7349-7375 (2024); ~4,000 SuperCon entries with no reported Tc or explicit non-superconductivity; median Tc taken per multiply-reported composition; cannot differentiate materials with multiple stable phases; family-specific models did not beat the general model.
verdicts.correction: Every specific claim is verbatim in the paper. Title: 'Machine-Learning Predictions of Critical Temperatures from Chemical Compositions of Superconductors', Son Gyo Jung, Guwon Jung, Jacqueline M. Cole, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 64(19), 7349-7375 (2024), DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c01137 — resolves. Quotes: 'includes around 4000 entries with either no reported superconducting transition temperature or a reported lack of superconductivity (Tc = 0 K)'; 'For chemical entries that were documented multiple times, we calculated the median Tc value'; 'the model cannot differentiate between materials which have multiple stable phases, each with distinct physical properties'; 'the regression models tailored to specific families of superconductors do not outperform the general model'. Affiliations (Cavendish Laboratory; ISIS Neutron and Muon Source and Scientific Computing Department, STFC RAL) confirmed in publisher metadata, plus Research Complex at Harwell.

verdicts.claim: Lee, Hattrick-Simpers, Kim, von Lilienfeld, arXiv:2406.14524 (June 2024, revised Nov 2024), journal version in Machine Learning: Science and Technology; similarity-based ridge regression on SuperCon, ~5 K average out-of-sample error; ~153,000 Materials Project entries screened; LiCuF4, Ag2H12S(NO)4, Na2H6PtO6 at roughly 315-316 K; no experimental verification claimed.
verdicts.correction: Verified against the arXiv record: 'High-Tc superconductor candidates proposed by machine learning', Siwoo Lee, Jason Hattrick-Simpers, Young-June Kim, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld (University of Toronto). Abstract confirms 'query-aware similarity-based ridge regression models on experimental SuperCon data achieve average Tc prediction errors of ~5 K', a scan of '~153k materials in the Materials Project', and the exact three candidates with LiCuF4 (316 K), Ag2H12S(NO)4 (316 K), Na2H6PtO6 (315 K). URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14524 resolves to this work. Journal version: Machine Learning: Science and Technology, DOI 10.1088/2632-2153/ae04c1 — add this DOI when citing the journal version. The interpretive sentence about extrapolation regime is the book's own argument, correctly flagged as such.

verdicts.claim: Tran, Dam, Kuenneth, Vu, Kino, 28-page review, Chemistry of Materials 36(22), 10939-10966 (2024), arXiv October 2025; states SuperCon data quality remains uncertain, ML struggles outside training distribution especially for high-pressure hydrides, and ML-predicted superconductors have rarely been experimentally confirmed.
verdicts.correction: Citation is real and correct except for one author's name form. Correct: Huan Tran, Hieu-Chi Dam, Christopher Kuenneth, VU NGOC TUOC, Hiori Kino, 'Superconductor Discovery in the Emerging Paradigm of Materials Informatics', Chemistry of Materials 36(22), 10939-10966 (2024), DOI 10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c01757. The dossier writes 'Tuoc N. Vu'; the printed byline is 'Vu Ngoc Tuoc' (Hanoi University of Science & Technology) — a book citing under a real author's name should match the printed byline exactly. Affiliations otherwise confirmed from publisher metadata: Georgia Tech (Tran); JAIST (Dam); University of Bayreuth (Kuenneth); Hanoi University of Science & Technology (Vu Ngoc Tuoc); NIMS (Kino). Page range 10939-10966 = 28 pages, confirmed. The arXiv posting is arXiv:2510.25971 (October 2025), i.e. a postprint appearing AFTER journal publication — that ordering is unusual and worth a word so it does not read as a typo. The three substantive assertions attributed to the review are consistent with its abstract and framing but were verified only at abstract/summary level, not by reading the 28 pages end to end; quote the review directly rather than paraphrasing if these lines are load-bearing.

verdicts.claim: Pogue et al., npj Computational Materials 9, 181 (2023), arXiv:2212.11855 Dec 2022; four closed-loop cycles more than doubled the discovery success rate; one new superconductor in the Zr-In-Ni system, five superconductors rediscovered absent from training data, two further phase diagrams flagged.
verdicts.correction: Fully verified, including the complete 18-author list in the exact order given. Crossref: 'Closed-loop superconducting materials discovery', npj Computational Materials 9(1), article 181 (5 Oct 2023), DOI 10.1038/s41524-023-01131-3 — URL resolves. arXiv:2212.11855 submitted 22 December 2022, titled 'Closed-loop machine learning for discovery of novel superconductors'. Abstract verbatim: 'success rates for superconductor discovery can be more than doubled. In four closed-loop cycles, we discovered a new superconductor in the Zr-In-Ni system, re-discovered five superconductors unknown in the training datasets, and identified two additional phase diagrams of interest'. The dossier's caveat about the modest scale of the win is fair and not an overstatement.

verdicts.claim: Choudhary and Garrity, npj Computational Materials 8, 244 (2022), arXiv:2205.00060 April 2022; BCS-inspired pre-screening of 1,736 materials, electron-phonon calculations for 1,058, 105 dynamically stable with Tc >= 5 K; example materials MoN, VC, VTe, KB6, Ru3NbC, V3Pt, ScN, LaN2, RuO2, TaC; predicting the Eliashberg function as an intermediate quantity improves the model over predicting Tc directly.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: 'Designing high-TC superconductors with BCS-inspired screening, density functional theory, and deep-learning', Kamal Choudhary and Kevin Garrity, npj Comput. Mater. 8(1), article 244 (22 Nov 2022), DOI 10.1038/s41524-022-00933-1 — resolves. arXiv:2205.00060 submitted 29 April 2022. All numbers (1736, 1058, 105) and the full example list match the abstract verbatim, as does 'by predicting the Eliashberg function as an intermediate quantity, we can improve model performance versus a direct DL prediction of Tc'. One-word precision fix: the abstract says 'Tc>5 K', not 'Tc >= 5 K'.

verdicts.claim: Xie, Quan, Hire, Deng, DeStefano, Salinas, Shah, Fanfarillo, Lim, Kim, Stewart, Hamlin, Hirschfeld, Hennig, npj Computational Materials 8, 14 (2022), arXiv:2106.05235 June 2021; SISSO symbolic regression on artificially generated alpha^2 F(omega) spectra and numerical Eliashberg solutions yields a closed-form Tc expression matching Allen-Dynes at low Tc and substantially outperforming it at high Tc.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms the 14-author list in exactly the order given, 'Machine learning of superconducting critical temperature from Eliashberg theory', npj Comput. Mater. 8(1), article 14 (25 Jan 2022), DOI 10.1038/s41524-021-00666-7 — resolves. arXiv:2106.05235 submitted 9 June 2021. Abstract verbatim: 'Using symbolic regression and the sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO) framework, together with a database of artificially generated alpha^2F functions... we derive a formula for Tc that performs as well as Allen-Dynes for low-Tc superconductors, and substantially better for higher-Tc ones.' University of Florida affiliation is correct.

verdicts.claim: Cerqueira, Sanna, Marques, Advanced Materials 36(1), 2307085 (2024), arXiv:2307.10728 July 2023; ~7,000 converged electron-phonon calculations train a model, ~200,000 metallic compounds evaluated, candidates above 5 K validated with DFPT, 541 compounds with Tc above 10 K identified; training labels are computed rather than experimental.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: 'Sampling the Materials Space for Conventional Superconducting Compounds', T. F. T. Cerqueira, A. Sanna, M. A. L. Marques, Advanced Materials 36(1), article 2307085 (online 2 Dec 2023, issue 2024), DOI 10.1002/adma.202307085 — resolves. One thing a strict reader will catch: the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2307.10728, 20 July 2023, titled 'Sampling the Whole Materials Space for Conventional Superconducting Materials') says 545 compounds with Tc above 10 K, while the published Advanced Materials version says 541. The dossier's 541 is right FOR THE JOURNAL VERSION; if the book cites the arXiv preprint the number must be 545. Everything else (≈7000 EPC calculations, ~200,000 metallic compounds, DFPT validation above 5 K) matches verbatim.

verdicts.claim: Shipley, Hutcheon, Needs, Pickard, Physical Review B 104, 054501 (2021), arXiv:2105.02296 May 2021; binary hydrides 10-500 GPa via crystal structure prediction, 'a learned model used to rank candidates', converged electron-phonon calculations for 121, 36 dynamically stable superconductors above 100 K; Editors' Suggestion; 'illustrates the standard hydride workflow: ML as a cost-reduction surrogate'.
verdicts.correction: The citation is correct but the method is mischaracterized, and this is load-bearing because the summary uses this paper as evidence that 'ML entered hydride work as a surrogate to triage structure-search candidates'. Bibliographic data confirmed: Alice M. Shipley, Michael J. Hutcheon, Richard J. Needs, Chris J. Pickard, 'High-throughput discovery of high-temperature conventional superconductors', Phys. Rev. B 104, 054501 (2021), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.104.054501, arXiv:2105.02296 submitted 5 May 2021; 121 converged electron-phonon calculations and 36 above-100 K dynamically stable superconductors confirmed verbatim. THE ERROR: the ranking model is NOT a machine-learning model. The abstract reads: 'Building a critical temperature (Tc) model, with inputs arising from density of states calculations and Gaspari-Gyorffy theory, allows us to predict which energetically competitive candidates are most promising for high-Tc superconductivity... and to refine the model in an iterative manner.' Neither the abstract nor the title invokes machine learning. Accurate replacement text: 'A high-throughput survey of binary hydrides across the periodic table from 10 to 500 GPa using crystal structure prediction, in which a physics-based Tc model built from density-of-states calculations and Gaspari-Gyorffy theory — refined iteratively against their own computed results, not a machine-learning surrogate — was used to rank candidates before converged electron-phonon calculations were run for 121 of them, yielding 36 dynamically stable superconductors above 100 K (18 above 200 K, including NaH6 at 248-279 K and CaH6 at 216-253 K at 100 GPa).' Cite Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques 2024 alone for the ML-surrogate point, since that paper does explicitly train a machine-learning model. SEPARATELY UNVERIFIABLE: the 'Editors' Suggestion' label could not be confirmed — APS pages (journals.aps.org and link.aps.org) return HTTP 403 to automated fetches and no secondary source attests it. Drop the claim or verify it by eye on the APS page before print.

verdicts.claim: Duan and colleagues predicted (H2S)2H2 metallization with Im-3m H3S at 191-204 K near 200 GPa (Scientific Reports 4, 6968, 2014); Drozdov, Eremets, Troyan, Ksenofontov, Shylin reported 203 K in the sulfur hydride system (Nature 525, 73-76, 2015) with a supporting isotope effect.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: 'Pressure-induced metallization of dense (H2S)2H2 with high-Tc superconductivity', Defang Duan, Yunxian Liu, Fubo Tian, Da Li, Xiaoli Huang, Zhonglong Zhao, Hongyu Yu, Bingbing Liu, Wenjing Tian, Tian Cui, Scientific Reports 4, article 6968 (10 Nov 2014), DOI 10.1038/srep06968 — URL resolves. The dossier's abbreviated author list ('Duan, Liu, Tian, Cui and co-workers') correctly names the first three and the senior author. Jilin University affiliation correct. The 191-204 K at ~200 GPa prediction and the Drozdov et al. Nature 525, 73-76 (2015) 203 K experiment with isotope effect are both standard and correctly stated. The framing that this came from structure search plus electron-phonon theory rather than data-driven ML is accurate.

verdicts.correction: Every element verified. PNAS 114(27), 6990-6995 (19 Jun 2017), 'Potential high-Tc superconducting lanthanum and yttrium hydrides at high pressure', Hanyu Liu, Ivan I. Naumov, Roald Hoffmann, N. W. Ashcroft, Russell J. Hemley — DOI 10.1073/pnas.1704505114 resolves. PRL 119, 107001 (2017), 'Hydrogen Clathrate Structures in Rare Earth Hydrides at High Pressures: Possible Route to Room-Temperature Superconductivity', Feng Peng, Ying Sun, Chris J. Pickard, Richard J. Needs, Qiang Wu, Yanming Ma — and the YH10 figure of 'up to 303 K at 400 GPa' is exactly what that paper predicts. PRL 122, 027001 (2019), 'Evidence for Superconductivity above 260 K in Lanthanum Superhydride at Megabar Pressures', Somayazulu, Ahart, Mishra, Geballe, Baldini, Meng, Struzhkin, Hemley. Nature 569(7757), 528-531 (2019), Drozdov, Kong, Minkov, Besedin, Kuzovnikov, Mozaffari, Balicas, Balakirev, Graf, Prakapenka, Greenberg, Knyazev, Tkacz, Eremets. Nature 578(7793), 66-69 (2020), Errea, Belli, Monacelli, Sanna, Koretsune, Tadano, Bianco, Calandra, Arita, Mauri, Flores-Livas — abstract states 'a colossal electron-phonon coupling of lambda ~ 3.5', confirming the dossier's figure.

verdicts.claim: Two Dias-led room-temperature claims retracted: carbonaceous sulfur hydride (Nature 586, 373-377, 2020, 15 C at 267 GPa) retracted 2022 (Retraction Note Nature 610, 804) over an undisclosed non-standard user-defined background subtraction of raw magnetic susceptibility data; N-doped lutetium hydride (Nature 615, 244-250, 2023) retracted November 2023 (Retraction Note Nature 624, 460) at the request of eight co-authors over provenance, measurements and data-processing protocols, with the journal separately finding credible, substantial, unresolved concerns about the resistance data.
verdicts.correction: Both retractions and both retraction rationales verified against the notes themselves. CSH: 'RETRACTED ARTICLE: Room-temperature superconductivity in a carbonaceous sulfur hydride', Snider, Dasenbrock-Gammon, McBride, Debessai, Vindana, Vencatasamy, Lawler, Salamat, Dias, Nature 586, 373-377 (2020); Retraction Note Nature 610(7933), 804 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41586-022-05294-9 — the URL given in the dossier resolves to the RETRACTION NOTE, which is appropriate here but should be labelled as such. The note states the background subtractions 'used a non-standard, user-defined procedure', that details were not specified in the paper, and that its validity was called into question. Lutetium hydride: Dasenbrock-Gammon, Snider, McBride, Pasan, Durkee, Khalvashi-Sutter, Munasinghe, Dissanayake, Lawler, Salamat, Dias, Nature 615, 244-250 (8 Mar 2023); Retraction Note Nature 624, 460 (7 Nov 2023), DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06774-2. Precision improvement: the retraction was requested by eight of the eleven authors, named in the note (Dasenbrock-Gammon, Snider, McBride, Pasan, Durkee, Dissanayake, Lawler, Salamat); Dias did not join the request. Their stated view — that the paper 'does not accurately reflect the provenance of the investigated materials, the experimental measurements undertaken and the data-processing protocols applied' — matches the dossier's paraphrase closely; quote it verbatim. Minor: the dossier's people field lists Snider first, but Dasenbrock-Gammon is first author of the 2023 lutetium hydride paper.

verdicts.claim: Hirsch and Marsiglio, Physical Review B 103, 134505 (2021), argue hydride observations rule out conventional superconductivity; Hirsch has also published with D. van der Marel; Eremets group rebuts with SQUID magnetometry reporting superconducting parameters for Im-3m H3S and Fm-3m LaH10 — Minkov, Prakapenka, Greenberg, Eremets, Nature Communications 13, 3194 (2022), subject to a 2023 author correction.
verdicts.correction: THE AUTHOR LIST FOR THE MINKOV PAPER IS WRONG — it names a person who is not an author and drops four who are. Correct: V. S. Minkov, S. L. Bud'ko, F. F. Balakirev, V. B. Prakapenka, S. Chariton, R. J. Husband, H. P. Liermann, M. I. Eremets, 'Magnetic field screening in hydrogen-rich high-temperature superconductors', Nature Communications 13, 3194 (9 June 2022), DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-30782-x, URL https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-30782-x. E. Greenberg is NOT an author of this paper — he is an author of the separate Drozdov et al. Nature 569, 528 (2019) LaH10 paper, and the two have evidently been conflated. Affiliations should read: Max-Planck-Institut für Chemie, Mainz (Minkov, Eremets); Ames Laboratory / Iowa State (Bud'ko); Los Alamos National Laboratory (Balakirev); University of Chicago, GSECARS (Prakapenka, Chariton); DESY (Husband, Liermann). The 2023 author correction is Nature Communications 14, 5322 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-40837-2 — cite that DOI rather than describing it vaguely; note also that in March 2024 Nature Communications editors were alerted to further concerns about raw-data processing, and a further exchange ran as Nature Communications 15 (2024), DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-52327-0. The Hirsch-Marsiglio citation itself is correct: 'Nonstandard superconductivity or no superconductivity in hydrides under high pressure', Phys. Rev. B 103, 134505 (6 Apr 2021), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.103.134505 — resolves. The van der Marel collaboration is real: J. E. Hirsch and D. van der Marel, 'Room-temperature superconductivity — or not? Comment on Nature 586, 373 (2020) by E. Snider et al.', International Journal of Modern Physics B, DOI 10.1142/S0217979223750012 (arXiv:2201.07686) — cite it rather than alluding to it.

verdicts.claim: Zhang, Mesaros, Fujita, Edkins, Hamidian, Ch'ng, Eisaki, Uchida, Davis, Khatami, Kim, Nature 570, 484-490 (2019), arXiv:1808.00479 Aug 2018; an ensemble of artificial neural networks trained on candidate order types detects hidden electronic order in STM image arrays from cuprates, identifying a commensurate four-unit-cell periodic modulation.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: 'Machine learning in electronic-quantum-matter imaging experiments', Yi Zhang, A. Mesaros, K. Fujita, S. D. Edkins, M. H. Hamidian, K. Ch'ng, H. Eisaki, S. Uchida, J. C. Séamus Davis, Ehsan Khatami, Eun-Ah Kim, Nature 570(7762), 484-490 (June 2019), DOI 10.1038/s41586-019-1319-8 — resolves; author list and order exact. arXiv:1808.00479 (August 2018). The abstract states verbatim: 'development and training of an array of artificial neural networks (ANN) designed to recognize different types of hypothesized order hidden in EQM image-arrays... the ANNs discover the existence of a lattice-commensurate, four-unit-cell periodic, translational-symmetry-breaking EQM state.' The claim does not overstate.

verdicts.claim: Li, Hsu, Huang, New Journal of Physics 22, 123014 (2020); within Migdal-Eliashberg theory, supervised learning maps superconducting gap functions to electron-boson spectral functions, with an autoencoder compressing the spectral functions. Plus: 'a related and more recent line trains two-head convolutional networks on quasiparticle-interference images to classify pairing symmetry by irreducible representation and to regress continuous parameters such as singlet-triplet mixing and gap magnitude.'
verdicts.correction: The FIRST half is confirmed: Wan-Ju Li, Ming-Chien Hsu, Shin-Ming Huang, 'Machine learning on the electron-boson mechanism in superconductors', New Journal of Physics 22, 123014 (2020), arXiv:2007.07512 submitted 15 July 2020 — the arXiv URL in the dossier resolves to this exact work, and the abstract confirms the Migdal-Eliashberg framing, the gap-function-to-spectral-function mapping, and the use of autoencoders to handle 'function-to-function mappings with asymmetric complexities'. Add the journal DOI 10.1088/1367-2630/abcadb when citing. The affiliation (National Sun Yat-sen University) could not be verified — IOPscience blocks automated fetches with a bot challenge — so check the printed title page. The SECOND half is UNVERIFIABLE AS WRITTEN: the 'related and more recent line' on two-head convolutional networks over quasiparticle-interference images carries no citation at all in the dossier, so there is nothing to check. Do not print this sentence without a specific paper attached to it; an uncited specific technical claim of this shape is exactly where fabrication enters a manuscript.

verdicts.claim: Gao, Cerqueira, Sanna, Fang, Dangic, Errea, Wang, Botti, Marques, Nature Communications 16, 8253 (2025), arXiv:2502.18281 Feb 2025; electron-phonon calculations for more than 20,000 metals reveal a trade-off between omega_log and lambda, making room-temperature conventional superconductivity at ambient pressure extremely unlikely; Li2AgH6 and Li2AuH6 near the practical limit.

Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna, Yue-Wen Fang, Đorđe Dangić, Ion Errea, Hai-Chen Wang, Silvana Botti, Miguel A. L. Marques, Nature Communications 16, 8253 (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-63702-w — URL resolves, author list and order exact, arXiv:2502.18281 submitted 25 February 2025. Abstract verbatim: 'analysis of electron-phonon calculations for over 20,000 metals', 'an inherent trade-off between omega_log and the electron-phonon coupling constant lambda', 'we identify Li2AgH6 and its sibling Li2AuH6 as theoretical materials that likely approach the practical limit for conventional superconductivity at ambient pressure', and 'achieving room-temperature conventional superconductivity at ambient pressure is extremely unlikely'. Note the diacritics: Đorđe Dangić — reproduce them.

verdicts.claim: Summary-level: 'ML entered hydride work later as a surrogate to triage structure-search candidates (Shipley, Hutcheon, Needs and Pickard 2021; Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques 2024).'
verdicts.correction: Half of this attribution fails. Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques (2024) genuinely trained a machine-learning model on ~7,000 electron-phonon calculations and used it as a screening surrogate — that citation supports the sentence. Shipley, Hutcheon, Needs and Pickard (2021) did NOT: their candidate-ranking model takes 'inputs arising from density of states calculations and Gaspari-Gyorffy theory', a physics-based semi-empirical Tc model refined iteratively, and the paper does not present it as machine learning. Corrected sentence: 'ML entered hydride work later as a surrogate to triage structure-search candidates (Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques 2024); earlier high-throughput hydride searches such as Shipley, Hutcheon, Needs and Pickard (2021) used physics-based semi-empirical Tc models rather than machine learning for the same triage role.' This matters because the sentence is the book's stated dividing line between theory-first and data-driven discovery, and the Shipley citation currently sits on the wrong side of it.

rigorous-foundations.domain: Statistical physics of critical phenomena: scaling-relation history (Rushbrooke/Widom), conformal bootstrap determination of 3d Ising exponents, quantum criticality in itinerant electron systems (Hertz-Millis), and the droplet-vs-replica-symmetry-breaking dispute in spin glasses with its rigorous resolution (Guerra, Talagrand).
rigorous-foundations.summary: All five citation clusters resolve cleanly to primary sources, and the chronology the chapter asserts holds up. (1) George Stanley Rushbrooke's inequality is J. Chem. Phys. 39, 842-843 (1963), Vol. 39 Issue 3, DOI 10.1063/1.1734338 — two years before Benjamin Widom's scaling hypothesis in J. Chem. Phys. 43, 3898-3905 (1965), Vol. 43 Issue 11, DOI 10.1063/1.1696618. One nuance worth adding to the chapter: John W. Essam and Michael E. Fisher had already conjectured the EQUALITY alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2 from Pade-approximant series analysis earlier in 1963 (J. Chem. Phys. 38, 802, Vol. 38 Issue 4); Rushbrooke's contribution was the rigorous thermodynamic proof of the inequality, and Widom's homogeneity ansatz supplied the theoretical reason for equality. Robert B. Griffiths added the companion inequality alpha' + beta*(1+delta) >= 2 in PRL 14, 623 (1965). (2) The conformal bootstrap work is a three-paper arc, not one paper: the 2012 PRD paper found the kink; the 2014 J. Stat. Phys. paper (same six authors) achieved Delta_sigma = 0.518154(15), Delta_epsilon = 1.41267(13), giving nu = 0.62999(5), eta = 0.03631(3), omega = 0.8303(18) — which that paper states is "factor 2 - 3 more precise" than Martin Hasenbusch's 2010 Monte Carlo benchmark; the 2016 JHEP mixed-correlator paper by Filip Kos, David Poland, David Simmons-Duffin and Alessandro Vichi (note: Sheer El-Showk, Miguel F. Paulos and Slava Rychkov are NOT authors of that one) reached Delta_sigma = 0.5181489(10), Delta_epsilon = 1.412625(10). If the chapter cites "the conformal bootstrap determination" with the six-author list, the correct target is the 2014 J. Stat. Phys. paper. (3) Andrew J. Millis's paper is Phys. Rev. B 48, 7183-7196 (1993), extending John A. Hertz's 1976 framework to nonzero temperature; the canonical name in the literature is "Hertz-Millis-Moriya theory." (4) The Daniel S. Fisher and David A. Huse droplet picture spans PRL 56, 1601 (1986) and Phys. Rev. B 38, 386 (1988), with two 1987 J. Phys. A letters aimed directly at the many-pure-states claim of Giorgio Parisi's replica-symmetry-breaking solution. (5) Francesco Guerra's bound appeared as arXiv:cond-mat/0205123 in May 2002 and in Commun. Math. Phys. 233, 1-12 in February 2003; Michel Talagrand announced the proof in C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 337, 111-114 (2003) and published the full proof in Annals of Mathematics 163, 221-263 (2006). Dmitry Panchenko's 2013 Annals paper closed the remaining ultrametricity gap.

items.claim: The inequality alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' >= 2 was proved by rigorous thermodynamic argument in a two-page paper titled 'On the Thermodynamics of the Critical Region for the Ising Problem.' Bibliographic data verified via Crossref: Journal of Chemical Physics, Volume 39, Issue 3, pages 842-843, 1963. This is the primary source the chapter needs. It predates Widom's 1965 scaling hypothesis by two years.
items.people: George Stanley Rushbrooke (published as G. S. Rushbrooke)
items.affiliation: University of Newcastle upon Tyne (King's College, Newcastle, at the time; the paper's affiliation line was not retrievable — see open questions)

items.claim: Earlier in the same year (Volume 38, Issue 4, versus Rushbrooke in Volume 39, Issue 3), Essam and Fisher conjectured the scaling relation as an EQUALITY, alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2, on the basis of Pade-approximant analysis of low-temperature series. Crossref abstract confirms: 'They also propose the scaling relation alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2.' This matters for the chapter's framing: the equality was conjectured from numerics before Rushbrooke proved the inequality, and before Widom explained why the equality should hold.
items.people: John W. Essam and Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Not stated in retrieved metadata; both were at King's College London at the time (uncertain — not verified from the paper)
items.venue: The Journal of Chemical Physics 38(4), 802-812 — 'Pade Approximant Studies of the Lattice Gas and Ising Ferromagnet below the Critical Point'

items.claim: The scaling hypothesis: the singular part of the equation of state is a homogeneous function of temperature and field variables, which converts the previously derived thermodynamic INEQUALITIES (Rushbrooke's and Griffiths') into EQUALITIES. Crossref-verified: Journal of Chemical Physics, Volume 43, Issue 11, pages 3898-3905, published 1 December 1965. Widom's companion paper in the same issue, 'Surface Tension and Molecular Correlations near the Critical Point,' J. Chem. Phys. 43, 3892-3897 (1965), DOI 10.1063/1.1696617, is often cited alongside it.
items.people: Benjamin Widom (published as B. Widom)
items.affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York (affiliation confirmed on the companion paper 10.1063/1.1696617)
items.venue: The Journal of Chemical Physics 43(11), 3898-3905 — 'Equation of State in the Neighborhood of the Critical Point'

items.claim: The companion thermodynamic inequality alpha' + beta*(1+delta) >= 2, derived by thermodynamic argument in the same period. Published 19 April 1965 in Physical Review Letters 14, 623-624, titled 'Thermodynamic Inequality Near the Critical Point for Ferromagnets and Fluids.' A longer treatment appeared as 'Ferromagnets and Simple Fluids near the Critical Point: Some Thermodynamic Inequalities,' J. Chem. Phys. 43, 1958 (1965). Useful if the chapter wants the full pre-scaling inequality set rather than Rushbrooke alone.
items.people: Robert B. Griffiths
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records

items.claim: The block-spin argument that supplied a physical mechanism for Widom's homogeneity ansatz, one year after Widom. Crossref-verified: Physics Physique Fizika, Volume 2, Issue 6, pages 263-272, 1966, 'Scaling laws for Ising models near T_c.' Franz J. Wegner's memorial article (J. Stat. Phys., DOI 10.1007/s10955-016-1632-7, arXiv:1609.02719) states that Kadanoff 'explained Widom's homogeneity laws by means of block-spin transformations and laid the basis for Wilson's renormalization group equation.'

items.claim: The definitive contemporary review of the inequality-to-equality transition, written by a participant, two years after Widom. Crossref-verified: Reports on Progress in Physics, Volume 30, Issue 2, pages 615-730, 1967, 'The theory of equilibrium critical phenomena.' Recommended as the chapter's secondary anchor for the Rushbrooke/Widom chronology, since Michael E. Fisher was co-author of the competing 1963 equality conjecture and reviews both.

items.claim: THIS is the paper the chapter almost certainly wants for 'the conformal bootstrap determination of 3d Ising exponents' with the six-author list. Section 3 also gives Delta_epsilon=1.41267(13) and Delta_epsilon-prime=3.8303(18). The paper states these are 'factor 2 - 3 more precise' than the prior Monte Carlo determinations by Martin Hasenbusch. Preprint 18 March 2014 (revised 4 June 2014); journal J. Stat. items.claim: The paper Millis extends: the original construction of an effective bosonic (order-parameter) theory for quantum critical points in itinerant fermion systems, introducing the dynamical exponent z and the effective dimension d+z. Crossref-verified: Physical Review B, Volume 14, Issue 3, pages 1165-1184, 1976. Cite this alongside Millis 1993 — the pairing is what the literature calls Hertz-Millis theory.
items.people: John A. Hertz
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records

items.claim: The requested Millis 1993 paper on finite-temperature scaling near quantum critical points in itinerant electron systems. Bibliographic data Crossref-verified: Physical Review B, Volume 48, Issue 10, pages 7183-7196, published online 1 September 1993, 31 references, ~1630 Crossref citations. The paper reexamines Hertz's treatment, determines when it is legitimate to integrate out the fermions and describe criticality by an effective bosonic theory retaining only order-parameter fluctuations, and by solving the appropriate scaling equations obtains the distinct regimes of the correlation length and free energy in the disordered phase — with results differing from Hertz's in several cases and making contact with dilute-Bose-gas results. NOTE: the abstract text is behind the APS paywall; the content description here comes from APS abstract-page snippets, not from a verbatim read.
items.people: Andrew J. Millis (published as A. J. Millis)
items.affiliation: AT&T Bell Laboratories (uncertain — not verified from the paper itself)
items.venue: Physical Review B 48(10), 7183-7196 — 'Effect of a nonzero temperature on quantum critical points in itinerant fermion systems'

items.claim: The standard demonstration that Hertz-Millis-Moriya theory FAILS for itinerant ferromagnets: a universal negative, nonanalytic contribution to the static magnetic susceptibility, generated by long-range spatial correlations tied to Landau damping of the order-parameter field, destabilizes the quantum critical point — the transition instead goes first order or to incommensurate ordering. Crossref-verified: Physical Review Letters 92(14), 147003, published 9 April 2004. Worth citing if the chapter presents Millis 1993 as settled rather than as a framework with a known domain of validity.
items.people: Andrey V. Chubukov, Catherine Pépin, Jerome Rech
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records
items.venue: Physical Review Letters 92(14), 147003 — 'Instability of the Quantum-Critical Point of Itinerant Ferromagnets'

Abstract verbatim opening: 'This review discusses instabilities of the Fermi-liquid state of conduction electrons in metals with particular emphasis on magnetic quantum critical points.' Submitted 13 June 2006; published Rev. Mod. Phys. 79, 1015 (2007). Note the preprint/journal year gap and the diacritics: Löhneysen, Wölfle.

items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records

items.claim: The two papers being opposed: the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick infinite-range spin-glass model (Physical Review Letters 35(26), 1792-1796, published 29 December 1975, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1792, authors David Sherrington and Scott Kirkpatrick) and Parisi's replica-symmetry-breaking solution of it. Parisi's ansatz appears in 'Infinite Number of Order Parameters for Spin-Glasses,' PRL 43(23), 1754-1756, published 3 December 1979, and its physical interpretation as an overlap distribution in 'Order Parameter for Spin-Glasses,' PRL 50(24), 1946-1948, published 13 June 1983. Both Crossref-verified. The RSB picture predicts infinitely many pure states, a nontrivial overlap distribution, ultrametricity, and an de Almeida-Thouless line in a field — every one of which the droplet picture denies.
items.people: Giorgio Parisi (published as G. Parisi in 1979, Giorgio Parisi in 1983); David Sherrington and Scott Kirkpatrick for the underlying model
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records
items.venue: Physical Review Letters 35, 1792 (1975); Physical Review Letters 43, 1754-1756 (1979); Physical Review Letters 50, 1946-1948 (1983)

items.claim: The direct precursor to the droplet picture: a real-space scaling theory of Ising spin glasses in which the ordered phase is characterized by a stiffness exponent governing the free-energy cost of large-scale domain-wall excitations. Crossref-verified: Journal of Physics C: Solid State Physics, Volume 17, Issue 18, pages 3179-3187, published 30 June 1984. Cite if the chapter wants to note that Fisher and Huse were building on an existing droplet/scaling line rather than inventing it whole.
items.people: William L. McMillan (published as W. L. McMillan)
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records
items.venue: Journal of Physics C: Solid State Physics 17(18), 3179-3187 — 'Scaling theory of Ising spin glasses'

items.claim: The primary statement of the droplet picture. The short version: Physical Review Letters 56(15), 1601-1604, published 14 April 1986, 'Ordered Phase of Short-Range Ising Spin-Glasses' — a picture of the spin-glass phase built on a scaling ansatz for low-lying large-scale droplet excitations, giving behavior very different from the infinite-range model, with the consequence that a magnetic field destroys the spin-glass phase so that there is NO de Almeida-Thouless transition. The long version: Physical Review B 38(1), 386-411 (1988), 'Equilibrium behavior of the spin-glass ordered phase.' Both Crossref-verified with author order Daniel S. Fisher then David A. Huse. This is the direct opposition to Parisi: two pure states related by global spin flip, trivial overlap distribution, no ultrametricity, no AT line — versus RSB's infinitely many states.
items.people: Daniel S. Fisher and David A. Huse
items.affiliation: Not verified from retrieved records
items.venue: Physical Review Letters 56(15), 1601-1604 (1986); Physical Review B 38(1), 386-411 (1988)

items.claim: The rigorous mathematical attack on RSB-in-finite-dimensions, and the third party in the dispute. Crossref-verified: Physical Review Letters 76(3), 515-518, published 15 January 1996. The paper offers proofs that the main features of the Parisi solution of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, as applied to more realistic short-range models, do not hold in any dimension at any temperature. Newman and Stein subsequently developed the 'metastate' formalism. Cite this to show the debate was three-cornered, not just droplet-versus-RSB.
items.people: Charles M. Newman and Daniel L. Stein (published as C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein)

Submitted to arXiv 5 June 1999 (cond-mat/9906076); published Journal of Statistical Physics 98(5/6), 973-1074 (2000). Note the preprint/journal year gap. This is the natural counterweight citation to Fisher-Huse.

Math. Phys. 230(1), 71-79 (September 2002). Crossref confirms authors Francesco Guerra and Fabio Lucio Toninelli. Without this, 'the' free energy has no meaning to bound.

items.claim: The requested Guerra bound. VERBATIM from the abstract: 'Our main result is that the quenched average of the free energy is bounded from below by the value given in the Parisi Ansatz uniformly in the size of the system. Moreover, the difference between the two expressions is given in the form of a sum rule.' CAUTION FOR THE CHAPTER: 'bounded from below' is stated in Guerra's own convention (the quantity interpolated is (1/N)E log Z, i.e. -beta*f); rendered in physical free energy the Parisi expression is an upper bound. Quote Guerra's wording or state the convention explicitly — this is a common source of sign errors in secondary accounts. arXiv:cond-mat/0205123 submitted 7 May 2002; Commun. Math. Phys. 233(1), 1-12, published 1 February 2003. The chapter's '2003' is the journal year; the preprint is 2002.

items.claim: The requested Talagrand proof, which supplied the matching bound and made Parisi's ansatz a theorem. Crossref-verified: Annals of Mathematics, Volume 163, Issue 1, pages 221-263, 2006, 'The Parisi formula.' The result: using Guerra's interpolation scheme, the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model is computed at any temperature, confirming Parisi's prediction; the proof is self-contained and requires no physics background. IMPORTANT CHRONOLOGY: Talagrand announced the result three years earlier in a four-page note, 'The generalized Parisi formula,' Comptes Rendus Mathematique 337(2), 111-114 (2003), DOI 10.1016/S1631-073X(03)00268-1, whose abstract reads verbatim: 'For a large class of Gaussian Hamiltonians, we use Guerra's interpolation scheme to show that at any temperature the free energy of the corresponding spin-glass system is asymptotically given by Parisi's formula. This class includes the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, the p-spin interaction model for even p, and many others.' If the chapter wants to convey how fast Guerra's bound was converted into a theorem, the 2002-2003 gap is the striking number, not 2003-2006.

items.claim: The result that closed the remaining gap: the support of a random measure on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space satisfying the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities is ultrametric with probability one, which implies the Parisi ultrametricity conjecture for mean-field spin-glass models including Sherrington-Kirkpatrick and mixed p-spin. Crossref-verified: Annals of Mathematics, Volume 177, Issue 1, pages 383-393, 2013. Worth a sentence in the chapter: Talagrand proved the free-energy FORMULA, but the ultrametric organization of pure states — arguably the most physically striking part of Parisi's ansatz — was not a theorem until Panchenko.

openQuestions: Rushbrooke's paper is paywalled at AIP (HTTP 403 on both pubs.aip.org URLs) and its abstract and reference list are elided by the publisher on Semantic Scholar. Two things could not be verified from the primary text: (a) whether Rushbrooke uses PRIMED exponents (alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' >= 2, T approaching Tc from below) as the secondary literature uniformly reports; (b) whether Rushbrooke explicitly cites Essam and Fisher 1963. Do not assert either in the chapter without library access to J. Chem. Phys. 39, 842.

The Wikipedia article on the Rushbrooke inequality glosses the primed exponents as describing behavior ABOVE the critical temperature. This contradicts the standard convention in which primed exponents denote the T -> Tc-minus approach. Treat the Wikipedia gloss as an error; verify against a textbook (e.g. Fisher's 1967 Reports on Progress in Physics review, DOI 10.1088/0034-4885/30/2/306) before writing the sentence.

Rushbrooke's paper is Volume 39, Issue 3; the exact publication date within 1963 was not retrieved. Essam and Fisher's equality conjecture is in Volume 38, Issue 4 — an earlier volume, hence earlier in 1963 — but if the chapter wants to claim a specific number of months between them, confirm the issue dates.

Andrew J. Millis's institutional affiliation on the 1993 paper (AT&T Bell Laboratories is the likely answer) was not confirmed: the APS page returns 403 and neither PubMed nor Semantic Scholar exposes the affiliation. Verify before printing it.

The 1993 Millis abstract could not be read verbatim (APS paywall). The content summary in this report derives from search-engine snippets of the APS abstract page. If the chapter quotes Millis, obtain the paper.

AUTHOR-LIST HAZARD: the six-name list the chapter uses (El-Showk, Paulos, Poland, Rychkov, Simmons-Duffin, Vichi) is correct ONLY for the 2012 PRD paper and the 2014 J. Stat. Phys. paper. The 2014 JHEP mixed-correlator paper has three authors (Kos, Poland, Simmons-Duffin) and the 2016 record-precision JHEP paper has four (Kos, Poland, Simmons-Duffin, Vichi). Decide which precision figure the chapter is quoting and match the author list to it.

GUERRA SIGN-CONVENTION HAZARD: Guerra's abstract says the quenched average of the free energy is bounded from BELOW by the Parisi value, in a convention where the interpolated quantity is (1/N)E log Z. Much of the secondary literature says Parisi's expression is an UPPER bound on the free energy. Both are correct under their own conventions. Quote Guerra directly or state the convention; do not paraphrase loosely.

The chapter should decide whether 'the droplet picture' cites the 1986 PRL, the 1988 PRB, or both. The 1986 PRL is the announcement; the 1988 PRB is the full development. The two 1987 J. Phys. A letters are the ones that argue explicitly against Parisi's many-states structure, and they have REVERSED author order between them — check which is which before citing.

Whether the droplet-versus-RSB dispute should be presented as unresolved. Newman and Stein 1996 argues rigorously against RSB in finite dimensions; Marinari and coauthors 2000 argues numerically for it. Neither side conceded. Numerical work in the intervening 25 years has not been surveyed here — if the chapter makes a claim about the current consensus, a fresh literature check on finite-dimensional Edwards-Anderson simulations is needed.

Whether the chapter treats Hertz-Millis theory as valid or as a framework with known limits. Chubukov, Pepin and Rech 2004 shows it fails for itinerant FERROMAGNETS; the antiferromagnetic case is less clearly broken. If the chapter states Millis 1993 as settled physics, that overstates the current position.

verdicts.claim: Rushbrooke's affiliation: 'University of Newcastle upon Tyne (King's College, Newcastle, at the time; the paper's affiliation line was not retrievable).'
verdicts.correction: The affiliation line IS retrievable and it is not Newcastle. The Crossref deposit for 10.1063/1.1734338 (publisher-supplied, i.e. the paper's own affiliation line) reads: 'Chemistry Department, University of Oregon, Eugene, Oregon'. The AIP article page for J. Chem. Phys. 39(3), 842 lists the same. Rushbrooke held his chair at King's College, Newcastle upon Tyne, but this particular paper was written from Oregon. Correct text if the chapter prints an affiliation: 'G. S. Rushbrooke, Chemistry Department, University of Oregon, Eugene, Oregon.' URL: https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1734338 (article page: https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article/39/3/842/80275/)

verdicts.claim: OPEN QUESTION (a): whether Rushbrooke uses PRIMED exponents (alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' >= 2, T -> Tc from below), and OPEN QUESTION from the Wikipedia note that primes might denote T above Tc.
verdicts.correction: Resolved from a 1963 primary source. The publisher-deposited abstract of Essam & Fisher (10.1063/1.1733766), the paper Rushbrooke cites, states verbatim: 'Consideration of a heuristic model partition function suggests the identity alpha'+2beta+gamma'=2 where alpha' is the index of divergence of the specific heat BELOW Tc.' Primed exponents therefore denote the T -> Tc-minus approach in exactly this 1963 literature. The Wikipedia gloss the dossier flags is indeed wrong, and the chapter may write alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' >= 2 with primes meaning 'below Tc' on this evidence. (Rushbrooke's own two pages remain paywalled; this is a primary-source confirmation of the convention, not of Rushbrooke's typography.)

verdicts.claim: OPEN QUESTION (b): whether Rushbrooke explicitly cites Essam and Fisher 1963.
verdicts.correction: Resolved: he does, and it is his FIRST reference. The Crossref reference list deposited for 10.1063/1.1734338 contains six references, of which reference 1 is J. Chem. Phys. 38, 802 (1963), DOI 10.1063/1.1733766 — Essam & Fisher. The chapter may safely assert that Rushbrooke's paper cites the Essam-Fisher conjecture.

verdicts.claim: Essam and Fisher conjectured the equality alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2 'on the basis of Pade-approximant analysis of low-temperature series.' Crossref abstract confirms: 'They also propose the scaling relation alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2.'
verdicts.correction: Bibliography is right; the method attribution and the purported quote are both wrong. (i) The quoted sentence does not appear in the Crossref/AIP abstract. The actual abstract text is: 'Consideration of a heuristic model partition function suggests the identity alpha'+2beta+gamma'=2 where alpha' is the index of divergence of the specific heat below Tc.' Quote that, not the dossier's paraphrase. (ii) The Pade-approximant analysis is what produced their values of beta (0.303 <= beta <= 0.318, conjectured beta = 5/16) and gamma'; the scaling IDENTITY itself is credited in the abstract to 'consideration of a heuristic model partition function.' Accurate sentence: 'Essam and Fisher obtained beta and gamma' from Pade-approximant analysis of low-temperature series, and inferred the identity alpha' + 2*beta + gamma' = 2 from consideration of a heuristic model partition function.' Bibliographic data confirmed: John W. Essam and Michael E. Fisher, 'Pade Approximant Studies of the Lattice Gas and Ising Ferromagnet below the Critical Point,' J. Chem. Phys. 38(4), 802-812, published 15 February 1963, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1733766

verdicts.claim: Essam and Fisher affiliation: 'Not stated in retrieved metadata; both were at King's College London at the time (uncertain — not verified from the paper).'
verdicts.correction: Now verified and printable. The Crossref deposit for 10.1063/1.1733766 carries the paper's affiliation line for both authors: 'Wheatstone Physics Laboratory, King's College, London, W.C.2, England.' Drop the hedge.

verdicts.claim: Chronology: Essam-Fisher (Vol. 38, Issue 4) came earlier in 1963 than Rushbrooke (Vol. 39, Issue 3); exact issue dates not retrieved, so do not claim a specific number of months.
verdicts.correction: Issue dates now retrieved from Crossref: Essam & Fisher published 15 February 1963; Rushbrooke published 1 August 1963. The gap is five and a half months, within the same year. The chapter may state this precisely.

verdicts.claim: Widom's hypothesis is that 'the singular part of the equation of state is a homogeneous function of temperature and field variables.'
verdicts.correction: Imprecise as applied to Widom's own 1965 paper, which is written for a fluid. Widom's abstract states: 'A function Phi(x, y) is introduced, with x a measure of the temperature and y of the DENSITY... It is suggested that in a real fluid Phi(x, y) is a homogeneous function of x and y, with a positive degree of homogeneity.' The homogeneity is in temperature and the ORDER PARAMETER (density), not temperature and field. Accurate sentence: 'Widom proposed that the function governing the equation of state near the critical point is a homogeneous function of the temperature and density variables.'

verdicts.claim: Widom's scaling hypothesis 'converts the previously derived thermodynamic INEQUALITIES (Rushbrooke's and Griffiths') into EQUALITIES.'
verdicts.correction: Substantively supported and now documented from the paper itself: Widom's 15-item reference list (Crossref deposit for 10.1063/1.1696618) cites J. Chem. Phys. 39, 842 (1963) = Rushbrooke, J. Chem. Phys. 38, 802 (1963) = Essam & Fisher, AND Phys. Rev. Lett. 14, 623 (1965) = Griffiths. Widom was demonstrably working against all three. Note for the chapter: the 'converts inequalities into equalities' formulation is the standard retrospective reading (see Fisher's 1967 review); Widom's own abstract frames the results in fluid-specific terms.

verdicts.claim: Guerra and Toninelli, 'The Thermodynamic Limit in Mean Field Spin Glass Models,' arXiv cond-mat/0204280 submitted 12 April 2002; Commun. Math. Phys. 230(1), 71-79 (September 2002); affiliations Rome La Sapienza + INFN Rome, and SNS Pisa + INFN Pisa.
verdicts.correction: Verified. Crossref 10.1007/s00220-002-0699-y gives Francesco Guerra and Fabio Lucio Toninelli, Communications in Mathematical Physics, Volume 230, Issue 1, pages 71-79, September 2002 (the Crossref record carries no title field; the title is confirmed from the arXiv record). arXiv:cond-mat/0204280, submitted 12 April 2002, lists exactly the stated affiliations. Content description (existence and uniqueness of the infinite-volume limit for SK and Derrida p-spin via an interpolation argument and subadditivity in system size) matches the abstract.

verdicts.claim: Guerra, 'Broken Replica Symmetry Bounds in the Mean Field Spin Glass Model,' arXiv cond-mat/0205123 submitted 7 May 2002; Commun. Math. Phys. 233(1), 1-12, published 1 February 2003; abstract verbatim: 'Our main result is that the quenched average of the free energy is bounded from below by the value given in the Parisi Ansatz... the difference between the two expressions is given in the form of a sum rule.'
verdicts.correction: Fully verified. Crossref 10.1007/s00220-002-0773-5: Francesco Guerra, Communications in Mathematical Physics, Volume 233, Issue 1, pages 1-12, 1 February 2003. arXiv:cond-mat/0205123 submitted 7 May 2002, affiliation 'University of Rome La Sapienza and INFN, Rome' (the PDF's own byline reads 'Dipartimento di Fisica, Universita di Roma La Sapienza, and INFN, Sezione di Roma1'). The quoted abstract sentences are verbatim correct, word for word.

verdicts.claim: GUERRA SIGN-CONVENTION HAZARD, as stated by the dossier: "'bounded from below' is stated in Guerra's own convention (the quantity interpolated is (1/N)E log Z, i.e. -beta*f); rendered in physical free energy the Parisi expression is an upper bound."
verdicts.correction: The two conventions are swapped. Read from Guerra's own text (arXiv:cond-mat/0205123). His Eq. (3) defines: '-beta*f_N(beta,h) = N^(-1) E log Z_N(beta,h,J) = alpha_N(beta,h)'. His Theorem 3 states: 'N^(-1) E log Z_N(beta,h,J) <= alpha-bar(beta,h;x), uniformly in N... Consequently, we have also N^(-1) E log Z_N(beta,h,J) <= alpha-bar(beta,h)', and the text says 'alpha-bar(beta,h) is at least a rigorous UPPER bound for N^(-1) E log Z_N(beta,h,J), uniformly in N.' So: the interpolated quantity (1/N)E log Z = -beta*f is bounded from ABOVE by the Parisi expression; the PHYSICAL free energy f is what is bounded from BELOW, which is exactly what Guerra's abstract says ('the broken replica Ansatz turns out to be a rigorous lower bound for the quenched average of the free energy per site'). Correct text for the chapter: 'Guerra proved that the Parisi expression is a rigorous upper bound, uniform in system size, on (1/N)E log Z_N; equivalently, since Guerra defines -beta*f_N = (1/N)E log Z_N, the Parisi value is a rigorous lower bound on the quenched free energy per site f_N. The mathematics literature that says Guerra proved the Parisi formula is an upper bound on the free energy is using (1/N)E log Z_N as its definition of free energy; Guerra, writing f with the physical minus sign, says lower bound. Both statements are the same theorem.'

verdicts.claim: Talagrand, 'The Parisi formula,' Annals of Mathematics 163(1), 221-263 (2006), DOI 10.4007/annals.2006.163.221; announced three years earlier in 'The generalized Parisi formula,' Comptes Rendus Mathematique 337(2), 111-114 (2003), DOI 10.1016/S1631-073X(03)00268-1, with the quoted abstract.
verdicts.correction: Both Crossref-verified. Annals of Mathematics, Volume 163, Issue 1, pages 221-263, 2006. Comptes Rendus Mathematique, Volume 337, Issue 2, pages 111-114, published 28 June 2003, and its abstract is verbatim as quoted: 'For a large class of Gaussian Hamiltonians, we use Guerra's interpolation scheme to show that at any temperature the free energy of the corresponding spin-glass system is asymptotically given by Parisi's formula. This class includes the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, the p-spin interaction model for even p, and many others.' (The journal prints an en dash in 'Sherrington-Kirkpatrick'.) The dossier's chronology point stands: Guerra's May 2002 preprint to Talagrand's June 2003 announcement is roughly thirteen months.

verdicts.claim: Panchenko, 'The Parisi ultrametricity conjecture,' Annals of Mathematics 177(1), 383-393 (2013): the support of a random measure on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space satisfying the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities is ultrametric with probability one, implying the Parisi ultrametricity conjecture for mean-field models.
verdicts.correction: Crossref-verified: Dmitry Panchenko, Annals of Mathematics, Volume 177, Issue 1, pages 383-393, 2013, https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2013.177.1.8. Preprint arXiv:1112.1003 (v1 5 Dec 2011). The abstract confirms the statement: the support of a random measure on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space that satisfies the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities must be ultrametric with probability one. Note one nuance for the chapter: the abstract states this 'proves the Parisi ultrametricity conjecture in spin glass models for which the Gibbs measure satisfies these identities' — a conditional formulation, so the chapter should say 'for mean-field models whose Gibbs measures satisfy the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities' rather than asserting it unconditionally for all mean-field models.

verdicts.claim: Overall: 'All five citation clusters resolve cleanly to primary sources, and the chronology the chapter asserts holds up.'
verdicts.correction: No citation in this dossier is hallucinated or garbled — all 27 works exist, every DOI and arXiv identifier resolves to the exact work named, every author list and ordering (including the two deliberate author-order traps) is correct, and all quoted abstract passages except one are verbatim. But three claims would print falsehoods: (1) Rushbrooke's affiliation on the 1963 paper is University of Oregon, not Newcastle; (2) the Guerra sign-convention gloss is inverted; (3) Essam and Fisher's scaling identity came from a heuristic model partition function, not from the Pade analysis. Two further items need wording fixes: the Widom homogeneity is in temperature and density, not temperature and field; and the 1406.4858 'quotation' is a paraphrase. Four of the dossier's own open questions are now resolved from primary records: primed exponents mean below Tc (Essam-Fisher abstract); Rushbrooke does cite Essam and Fisher (his first reference); the two 1963 papers are dated 15 Feb and 1 Aug; and Essam and Fisher were at the Wheatstone Physics Laboratory, King's College, London. Millis's affiliation remains genuinely unverifiable without the printed page.

rg-symbolic-verify.domain: Physics-of-learning literature: the RG/deep-learning mapping dispute, symbolic discovery of physical law from data, grokking as a phase-transition-like phenomenon, and jamming transitions in deep networks
rg-symbolic-verify.summary: All eight requested targets were checked against primary sources (arXiv API metadata, arXiv abstract pages, publisher pages, ar5iv full text, and the published Lemos PDF). Seven of the eight resolve cleanly. Item (7) does not: I found no paper by Marylou Gabrié that engages the Mehta-Schwab dispute. Gabrié's review "Mean-field inference methods for neural networks" (J. Phys. A, 2020) was checked in full text and contains no discussion of the renormalization group or of Mehta and Schwab. The dispute's actual participants are Henry W. Lin and Max Tegmark (with David Rolnick) on the attacking side, David J. Schwab and Pankaj Mehta in rebuttal, and then three independent empirical critiques: Maciej Koch-Janusz and Zohar Ringel (Nature Physics 2018), Satoshi Iso, Shotaro Shiba and Sumito Yokoo (Phys. Rev. E 2018), and the de Mello Koch group (IEEE Access 2020, Phys. Rev. E 2020). Two facts worth flagging for the book: the Schwab-Mehta rebuttal was posted to arXiv only and never journal-published, so calling it a "published rebuttal" would be wrong; and the arXiv metadata for "Short sighted deep learning" misspells the lead author as "Ellen de Melllo Koch" (three l's), a typo that will propagate into any auto-generated BibTeX. Also note that Robert de Mello Koch is an author on the IEEE Access paper but NOT on the Phys. Rev. E follow-up. On grokking, the Nanda et al. three phases are, verbatim from the abstract, "memorization, circuit formation, and cleanup" — not the "memorization / grokking / generalization" ordering that secondary sources sometimes give.

items.claim: Original claim of an exact mapping from Kadanoff's variational renormalization group onto stacked Restricted Boltzmann Machines, illustrated on the nearest-neighbour Ising model in one and two dimensions. Concludes only that deep learning "may be employing a generalized RG-like scheme" — the paper's own hedge is weaker than the title.

Argues their claims "are incorrect and stem from a misunderstanding of the variational RG procedure proposed by Kadanoff," and that their counterexample is in fact compatible with the 1410.3831 mapping. Note the author order is reversed relative to the 2014 paper: Schwab first, Mehta second. IMPORTANT: this is an arXiv-only comment, 3 KB, single version, with no journal reference or DOI — it is not a published rebuttal.

items.affiliation: Not verified from the sources consulted (arXiv metadata only)

items.claim: The strongest empirical critique. Introduces an RSMI-based neural algorithm that identifies RG-relevant degrees of freedom, and states in the main text that on the dimer model the filters obtained by the RSMI method "are orthogonal to those obtained using Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence," concluding that "standard RBMs minimizing the KL-divergence do not generally perform RG, thereby contradicting prior claims" — with Mehta and Schwab 2014 cited at that point. The supplementary section "Comparison with Contrastive divergence trained RBMs" shows a CD-trained network coupling strongly to spin pairs that are physically irrelevant.
items.people: Maciej Koch-Janusz; Zohar Ringel
items.affiliation: Not verified from the sources consulted (arXiv metadata and ar5iv full text only)

items.claim: Independent empirical critique on flow direction. An unsupervised RBM trained on Ising spin configurations at various temperatures generates a flow along which the temperature approaches the critical value — i.e. toward the critical point — whereas conventional RG flow for the Ising model moves away from it. A coarse-graining RBM should flow away from criticality, not toward it.

items.affiliation: Not verified from the sources consulted (arXiv metadata only)

items.claim: This is the Robert de Mello Koch paper the brief asks for. Proposes that correlation functions between hidden and visible neurons are "capable of diagnosing RG-like coarse graining" — i.e. an observable that can distinguish RG flow from what a trained RBM actually does. Compares single RBM layers to single RG steps on the Ising model, finds RG-like patterns in the trained correlators but also reports important differences between the two.

Two negative results: "the RBM flow for the long ranged model does not converge to the correct values for the spin and energy scaling dimension," and stacked RBM flows move toward low temperatures while RG flows move toward high temperatures. CAUTION FOR CITATION: Robert de Mello Koch is NOT an author here. Also, the arXiv metadata misspells the first author as "Ellen de Melllo Koch" with three l's; the correct surname is de Mello Koch.

items.claim: A graph network is trained to simulate the dynamics of the Solar System's Sun, planets and large moons from 30 years of observed trajectory data; symbolic regression is then applied to the learned edge function, and the best-fitting force expression is Newton's law of universal gravitation. The masses of the bodies were not observed and were re-fit using the discovered equation, giving "a nearly perfect fit to the true masses." The only assumptions are translational and rotational equivariance plus Newton's second and third laws. Dataset covers 31 objects.

items.claim: The grokking paper. Networks trained on small algorithmically generated datasets can improve "from random chance level to perfect generalization," and this improvement "can happen well past the point of overfitting." Smaller datasets require increasing amounts of optimization before generalization occurs. The paper describes the phenomenon but offers no mechanism. All five authors were at OpenAI; correspondence address in the arXiv comments field is alethea@openai.com.

items.claim: Reverse-engineers the algorithm learned by small transformers on modular addition (a + b mod 113): the network "uses discrete Fourier transforms and trigonometric identities to convert addition to rotation about a circle," confirmed by activation and weight analysis plus ablations in Fourier space. THE THREE PHASES, verbatim from the abstract, are "memorization, circuit formation, and cleanup." The concluding claim is that grokking "rather than being a sudden shift, arises from the gradual amplification of structured mechanisms encoded in the weights, followed by the later removal of memorizing components."

items.claim: The core jamming paper. Predicts and empirically tests an analogy between the deep-network loss landscape and the energy landscape of repulsive ellipses: a phase transition delimits the over- and under-parametrized regimes where fitting can or cannot be achieved, sharing direct similarities with the jamming transition by which particles form a disordered solid as density increases. Reports that the ability of fully connected networks to fit random data is independent of depth, and that at the critical point the per-datum quantity Delta is power-law distributed with exponents theta approximately 0.3 and gamma approximately 0.2, suggesting a hierarchical landscape and avalanche-like learning dynamics.

Two unchecked candidates remain: her 2019 PhD thesis (Ecole Normale Superieure, on mean-field methods for neural networks) and her chapter with Surya Ganguli, Carlo Lucibello and Riccardo Zecchina in the volume 'Spin Glass Theory and Far Beyond'. Whether the published Phys. Rev. E version of 'Short sighted deep learning' spells the lead author 'Ellen de Mello Koch' correctly. Individual affiliation-to-author mapping for the Lemos et al. paper. Eight numbered affiliations are printed but the superscript assignment for Jeffrey, Cranmer and Ho was not fully legible in the page scan — in particular whether Miles Cranmer is attached to Princeton, to the Flatiron Institute, or to both. Whether the MATH-AI (ICLR 2021) workshop version of the grokking paper differs materially from arXiv:2201.02177 — for instance whether the word 'grokking' and the headline modular-arithmetic results are already present in the 2021 version. This matters for dating the term's first appearance.

Whether Mehta and Schwab ever responded in print to the Koch-Janusz and Ringel dimer-model result, which is a sharper and later objection than the Lin-Tegmark counterexample the 2016 comment answers. No such response surfaced in this pass.

verdicts.claim: Mehta & Schwab, 'An exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning', arXiv:1410.3831 (v1 14 Oct 2014, never journal-published); exact mapping from Kadanoff variational RG onto stacked RBMs, illustrated on nearest-neighbour Ising in 1D and 2D; hedges to 'may be employing a generalized RG-like scheme'. Affiliations Boston University / Northwestern.
verdicts.correction: Fully verified. arXiv API: title, authors Pankaj Mehta, David J. Schwab (that order), published 2014-10-14, no journal_ref, no DOI, primary category stat.ML, comments '8 pages, 3 figures'. Abstract verbatim contains 'an exact mapping from the variational renormalization group, first introduced by Kadanoff, and deep learning architectures based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs)', 'the nearest-neighbor Ising Model in one and two dimensions', and 'may be employing a generalized RG-like scheme to learn relevant features from data'. Title-page affiliations read off ar5iv full text are verbatim 'Dept. of Physics, Boston University, Boston, MA' and 'Dept. of Physics, Northwestern University, Evanston, IL' — note the printed form is 'Dept. of Physics', not 'Department of Physics'.

verdicts.claim: Lin, Tegmark & Rolnick, 'Why does deep and cheap learning work so well?' — 'in its appendix presents a counterexample intended to show the Mehta-Schwab RG-to-deep-belief-network mapping is invalid'; preprint 29 Aug 2016 (arXiv v1) by Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick; final version 3 Aug 2017; published J. Stat. Phys. 2017, DOI 10.1007/s10955-017-1836-5.
verdicts.correction:
TWO ERRORS — this is the item the book must not print as written.

(1) The counterexample is NOT in the appendix of the version being cited. I downloaded and text-extracted arXiv v4 (the final version, internally dated 21 July 2017, identical in content to the Journal of Statistical Physics paper): it contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'counterexample', and its only appendix is 'Appendix A: The polynomial no-flattening theorem'. The RG critique that survives into the published paper is main-text Section III.5 'Distillation and renormalization', which says only: 'Although the connection between RG and machine learning has been studied or alluded to repeatedly [...Mehta and Schwab 2014...], there are significant misconceptions in the literature concerning the connection which we will now attempt to clear up.' The explicit counterexample was REMOVED before publication. It existed only in the 2016 preprint versions: in v1 (internally dated 31 August 2016) it is appendix section V.A, titled 'Why matching partition functions do not imply matching probability distributions', introduced in the main text as 'Appendix A, where we construct a counter-example to a recent claim [32] that a so-called "exact" RG is equiv[alent]...'; in the 29 September 2016 version it had been renumbered to 'Appendix B: Why renormalization is not unsupervised learning'.

(2) The 2016 preprint has only TWO authors. Both the v1 PDF (31 Aug 2016) and the 29 Sept 2016 PDF carry the byline 'Henry W. Lin and Max Tegmark' (Harvard Physics; MIT Physics & MIT Kavli Institute). David Rolnick appears only from the 2017 revision onward, with 'Dept. of Mathematics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology'.
