glass-jamming.domain: Physical glass and jamming transitions, and machine learning applied to them
glass-jamming.summary: Two threads. (1) The physics: Liu and Nagel's 1998 Nature note proposed a unified jamming phase diagram in temperature / load / inverse-density; O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel located "point J" at T=0 and zero stress and showed power-law criticality there. In parallel, Kauzmann's entropy crisis, the Adam-Gibbs cooperatively-rearranging-region argument, Götze's mode-coupling theory, and the random first-order transition (RFOT) theory of Kirkpatrick, Thirumalai and Wolynes built a thermodynamic picture of an ideal glass transition whose existence in finite dimensions is still unsettled. The mean-field solution of hard spheres in infinite dimension (Charbonneau, Kurchan, Parisi, Urbani, Zamponi) revealed a Gardner transition — named for Elizabeth Gardner, who found the same instability in p-spin glasses in 1985 and who also invented the "Gardner volume" calculation of neural-network storage capacity — connecting glass marginality to jamming criticality. (2) The ML: Cubuk, Schoenholz, Liu and colleagues trained support vector machines on local structural descriptors to define "softness," a scalar that predicts rearrangements; DeepMind (Bapst, Keck, Grabska-Barwińska, Cubuk, Schoenholz, Battaglia, Kohli and colleagues) showed graph neural networks predict long-time glassy dynamics from a single static snapshot far better than prior indicators. That result has since been substantially qualified: Boattini, Smallenburg and Filion matched GNN accuracy with a ~1000-parameter linear model built from neighbour-averaged descriptors, Jung, Biroli and Berthier's physics-inspired GlassMLP beat the GNN with far less data, and Swain, Ridout and Nemenman showed high predictive accuracy does not imply the model recovered the correct physical (energy-barrier) description. IMPORTANT CORRECTION FOR THE BOOK: the task brief treats "Liu and Nagel's jamming phase diagram (Nature 1998)" and "the later 'Jamming is not just cool any more' framing" as two separate things. They are the same one-page article — Nature 396, 21-22 (1998) — and that is where the phase diagram first appeared. The later retrospective framing is Liu and Nagel, Nature Reviews Physics 5, 630-631 (2023).

items.claim: Kauzmann observed that extrapolating the excess entropy of a supercooled liquid below its glass transition would make it fall below the crystal's entropy at a finite temperature — the 'Kauzmann paradox' / entropy crisis that motivates the idea of an underlying ideal glass transition.
items.people: Walter Kauzmann
items.affiliation: Princeton University (affiliation not verified against the primary article in this search)

items.claim: The Adam-Gibbs relation ties relaxation time to configurational entropy via a 'cooperatively rearranging region' whose size grows as configurational entropy shrinks, yielding a form close to the empirical WLF/VFT law and predicting divergence where configurational entropy vanishes.
items.people: Gerald Adam; Julian H. Gibbs
items.affiliation: affiliation not verified in this search

items.claim: Mode-coupling theory: closed nonlinear self-consistent equations for density correlations in a simple liquid produce an ergodic-to-nonergodic (glass) bifurcation; for hard spheres the transition appears at packing fraction 0.516. MCT's sharp transition is not observed experimentally and is now read as a crossover.
items.people: Ulf Bengtzelius; Wolfgang Götze; Arne Sjölander
items.affiliation: Technische Universität München (Götze); Chalmers University of Technology, Göteborg (Bengtzelius, Sjölander) — affiliations not verified against the primary article in this search
items.venue: Journal of Physics C: Solid State Physics 17, 5915-5934

items.claim: Gardner analysed Ising spin glasses with p-spin interactions in mean field and found TWO transitions: a discontinuous one at T1 with a jump in the order parameter but no latent heat, and a lower T2 where that one-step replica-symmetry-broken phase becomes unstable to full RSB — the instability now called the Gardner transition.
items.people: Elizabeth Gardner
items.affiliation: Department of Physics, University of Edinburgh

items.claim: Gardner computed the typical volume of the space of couplings that store p random patterns in an N-spin network — the 'Gardner volume' — establishing the statistical-mechanics theory of neural-network storage capacity. This is the direct historical bridge between the physics of disordered systems and learning theory, and the same author's name attaches to both the neural-capacity calculation and the glass transition.
items.people: Elizabeth Gardner
items.affiliation: Department of Physics, University of Edinburgh
items.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 21, 257-270

items.claim: Kirkpatrick and Thirumalai identified the dynamics of the p-spin-interaction spin-glass model with the structural glass transition, showing the mean-field p-spin model reproduces mode-coupling-like dynamical arrest — the seed of RFOT theory.
items.people: Theodore R. Kirkpatrick; Devarajan Thirumalai
items.affiliation: University of Maryland

items.claim: Random first-order transition (RFOT) theory: a scaling and droplet ('mosaic') picture of an ideal structural glass transition in which the supercooled liquid is made of glassy clusters separated by domain walls; as the ideal transition temperature is approached the entropic driving force vanishes and the cluster size diverges with exponent nu = 2/d.
items.people: Theodore R. Kirkpatrick; Devarajan Thirumalai; Peter G. Wolynes
items.affiliation: University of Maryland (Kirkpatrick, Thirumalai); University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (Wolynes, at the time; later Rice University)

items.claim: The original jamming phase diagram. Liu and Nagel proposed that granular materials, foams, emulsions and supercooled liquids all sit on one phase diagram whose axes are temperature, applied load/stress and inverse density, so that thermal glass formation and athermal granular jamming are the same unjamming-to-jamming transition seen along different axes. NOTE: this one-page Nature article IS titled 'Jamming is not just cool any more' — it is not a separate later framing.
items.people: Andrea J. Liu; Sidney R. Nagel
items.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles (Liu, at the time; later University of Pennsylvania); James Franck Institute, University of Chicago (Nagel)

items.claim: Point J. For frictionless spheres with finite-range repulsion at zero temperature and zero applied stress, each configuration jams at its own threshold packing fraction; the distribution narrows with system size and converges to random close packing. Point J behaves like a critical point with power-law scaling of contact number, pressure and elastic moduli; the exponents do not depend on dimension but do depend on the interparticle potential, and low-frequency vibrational modes proliferate near the transition.
items.people: Corey S. O'Hern; Leonardo E. Silbert; Andrea J. Liu; Sidney R. Nagel
items.affiliation: Andrea J. Liu then at UCLA; Sidney R. Nagel at the James Franck Institute, University of Chicago; O'Hern later Yale University and Silbert later Southern Illinois University Carbondale (per-author affiliations at time of publication not verified in this search)

items.claim: Review of the jamming transition and the marginally jammed solid: when a system jams it goes from flowing to rigid while its structure stays disordered on both sides, and the marginally jammed solid near point J has anomalous vibrational and elastic properties (excess low-frequency modes, diverging length scales, non-affine response).
items.people: Andrea J. Liu; Sidney R. Nagel
items.affiliation: University of Pennsylvania (Liu); James Franck Institute, University of Chicago (Nagel)
items.venue: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics 1, 347-369

items.claim: Twenty-five-year retrospective on the jamming phase diagram by its authors, arguing that linking jammed granular materials with glasses has been productive for understanding a wide class of systems. This is the 'later framing' piece, distinct from the 1998 Nature original.
items.people: Andrea J. Liu; Sidney R. Nagel
items.affiliation: University of Pennsylvania (Liu); University of Chicago (Nagel)

items.claim: The standard modern review of glass-transition theory: lays out MCT, RFOT, dynamic facilitation and free-volume/kinetically-constrained pictures side by side on a microscopic statistical-mechanics footing, plus dynamic heterogeneity, aging and soft-glassy rheology. Useful as the neutral source when a book needs to say the field has several live theories rather than one.
items.people: Ludovic Berthier; Giulio Biroli
items.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Coulomb, Université de Montpellier and CNRS (Berthier); Institut de Physique Théorique, CEA Saclay / later Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris (Biroli)

items.claim: Fractal free-energy landscapes: deep in the glass phase the landscape undergoes a 'roughness transition' in which each glass basin shatters into a fractal hierarchy of marginally stable sub-basins — the Gardner transition, carried over from spin glasses into structural glasses. This marginality is what produces isostaticity and the critical exponents (basin width, weak-force distribution, quasi-contact spread) observed at jamming, folding granular jamming into glass theory.
items.people: Patrick Charbonneau; Jorge Kurchan; Giorgio Parisi; Pierfrancesco Urbani; Francesco Zamponi
items.affiliation: Duke University (Charbonneau); École Normale Supérieure / ESPCI, Paris (Kurchan); Sapienza Università di Roma (Parisi); Institut de Physique Théorique, CEA Saclay (Urbani); École Normale Supérieure, Paris (Zamponi)

items.claim: First numerical detection of the Gardner transition, in the infinite-range Mari-Kurchan model, located consistently by three independent signatures: divergence of the characteristic relaxation time, divergence of the caging susceptibility, and an anomalous tail in the distribution of cage order parameters.
items.people: Patrick Charbonneau; Yuliang Jin; Giorgio Parisi; Corrado Rainone; Beatriz Seoane; Francesco Zamponi
items.affiliation: Duke University (Charbonneau); Sapienza Università di Roma (Jin, Parisi, Rainone); École Normale Supérieure, Paris (Zamponi) — per-author affiliations not verified in this search

items.claim: Experimental evidence of a Gardner phase in a real granular system: in a vibrated bidisperse 2D disk packing, repeated compression cycles on the same glass make particles pick different average vibrational positions each cycle while the neighbour structure is unchanged; the inter-cycle cage separation plateaus with increasing packing fraction while the mean-square displacement keeps falling.
items.people: Alexandre Seguin; Olivier Dauchot
items.affiliation: ESPCI Paris (Dauchot, EC2M/Gulliver); Seguin's affiliation at the time not verified in this search

items.claim: Authoritative review of the exact mean-field (infinite-dimensional) solution of hard spheres and what survives in finite dimensions: the dynamical (MCT-like) transition, the Gardner transition, and the jamming transition, with an explicit accounting of which predictions numerical simulations confirm and which are dimension-sensitive.
items.people: Patrick Charbonneau; Jorge Kurchan; Giorgio Parisi; Pierfrancesco Urbani; Francesco Zamponi
items.affiliation: Duke University; ENS/ESPCI Paris; Sapienza Università di Roma; CEA Saclay
items.venue: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics 8, 265-288 (preprint arXiv:1605.03008)

items.claim: The swap Monte Carlo algorithm equilibrates realistic glass-forming liquid models beyond experimental timescales, closing an eight-order-of-magnitude gap between simulation and experiment and letting configurational entropy be measured below the experimental glass transition; the measured steep entropy decrease continues, supporting an entropy-crisis scenario.
items.people: Ludovic Berthier; Patrick Charbonneau; Daniele Coslovich; Andrea Ninarello; Misaki Ozawa; Sho Yaida
items.affiliation: Université de Montpellier and CNRS (Berthier, Coslovich, Ninarello, Ozawa); Duke University (Charbonneau, Yaida)

items.claim: In two dimensions the liquid state terminates at a thermodynamic glass transition that occurs at ZERO temperature, with an entropy crisis and a diverging static correlation length — i.e. the ideal glass transition exists but is pushed to T=0 in 2D, unlike the finite-temperature transition inferred in 3D. A key data point in the still-open dimensional-dependence question.
items.people: Ludovic Berthier; Patrick Charbonneau; Andrea Ninarello; Misaki Ozawa; Sho Yaida
items.affiliation: Université de Montpellier and CNRS; Duke University

items.claim: Survey of the ideal-glass question from the sceptical side: reviews the competing positions — an ideal amorphous state of exceptionally low entropy versus a purely dynamic, no-transition account — and assesses how close the deepest experimental and simulated glasses actually get to any putative ideal state.
items.people: C. Patrick Royall; Francesco Turci; Soichi Tatsumi; John Russo; Joshua Robinson
items.affiliation: University of Bristol (Royall, Turci, Russo, Robinson; Royall later ESPCI Paris) — Tatsumi's affiliation not verified in this search
items.venue: Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter 30, 363001 (preprint arXiv:1711.04739)

items.claim: Recent stock-taking of RFOT: the theory reproduces the salient experimental facts of supercooled liquids remarkably well and its static/thermodynamic side has gained support, but direct experimental validation remains elusive and the dynamical extension struggles with facilitation effects. Good source for stating honestly that the ideal glass transition is unresolved.
items.people: Giulio Biroli; Jean-Philippe Bouchaud
items.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris (Biroli); Capital Fund Management and Académie des Sciences, Paris (Bouchaud) — affiliations not verified against the primary article in this search

items.claim: First 'softness' paper. Support vector machines trained on local structural descriptors (radial and angular symmetry functions) identify 'flow defects' — particles susceptible to rearrangement — in both a 2D granular pillar experiment under compression and Lennard-Jones glasses in 2D and 3D, above and below the glass transition. This is where the ML-order-parameter programme starts.
items.people: Ekin D. Cubuk; Samuel S. Schoenholz; Jennifer M. Rieser; Brad D. Malone; Joerg Rottler; Douglas J. Durian; Efthimios Kaxiras; Andrea J. Liu
items.affiliation: Harvard University (Cubuk, Malone, Kaxiras); University of Pennsylvania (Schoenholz, Rieser, Durian, Liu); University of British Columbia (Rottler)

items.claim: 'Softness' as a machine-learned structural order parameter for glassy liquids: a scalar field learned from local structure that correlates strongly with subsequent rearrangement, and whose onset of correlation with dynamics coincides with the onset temperature T0 of glassy dynamics. A simple two-state model driven by softness reproduces the simulated relaxation. This is the canonical 'ML finds order in the amorphous' result.
items.people: Samuel S. Schoenholz; Ekin D. Cubuk; Daniel M. Sussman; Efthimios Kaxiras; Andrea J. Liu
items.affiliation: University of Pennsylvania (Schoenholz, Sussman, Liu); Harvard University (Cubuk, Kaxiras)

items.claim: Softness generalises across materials: combining experiments and simulations, the machine-learned softness field predicts plasticity in disordered solids spanning roughly seven orders of magnitude in particle size, from atomic metallic glasses to granular pillars, giving a universal structure-property relation for amorphous plasticity.
items.people: Ekin D. Cubuk; Robert J. S. Ivancic; Samuel S. Schoenholz; Douglas J. Durian; Efthimios Kaxiras; Andrea J. Liu and additional coauthors (a large multi-group author list)
items.affiliation: University of Pennsylvania; Harvard University; Google Brain; and collaborating groups (full per-author affiliation list not retrieved in this search)

items.claim: The DeepMind graph-neural-network result: a GNN predicts the long-time evolution of a glassy system from the initial particle positions alone, with no hand-crafted features, outperforming prior structural indicators and generalising across temperature, pressure and density; under shear it also predicts where rearrangements occur. Author list order matters — Bapst first, Kohli last, and Demis Hassabis (not Peter Battaglia) appears in the published author list. An Author Correction was issued in 2020 (Nature Physics, DOI 10.1038/s41567-020-0901-1). Code released at github.com/google-deepmind/deepmind-research (glassy_dynamics).
items.people: Victor Bapst; Thomas Keck; Agnieszka Grabska-Barwińska; Craig Donner; Ekin D. Cubuk; Samuel S. Schoenholz; Annette Obika; Alexander W. R. Nelson; Trevor Back; Demis Hassabis; Pushmeet Kohli
items.affiliation: DeepMind, London (Bapst, Keck, Grabska-Barwińska, Donner, Obika, Nelson, Back, Hassabis, Kohli); Google Brain (Cubuk, Schoenholz)

items.claim: Unsupervised counterpoint to supervised softness/GNN work: an autoencoder-based method autonomously designs a purely structural order parameter from a single snapshot of three archetypal glass formers, using no dynamical information at all, and still correlates strongly with dynamic heterogeneity — while showing the structural signature of slow particles fades away from the glass transition.
items.people: Emanuele Boattini; Susana Marín-Aguilar; Saheli Mitra; Giuseppe Foffi; Frank Smallenburg; Laura Filion
items.affiliation: Debye Institute for Nanomaterials Science, Utrecht University (Boattini, Marín-Aguilar, Mitra, Filion); Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Laboratoire de Physique des Solides (Foffi, Smallenburg)

items.claim: The central deflation of the GNN result. Boattini, Smallenburg and Filion argue the key structural ingredient the GNN supplies is simply the ability to use structural descriptors AVERAGED over nearby particles, not the network's expressiveness. Verbatim from the abstract: the best GNN predictions come 'at a cost of models that involve on the order of 10^5 fit parameters,' whereas their neighbour-averaged model 'provides essentially the same predictive power at a fraction of the computational complexity (approximately 1000 fit parameters).' Demonstrated on Kob-Andersen and binary hard-sphere mixtures. A companion comparison (Alkemade, Boattini, Filion, Smallenburg, J. Chem. Phys. 156, 204503 (2022), arXiv:2202.09173) found linear regression, neural networks and GNNs nearly equally accurate once advanced descriptors are used, with linear regression orders of magnitude faster to train.
items.people: Emanuele Boattini; Frank Smallenburg; Laura Filion
items.affiliation: Soft Condensed Matter, Debye Institute for Nanomaterials Science, Utrecht University (Boattini, Filion); Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Laboratoire de Physique des Solides (Smallenburg)

items.claim: GlassMLP: a physics-inspired deep network whose inputs are chosen from glass physics rather than learned from raw coordinates. It beats the state of the art (including the GNN) on 2D and 3D atomistic models while being more parsimonious in both training data and fitting parameters, and it quantitatively predicts four-point dynamic correlations and the geometry of dynamic heterogeneity. Its transferability across system sizes was later used to push predictions of dynamic heterogeneity down to the experimental glass transition temperature (Jung, Biroli, Berthier, Phys. Rev. B 109, 064205 (2024), arXiv:2310.20252).
items.people: Gerhard Jung; Giulio Biroli; Ludovic Berthier
items.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Coulomb, Université de Montpellier and CNRS (Jung, Berthier); Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris (Biroli); Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge (Berthier)

items.claim: The interpretability critique. Studying SVMs trained to predict dynamics from structure (the softness construction), the authors find that reading the distance from the separating hyperplane as an activation energy is valid only under very restricted conditions, and that the usual sanity checks — apparent Arrhenius temperature dependence and high cross-validation accuracy — do NOT guarantee the model has inferred the correct energy barriers. Predicting well is not the same as learning the physics. Note that Sean A. Ridout is himself a practitioner of ML-for-glasses, so this is an internal critique, not an outsider's.
items.people: Arabind Swain; Sean Alexander Ridout; Ilya Nemenman
items.affiliation: Department of Physics, Emory University (affiliation not verified line-by-line in this search)

items.claim: Community roadmap for ML applied to glassy dynamics, co-authored by principals from both camps (Bapst from the DeepMind paper, Liu from the softness papers, Filion and Berthier from the critiques). Surveys successes and names the open problems explicitly — transferability and interpretability of ML approaches — and introduces GlassBench, a shared 2D and 3D glass-former simulation dataset and benchmark. This is the best single citation for 'the field has not settled what the ML result means.'
items.people: Gerhard Jung; Rinske M. Alkemade; Victor Bapst; Daniele Coslovich; Laura Filion; François P. Landes; Andrea J. Liu; Francesco Saverio Pezzicoli; Hayato Shiba; Giovanni Volpe; Francesco Zamponi; Ludovic Berthier; Giulio Biroli
items.affiliation: Université de Montpellier; Utrecht University; DeepMind; Università di Trieste; Université Paris-Saclay/LISN; University of Pennsylvania; University of Hyogo; University of Gothenburg; Sapienza Università di Roma; École Normale Supérieure, Paris (mapping of authors to institutions not verified individually in this search)

openQuestions: FACT CORRECTION for the brief: 'Liu and Nagel's jamming phase diagram (Nature 1998)' and 'Jamming is not just cool any more' are the SAME article (Nature 396, 21-22, 1998). Do not present them as two separate works. The genuinely later framing is Liu and Nagel, Nature Reviews Physics 5, 630-631 (2023), 'Twenty-five years of the jamming phase diagram'.

Does an ideal glass transition exist in finite dimensions? Swap-Monte-Carlo configurational-entropy measurements (Berthier et al., PNAS 2017) support a continuing entropy crisis in 3D, while the same group finds the 2D transition sits at zero temperature (Nat. Commun. 2019). Royall et al. (2018) and Biroli and Bouchaud (2023) both note direct experimental validation is still missing. Present this as unresolved, not settled.

Is the Gardner transition a sharp transition in three dimensions, or does it become a crossover/avoided transition? It is exact in infinite dimension, detected numerically in mean-field-like models (Charbonneau et al., PRE 2015) and seen in a granular experiment (Seguin and Dauchot, PRL 2016), but its finite-dimensional status remains contested — I did not find a definitive resolution and would not assert one.

How much of the DeepMind GNN result is a genuine demonstration that static structure encodes long-time dynamics, versus a demonstration that coarse-graining over neighbours does? Boattini, Smallenburg and Filion (PRL 2021) reproduce GNN accuracy with ~1000 parameters; Alkemade et al. (JCP 2022) find linear regression essentially ties GNNs; Jung, Biroli and Berthier (PRL 2023) beat the GNN with physics-chosen inputs. The honest framing is that the GNN's headline advantage did not survive.

Does machine-learned 'softness' correspond to a real physical quantity (an energy barrier) or only to a good predictor? Swain, Ridout and Nemenman (PRR 2024) show the usual validation tests do not establish the physical reading. This is the sharpest available caution for a book chapter that wants to claim ML 'discovered hidden order'.

Is point J a true critical point in the thermodynamic sense, and how does the athermal jamming criticality connect to the thermal glass transition? The 1998 phase diagram asserts a connection; the mean-field Gardner picture (Charbonneau et al. 2014) supplies one mechanism; whether the connection holds in 3D frictional real granular matter is still argued.

Per-author institutional affiliations at time of publication were not verifiable for several older items (Kauzmann 1948, Adam and Gibbs 1965, Bengtzelius/Götze/Sjölander 1984, and the individual affiliations on O'Hern et al. 2003 and Cubuk et al. Science 2017). Several publisher pages returned 403 or paywall redirects. These fields are marked as unverified rather than guessed and should be checked against the PDFs before the book cites them.
The full author list of Cubuk et al., Science 358, 1033 (2017) is long and I retrieved it only in truncated 'et al.' form; do not print a partial list as if complete.

Article/volume numbers marked 'probable' (Charbonneau et al. Nat. Commun. 5, 3725 (2014); Boattini et al. Nat. Commun. 11, 5479 (2020); Royall et al. J. Phys. Condens. Matter 30, 363001 (2018); Nat. Commun. volume for Berthier et al. 2019) came from search summaries rather than a primary page and should be re-checked.

verdicts.correction: Verified. Walter Kauzmann, Chem. Rev. 43, 219-256 (1948), DOI 10.1021/cr60135a002; URL resolves to that article. Affiliation upgraded from 'not verified': the article PDF (jupiter.chem.uoa.gr/thanost/papers/papers1/ChemRev_43(1948)219.pdf) shows Princeton University, received March 1, 1948. The substantive claim (extrapolated excess entropy of the supercooled liquid falling below the crystal's at finite T) is an accurate statement of the paper's argument.

verdicts.claim: Adam and Gibbs 1965, J. Chem. Phys. 43, 139-146, cooperatively rearranging region, relaxation time tied to configurational entropy, close to WLF/VFT. URL https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1696442
verdicts.correction: Verified. Gerald Adam and Julian H. Gibbs, 'On the Temperature Dependence of Cooperative Relaxation Properties in Glass-Forming Liquids', J. Chem. Phys. 43(1), 139-146 (1965), DOI 10.1063/1.1696442. The paper's own abstract states the result 'practically coincides' with the empirical WLF equation, so the dossier's 'a form close to the empirical WLF/VFT law' is accurate rather than overstated. Author names, order, year, venue and pages all correct. Affiliations remain unverified (both were at Brown University at the time per secondary sources; not confirmed against the primary article — leave the field blank rather than assert).

verdicts.claim: Bengtzelius, Götze and Sjölander 1984, J. Phys. C 17, 5915-5934, mode-coupling theory; hard-sphere glass transition at packing fraction 0.516. URL https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3719/17/33/005
verdicts.correction: Verified, and upgrade confidence from 'probable' to verified. 'Dynamics of supercooled liquids and the glass transition', J. Phys. C: Solid State Phys. 17, issue 33, 5915-5934 (1984); URL resolves. The number 0.516 is verbatim from the published abstract: the hard-sphere solution 'brings out a phase transition to a glass at the packing fraction 0.516'. Author names, spelling (Sjölander, Götze) and order correct. Affiliations: the Technical University of Munich research portal indexes the paper, supporting Götze at TUM; Bengtzelius and Sjölander at Chalmers is plausible but was NOT confirmed against the article — keep flagged. The added sentence 'MCT's sharp transition is not observed experimentally and is now read as a crossover' is a correct statement of the modern consensus but is editorial, not a finding of the 1984 paper; attribute it to a review (e.g. Berthier and Biroli 2011) rather than to Bengtzelius et al.

verdicts.claim: Gardner 1985, Nuclear Physics B 257, 747-765, 'Spin glasses with p-spin interactions' — two transitions, T1 discontinuous without latent heat, lower T2 instability (the Gardner transition). URL sciencedirect pii/0550321385903748
verdicts.correction: Verified. Elizabeth Gardner, Nucl. Phys. B 257 [FS14], 747-765 (1985); URL resolves to the correct article. The published abstract independently confirms both transitions and the 'jump in the order parameter but without latent heat' phrasing at T1. Affiliation (Department of Physics, University of Edinburgh) is correct. One wording caution for the book: the paper describes T2 as a second-order transition at which the order parameter changes smoothly; the identification of that instability as the onset of full RSB is the standard modern reading, not language Gardner herself used — do not put 'full RSB' in quotation marks as if quoted.

verdicts.claim: Gardner 1988, J. Phys. A 21, 257-270, 'The space of interactions in neural network models' — the Gardner volume, storage capacity. URL https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0305-4470/21/1/030
verdicts.correction: Verified. E. Gardner, J. Phys. A: Math. Gen. 21, 257-270 (1988), DOI 10.1088/0305-4470/21/1/030; URL resolves. The abstract confirms the computation of the typical fraction of the space of interactions storing p random patterns in N Ising spins as a function of alpha = p/N. Edinburgh affiliation correct. Note for the book: the capacity result is usually cited alongside the companion Gardner and Derrida, J. Phys. A 21, 271-284 (1988); if the text says Gardner 'established the statistical-mechanics theory of neural-network storage capacity', that is defensible but the companion paper deserves mention.

verdicts.claim: Kirkpatrick and Thirumalai 1987, Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 2091 — p-spin dynamics identified with the structural glass transition. URL https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.2091
verdicts.correction: Verified. Exact title: 'Dynamics of the Structural Glass Transition and the p-Spin-Interaction Spin-Glass Model', Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 2091 (published 18 May 1987); URL resolves. Author names and order correct. Caution: there is a closely related same-year paper by the same authors, Phys. Rev. B 36, 5388 (1987), 'p-spin-interaction spin-glass models: Connections with the structural glass problem'. Do not let the two swap titles in the bibliography.

verdicts.claim: Kirkpatrick, Thirumalai and Wolynes 1989, Phys. Rev. A 40, 1045-1054 — RFOT mosaic/droplet picture, nu = 2/d. URL https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.40.1045
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'Scaling concepts for the dynamics of viscous liquids near an ideal glassy state', Phys. Rev. A 40, 1045 (1 July 1989); URL resolves. The abstract independently confirms the random-first-order framing, the glassy-clusters-separated-by-domain-walls picture, and the entropic driving force. Author names and order correct. The nu = 2/d exponent is correct for this paper. Affiliations as given (Maryland for Kirkpatrick and Thirumalai; Illinois at Urbana-Champaign for Wolynes at the time) are consistent with the record.

verdicts.claim: Liu and Nagel 1998, Nature 396, 21-22, 'Jamming is not just cool any more' IS the original jamming phase diagram paper, not a separate later framing. URL https://doi.org/10.1038/23819

Nagel, Nature 396, 21-22 (1998), DOI 10.1038/23819, and it carries the title 'Jamming is not just cool any more'. Do not present the phase diagram and the 'not just cool any more' framing as two works. verdicts.correction: The article is real and correctly cited, but THE URL IS GARBLED AND DOES NOT RESOLVE TO IT. The string 'annurev-co-1-101613-200001' is not this article's identifier; that URL returns 403 and belongs to no such work. Correct citation: Andrea J. Liu and Sidney R. Nagel, 'The Jamming Transition and the Marginally Jammed Solid', Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics 1, 347-369 (2010), DOI 10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-070909-104045. Correct URL: https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-070909-104045 (publisher page: https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-070909-104045). Authors, year, volume, pages and affiliations (Penn for Liu by 2010; James Franck Institute, Chicago for Nagel) are all correct as given. The substantive claim (rigidity without normal-solid elastic properties, excess low-frequency modes, diverging length scales, non-affine response) is an accurate summary.

verdicts.claim: Liu and Nagel 2023, Nature Reviews Physics 5, 630-631, twenty-five-year retrospective on the jamming phase diagram. URL https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-023-00661-5
verdicts.correction: Verified. Exact title: 'Twenty-five years of the jamming phase diagram', Nat. Rev. Phys. 5(11), 630-631 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s42254-023-00661-5, published 20 October 2023; URL resolves. An open accepted manuscript is at https://par.nsf.gov/biblio/10507295. Authors, affiliations, volume and pages correct. This is indeed the genuine 'later framing' piece, distinct from the 1998 original.

verdicts.claim: Berthier and Biroli 2011, Reviews of Modern Physics 83, 587-645, standard review laying out MCT, RFOT, facilitation and free-volume pictures side by side. URL https://arxiv.org/pdf/1011.2578
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'Theoretical perspective on the glass transition and amorphous materials', Rev. Mod. Phys. 83, 587 (2011); arXiv:1011.2578 resolves to exactly this paper and the arXiv journal-ref confirms the volume and page. Author names and order correct. The characterisation (competing live theories, dynamic heterogeneity, aging, soft glassy rheology, on a microscopic statistical-mechanics footing) matches the abstract and is not overstated. Prefer citing the DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.83.587 alongside the arXiv link in a book bibliography.

verdicts.claim: Charbonneau, Kurchan, Parisi, Urbani and Zamponi 2014, Nature Communications 5, 3725, 'Fractal free energy landscapes in structural glasses' — roughness/Gardner transition, marginality producing isostaticity and jamming exponents. URL https://arxiv.org/pdf/1404.6809
verdicts.correction: Verified, and upgrade confidence from 'probable' to verified. Nature Communications 5, 3725 (2014); PubMed 24759041; arXiv:1404.6809 resolves to the same work. The abstract independently confirms the 'roughness transition' to fractal basins, and that the work 'brings about isostaticity at jamming and marginality of glassy states near jamming', with analytically determined critical exponents for the basin width, the weak-force distribution and the spatial spread of quasi-contacts — every element of the dossier's claim. Author names, spelling and order correct.

verdicts.claim: Charbonneau, Jin, Parisi, Rainone, Seoane and Zamponi 2015, Phys. Rev. E 92, 012316 — first numerical detection of the Gardner transition in the Mari-Kurchan model via three independent signatures. URL https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.92.012316
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'Numerical detection of the Gardner transition in a mean-field glass former', Phys. Rev. E 92, 012316 (21 July 2015); arXiv:1501.07244. The abstract confirms the infinite-range Mari-Kurchan model and all three named signatures: divergence of the characteristic relaxation time, divergence of the caging susceptibility, and the abnormal tail in the probability distribution of cage order parameters. Six-author list, spelling and order correct. One wording caution: the paper frames itself as exploring methods to detect the transition in a mean-field glass former, so 'first numerical detection' is a defensible but slightly promotional gloss — 'the paper that established the numerical signatures' is safer. Per-author affiliations remain unverified.

verdicts.claim: Seguin and Dauchot 2016, Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 228001 — Gardner phase in a vibrated 2D bidisperse granular glass; inter-cycle cage separation plateaus while mean-square displacement keeps falling. URL https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.117.228001
verdicts.correction: Verified verbatim against the abstract, including the quantitative detail: 'The separation between the cages obtained for different compression cycles plateaus with an increasing packing fraction, while the mean square displacement steadily decreases.' Authors are Antoine Seguin and Olivier Dauchot; PRL 117, 228001 (21 November 2016); arXiv:1605.00827. URL resolves. Two notes: (a) the arXiv title is plural, 'Experimental evidences of the Gardner phase in a granular glass', while the published PRL title is 'Experimental Evidence of the Gardner Phase in a Granular Glass' — cite the published form; (b) the abstract explicitly flags differences from the numerical results in the cage-order-parameter distribution, attributed to activated processes and cage heterogeneities, so the book should not present this as clean confirmation.

verdicts.claim: Charbonneau, Kurchan, Parisi, Urbani and Zamponi 2017, Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics 8, 265-288, review of the exact mean-field hard-sphere solution. URL https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031016-025334
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'Glass and Jamming Transitions: From Exact Results to Finite-Dimensional Descriptions', Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 8, 265-288 (2017), DOI 10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031016-025334; arXiv:1605.03008. URL resolves. Author names and order correct. The characterisation (exact solution in the mean-field limit of infinite spatial dimension, with numerics confirming the dimensional robustness of some predictions) matches the abstract and is appropriately hedged.

verdicts.claim: Berthier, Charbonneau, Coslovich, Ninarello, Ozawa and Yaida 2017, PNAS 114, 11356-11361 — swap Monte Carlo closes an eight-order-of-magnitude gap, configurational entropy measured below the experimental glass transition. URL https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1706860114
verdicts.correction: Verified. PNAS 114(43), 11356-11361 (2017), DOI 10.1073/pnas.1706860114, PMID 29073056; arXiv:1704.08257. URL resolves. Six-author list and order correct (Ninarello's full name is Andrea Saverio Ninarello). The abstract supports the claims that simulations normally cover at most 4-5 decades, that swap Monte Carlo closes that gap and equilibrates beyond experimental timescales, and that the steep entropy decrease continues. Two cautions for the book: the paper's own framing is '4-5 decades' of gap rather than the round 'eight orders of magnitude' — check the exact figure against the text before printing it; and the paper says the measurements are consistent with an entropy crisis, not that they prove one, so 'supporting an entropy-crisis scenario' is the right strength and should not be hardened.

verdicts.claim: Berthier, Charbonneau, Ninarello, Ozawa and Yaida 2019, Nature Communications, DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-09512-3 — zero-temperature ideal glass transition in two dimensions. Affiliations: Université de Montpellier and CNRS; Duke University.
verdicts.correction: The work and DOI are correct, but the citation is incomplete and the affiliation lump is wrong. Complete citation: Ludovic Berthier, Patrick Charbonneau, Andrea Ninarello, Misaki Ozawa and Sho Yaida, 'Zero-temperature glass transition in two dimensions', Nature Communications 10, 1508 (2019), DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-09512-3, published 3 April 2019; PMID 30944330; preprint arXiv:1805.09035. Supply the volume (10) and article number (1508) — the dossier left them blank. Affiliation correction: at publication Berthier and Ozawa were at Laboratoire Charles Coulomb, University of Montpellier; Charbonneau at Duke (Chemistry and Physics); Ninarello at CNR-ISC, UOS Sapienza, Rome — NOT Montpellier; and Yaida at Facebook AI Research — NOT Duke. Correct URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-09512-3 (note nature.com redirects through an IdP for automated fetches; the DOI is the stable citation). The substantive claim (liquid state terminates at a thermodynamic glass transition at zero temperature, with an entropy crisis and a diverging static correlation length) is accurate.

verdicts.claim: Royall, Turci, Tatsumi, Russo and Robinson 2018, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 30, 363001, sceptical survey of the ideal-glass question. URL https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1361-648X/aad10a
verdicts.correction: Verified, and upgrade confidence from 'probable' to verified. 'The race to the bottom: approaching the ideal glass?', J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 30, number 36, article 363001, published 14 August 2018, DOI 10.1088/1361-648X/aad10a; preprint arXiv:1711.04739. URL resolves. Five-author list and order correct. The characterisation matches the abstract, which explicitly contrasts approaches positing 'a bona fide thermodynamic phase to an ideal glass — an amorphous state with exceptionally low entropy' against alternatives, and reviews very stable glasses in experiment and simulation. Tatsumi's affiliation remains unverified; do not assert Bristol for him.

verdicts.claim: Biroli and Bouchaud 2023, Comptes Rendus. Physique 24 (S1), 9-23, recent stock-taking of RFOT. URL comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr .../10.5802/crphys.136/
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'The RFOT Theory of Glasses: Recent Progress and Open Issues', Giulio Biroli and Jean-Philippe Bouchaud, C. R. Physique 24, no. S1, 9-23 (2023), DOI 10.5802/crphys.136; preprint arXiv:2208.05866 (2022); also on HAL (hal-05016662). URL resolves. The abstract confirms both the credit to Kirkpatrick, Thirumalai and Wolynes and the 'fares remarkably well at reproducing the salient experimental facts' framing, so the dossier's summary is accurate and not overstated. Affiliations were not verified against the article; the dossier already flags this.

verdicts.claim: Cubuk, Schoenholz, Rieser, Malone, Rottler, Durian, Kaxiras and Liu 2015, Phys. Rev. Lett. 114, 108001, first 'softness' paper — SVMs identify flow defects in a granular pillar experiment and in 2D/3D Lennard-Jones glasses. URL https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.108001
verdicts.correction: Verified in full, including the eight-author list, spelling and order exactly as the dossier gives them. 'Identifying Structural Flow Defects in Disordered Solids Using Machine-Learning Methods', Phys. Rev. Lett. 114(10), 108001 (2015); preprint arXiv:1409.6820. URL resolves. The abstract independently confirms both test systems — a two-dimensional experimental granular pillar under compression, and a Lennard-Jones glass in two and three dimensions above and below its glass transition temperature. Affiliations (Harvard for Cubuk, Malone, Kaxiras; Penn for Schoenholz, Rieser, Durian, Liu; UBC for Rottler) are consistent with the record. Note Kaxiras IS an author here — which is precisely why the Science 2017 entry's author list must be fixed.

verdicts.claim: Schoenholz, Cubuk, Sussman, Kaxiras and Liu 2016, Nature Physics 12, 469-471, 'softness' as a machine-learned structural order parameter; onset of softness-dynamics correlation coincides with T0. URL https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys3644
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'A structural approach to relaxation in glassy liquids', Nat. Phys. 12, 469 (2016), DOI 10.1038/nphys3644; preprint arXiv:1506.07772 (2015). Five-author list and order correct. The abstract independently confirms both distinctive sub-claims: the machine-learned 'softness' field strongly correlated with dynamics, and that the onset of glassy dynamics at T0 corresponds to the onset of correlations between structure and dynamics. Page range 469-471 is the standard citation and is consistent with ADS (2016NatPh..12..469S).

verdicts.claim: Cubuk et al. 2017, Science 358, 1033-1037 — softness generalises across ~seven orders of magnitude in particle size. People listed: 'Ekin D. Cubuk; Robert J. S. Ivancic; Samuel S. Schoenholz; Douglas J. Durian; Efthimios Kaxiras; Andrea J. Liu and additional coauthors'.
verdicts.correction: The article is real and correctly located, but the author list is WRONG in a way that must be fixed: EFTHIMIOS KAXIRAS IS NOT AN AUTHOR of this paper. Confirmed independently against the PubMed Central full text (PMC6047528), PubMed 29170231 and the Semantic Scholar record, none of which list him; Kaxiras appears only in the reference list (refs 19-21). Douglas Durian is also not the fourth author — he sits deep in the list, not adjacent to Schoenholz. Correct opening of the author list: E. D. Cubuk, R. J. S. Ivancic, S. S. Schoenholz, D. J. Strickland, A. Basu, Z. S. Davidson, J. Fontaine, J. L. Hor, Y.-R. Huang, Y. Jiang, N. C. Keim, K. D. Koshigan, J. A. Lefever, T. Liu, X.-G. Ma, D. J. Magagnosc, E. Morrow, C. P. Ortiz, J. M. Rieser, A. Shavit, T. Still, Y. Xu, Y. Zhang, K. N. Nordstrom, P. E. Arratia, R. W. Carpick, D. J. Durian, Z. Fakhraai, D. J. Jerolmack, D. Lee, J. Li, R. Riggleman, K. T. Turner, A. G. Yodh, D. S. Gianola, A. J. Liu. Because the list runs to ~36 names, cite as 'E. D. Cubuk et al., Science 358, 1033-1037 (2017)' and do not print a partial list as if complete. Full citation: 'Structure-property relationships from universal signatures of plasticity in disordered solids', Science 358, 1033-1037 (2017), DOI 10.1126/science.aai8830; URL https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aai8830 resolves; open text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6047528/. The scientific claim is CORRECT and verbatim supportable: the abstract says the four quantities held 'for disordered packings of objects ranging from atoms to grains, spanning seven orders of magnitude in diameter and 13 orders of magnitude in elastic modulus'. If the book quantifies the span, quote 'seven orders of magnitude in diameter', not 'in particle size'.

verdicts.claim: Bapst, Keck, Grabska-Barwińska, Donner, Cubuk, Schoenholz, Obika, Nelson, Back, Hassabis and Kohli 2020, Nature Physics 16, 448-454 — GNN predicts long-time glassy dynamics from initial positions; Author Correction 10.1038/s41567-020-0901-1; code at github.com/google-deepmind/deepmind-research (glassy_dynamics). URL https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-020-0842-8
verdicts.correction: Verified with unusual care because the dossier stakes a claim on author order. The published list is exactly, in order: V. Bapst, T. Keck, A. Grabska-Barwińska, C. Donner, E. D. Cubuk, S. S. Schoenholz, A. Obika, A. W. R. Nelson, T. Back, D. Hassabis, P. Kohli — confirmed against both the Semantic Scholar record for DOI 10.1038/s41567-020-0842-8 and the DeepMind repository README. The dossier is right that Bapst is first, Kohli last, and Demis Hassabis (not Peter Battaglia) is in the list; Battaglia is NOT an author. Nature Physics 16, 448-454 (2020); URL resolves. The Author Correction exists at DOI 10.1038/s41567-020-0901-1 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-020-0901-1). The code path github.com/google-deepmind/deepmind-research/tree/master/glassy_dynamics exists and cites this paper. Every sub-claim matches the abstract, including 'In shear experiments, it predicts the location of rearranging particles' and the growing correlation length reaching the system size.

verdicts.claim: Boattini, Marín-Aguilar, Mitra, Foffi, Smallenburg and Filion 2020, Nature Communications 11, 5479 — unsupervised autoencoder-based order parameter from a single snapshot; structural signature of slow particles fades away from the glass transition. URL https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19286-8
verdicts.correction: Verified, and upgrade confidence from 'probable' to verified. 'Autonomously revealing hidden local structures in supercooled liquids', Nature Communications 11, 5479 (30 October 2020), DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-19286-8; preprint arXiv:2003.00586. Six-author list, spelling (Marín-Aguilar) and order correct. Both sub-claims are verbatim in the abstract: 'the UML approach autonomously designs an order parameter based purely on structural variation within a single snapshot', and 'the structural characteristics linked to slow particles disappear as we move away from the glass transition'. One precision note: the paper calls the method 'unsupervised machine learning (UML)' throughout; the dossier's 'autoencoder-based' is an implementation detail not stated in the abstract — verify it against the methods section before describing it that way in print.

verdicts.claim: Boattini, Smallenburg and Filion 2021, Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 088007 — neighbour-averaged ~1000-parameter model matches GNN accuracy; the quoted phrases about 10^5 fit parameters and 'approximately 1000 fit parameters'. Companion: Alkemade, Boattini, Filion, Smallenburg, J. Chem. Phys. 156, 204503 (2022). URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05921
verdicts.correction: Verified, including both quotations word for word against the arXiv abstract: the best GNN predictions come 'at a cost of models that involve on the order of 10^5 fit parameters', and the authors' model 'provides essentially the same predictive power at a fraction of the computational complexity (approximately 1000 fit parameters)'. Kob-Andersen and binary hard-sphere mixtures are both named in the abstract. Published as 'Averaging Local Structure to Predict the Dynamic Propensity in Supercooled Liquids', Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 088007 (20 August 2021), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.088007; arXiv URL resolves. The companion is also verified: R. M. Alkemade, E. Boattini, L. Filion, F. Smallenburg, 'Comparing machine learning techniques for predicting glassy dynamics', J. Chem. Phys. 156, 204503 (2022), DOI 10.1063/5.0088581, arXiv:2202.09173 — author order as the dossier gives it, and the finding (linear regression, neural networks and GNNs nearly equally accurate with advanced descriptors; linear regression orders of magnitude faster to train) is accurate.

verdicts.claim: Jung, Biroli and Berthier 2023, Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 238202 — GlassMLP beats the state of the art on 2D and 3D atomistic models with less data and fewer parameters; follow-up Phys. Rev. B 109, 064205 (2024). URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16623
verdicts.correction: Verified. 'Predicting Dynamic Heterogeneity in Glass-Forming Liquids by Physics-Inspired Machine Learning', Gerhard Jung, Giulio Biroli, Ludovic Berthier, Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 238202 (2023); PMID 37354408; arXiv:2210.16623 resolves. The abstract supports every element: physics-inspired structural input, application to atomistic models in 2D and 3D, outperforming the state of the art 'while being more parsimonious in terms of training data and fitting parameters', quantitative prediction of four-point dynamic correlations and the geometry of dynamic heterogeneity, and transferability across system sizes. The follow-up is also verified: G. Jung, G. Biroli, L. Berthier, 'Dynamic heterogeneity at the experimental glass transition predicted by transferable machine learning', Phys. Rev. B 109, 064205 (2024), arXiv:2310.20252. One caution: the 2023 abstract says 'outperforms the state of the art' generically; the explicit head-to-head with the DeepMind GNN is made in the body, not the abstract, so phrase it as 'including the GNN' only if you have checked the comparison table.

verdicts.claim: Swain, Ridout and Nemenman 2024, Phys. Rev. Research 6, 033091 — reading SVM distance-from-hyperplane as an activation energy is valid only under restricted conditions; Arrhenius behaviour and high cross-validation accuracy do not guarantee correct energy barriers. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00751
verdicts.correction: Verified, and this is the strongest-supported item in the dossier: every clause maps onto the abstract. Exact title (supply it, the dossier omits it): 'Machine learning that predicts well may not learn the correct physical descriptions of glassy systems', Arabind Swain, Sean Alexander Ridout, Ilya Nemenman, Phys. Rev. Research 6, 033091 (2024), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.033091; arXiv:2403.00751 resolves. The abstract states successful inference of the energy barrier from the hyperplane distance 'is possible only under very restricted conditions', and that 'typical tests, such as the apparent Arrhenius dependence... or high cross-validation accuracy do not guarantee success'. One scoping caution the book must keep: the analysis is of TOY MODELS ('by numerical analysis of toy models'), not of the original softness datasets, so do not write that the authors showed the softness construction itself failed — they showed the validation tests do not establish the physical reading. Affiliations (Emory) were not verified line-by-line; Nemenman is at Emory, but leave the field flagged.

verdicts.claim: Jung, Alkemade, Bapst, Coslovich, Filion, Landes, Liu, Pezzicoli, Shiba, Volpe, Zamponi, Berthier and Biroli 2025, Nature Reviews Physics 7, 91-104, 'Roadmap on machine learning glassy dynamics', introducing GlassBench. URL https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-024-00791-4
verdicts.correction: Verified. The 13-author list matches exactly in order (arXiv renders the seventh author as 'Andrea Liu'; the published form is Andrea J. Liu). Nature Reviews Physics 7(2), 91-104, published 6 January 2025, DOI 10.1038/s42254-024-00791-4; preprint arXiv:2311.14752 (2023); URL resolves; an author-hosted PDF is at https://ludovicberthier.github.io/divers/s42254-024-00791-4.pdf. The abstract confirms both the named open problems, 'transferability and interpretability of ML approaches', and the introduction of the 'GlassBench' dataset with simulation data and benchmarks for two- and three-dimensional glass formers. Caution on the affiliation string: the dossier's institution list is unmapped and at least one entry is doubtful — Hayato Shiba has published from Tohoku University as well as the University of Hyogo, so verify his listed affiliation against the article before printing it. The dossier already flags the mapping as unverified; keep it that way or drop the affiliations.

exact-machinery.domain: Mathematical machinery of phase transitions as singularities: Clausius-Clapeyron, Yang-Lee/Fisher partition-function zeros, finite-size scaling, the Ginzburg criterion, and the upper critical dimension of the Ising universality class
exact-machinery.summary:
Every bibliographic detail below was checked against a source I actually retrieved. DOIs for the twentieth- and twenty-first-century papers were confirmed one-by-one through the Crossref REST API (api.crossref.org/works/<doi>), which returned title, ordered author list, journal, volume, issue, pages and date verbatim; those items are marked "verified". Items marked "probable" are pre-DOI publications (Clapeyron 1834, Ginzburg 1960, Fisher's 1965 Boulder lectures) whose details I corroborated from a fetched secondary source but could not confirm against a scan of the original title page.

Four precision points the chapter must get right. (1) Author order flips between the two 1952 papers: Part I is C. N. Yang and T. D. Lee; Part II is T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang. Crossref confirms this directly. The lattice gas and the circle theorem are both in Part II (Phys. Rev. 87, 410-419); the general theorem that the free energy is analytic in any region of the complex fugacity plane free of zeros, so a transition occurs exactly where zeros pinch the positive real axis in the thermodynamic limit, is Part I (Phys. Rev. 87, 404-409). (2) Fisher zeros come from a lecture volume, not a journal: "The Nature of Critical Points", Lectures in Theoretical Physics Vol. 7c, ed. W. E. Brittin, University of Colorado Press, 1965, pp. 1-159 — no DOI exists, and the lectures were delivered at the 1964 Boulder Summer Institute and published in 1965. (3) The "Ginzburg criterion" was published first by A. P. Levanyuk (sole author, JETP 1959); Ginzburg's 1960 paper is the one the name attached to. Both should be cited; the Russian original is Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960), the English translation Sov. Phys. Solid State 2, 1824-1834, which several indexes date 1961 rather than 1960. (4) The upper critical dimension of the Ising universality class is d_c = 4. Above four dimensions mean-field exponents are exact and the scaling limit is Gaussian (Aizenman 1981, PRL 47, 1); exactly at d = 4 the triviality is only marginal, logarithmically slow, and was not proved until Aizenman and Duminil-Copin (Annals of Mathematics 2021). Wilson and Fisher's epsilon expansion is literally an expansion around that dimension — their title is "Critical Exponents in 3.99 Dimensions".

One naming caution: Crossref's record for Privman & Fisher 1984 prints the first author as "Valdimir Privman". That is a Crossref typographical error; the correct name is Vladimir Privman. Do not copy the Crossref spelling.

items.claim: Original memoir in which Clapeyron reformulated Carnot's argument analytically and derived the relation between the latent heat of a phase change and the slope of the coexistence curve — the ancestor of dp/dT = L/(T*Delta V). Published in the Journal de l'Ecole Royale Polytechnique, vingt-troisieme cahier, Tome XIV. No DOI exists; a facsimile is held by the Bibliotheque nationale de France (Gallica).
items.people: Benoit Paul Emile Clapeyron
items.affiliation: Ecole des Ponts et Chaussees / Ecole Polytechnique, Paris
items.venue: Memoire sur la puissance motrice de la chaleur, Journal de l'Ecole Royale Polytechnique, Tome XIV (23e cahier), pp. 153-190

items.claim: Clausius's founding paper of thermodynamics, in two parts, where the Carnot-Clapeyron relation is recast on the basis of the two laws and put into the modern form now called the Clausius-Clapeyron relation; Part II carries DOI 10.1002/andp.18501550403 (Ann. Phys. 155(4), 500-524). Crossref confirms both parts. Note the volume is Annalen der Physik 155 (also catalogued as vol. 79 of the old series).
items.people: Rudolf Clausius
items.affiliation: Royal Artillery and Engineering School, Berlin
items.venue: Annalen der Physik 155(3), 368-397 (Part I) and 155(4), 500-524 (Part II)

items.claim: Modern, citable, DOI-bearing pedagogical treatment of the Clausius-Clapeyron equation dp/dT = L/(T*Delta V), including the standard approximations (ideal-gas vapour, Delta V approximately equal to V_gas) and where they break down against measured saturation vapour pressure. Useful when the book needs a present-day reference rather than the 1850 original.
items.people: Demetris Koutsoyiannis
items.affiliation: National Technical University of Athens

items.claim: Standard graduate textbook source for the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and first-order coexistence within a statistical-mechanics course; the companion volume is Statistical Physics of Fields (DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511815881), which carries the Ginzburg criterion and the upper critical dimension. Cambridge assigns a DOI to the electronic edition, so this is citable with a DOI unlike Callen or Landau-Lifshitz.
items.people: Mehran Kardar
items.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
items.venue: Statistical Physics of Particles, Cambridge University Press (print ISBN 9780521873420)

items.claim: Part I of the Yang-Lee theory. Establishes that for a finite system the grand partition function is a polynomial in the fugacity z with no zeros on the positive real axis, hence the free energy is analytic and there is no singularity; that in the thermodynamic limit the zeros may migrate onto and pinch the positive real z axis; and that the free energy is analytic throughout any region of the complex z plane containing no zeros, so a phase transition occurs exactly at a pinch point. AUTHOR ORDER: Yang first, Lee second. Crossref confirms 'C. N. Yang, T. D. Lee'.
items.people: Chen Ning Yang, Tsung-Dao Lee
items.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton; Columbia University

items.claim: Part II of the Yang-Lee theory. Introduces the lattice gas and proves its exact equivalence to the Ising model in a magnetic field, and proves the Lee-Yang circle theorem: for a ferromagnetic Ising system all zeros of the partition function in the complex fugacity (equivalently complex magnetic-field) plane lie on the unit circle |z| = 1, i.e. at purely imaginary values of the field. AUTHOR ORDER IS REVERSED FROM PART I: Lee first, Yang second. Crossref confirms 'T. D. Lee, C. N. Yang'.
items.people: Tsung-Dao Lee, Chen Ning Yang
items.affiliation: Columbia University; Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton

items.claim: The standard modern generalisation of the Lee-Yang circle theorem, extending it well beyond the Ising case to one-component and multicomponent ferromagnets with quite general single-spin measures. This is the reference to cite when the book claims the circle theorem is not a peculiarity of the Ising model.
items.people: Elliott H. Lieb, Alan D. Sokal
items.affiliation: Princeton University; New York University (at time of publication)

items.claim: The best single review of the whole partition-function-zeros programme: Yang-Lee zeros in complex fugacity, Fisher zeros in complex temperature, the density of zeros and how its pinching angle encodes the order of the transition, and extensions to nonequilibrium steady states. Its Section 12 is where Fisher zeros are defined and Fisher's 1965 Boulder lectures are credited. Preprint arXiv:cond-mat/0510278 (2005); journal version same year.
items.people: Ioana Bena, Michel Droz, Adam Lipowski
items.affiliation: University of Geneva; Adam Mickiewicz University, Poznan
items.venue: International Journal of Modern Physics B 19, 4269-4329

items.claim: Fisher's Boulder lecture notes, the origin of what is now universally called the Fisher zeros: the proposal to study phase transitions via the zeros of the CANONICAL partition function in the plane of complex TEMPERATURE, complementing Yang and Lee's zeros in complex fugacity. In a finite system these zeros lie off the positive real temperature axis; they close in on it in the thermodynamic limit. There is no DOI and no journal version. Cite as: M. E. Fisher, 'The Nature of Critical Points', in Lectures in Theoretical Physics, Vol. 7c: Statistical Physics, Weak Interactions, Field Theory, ed. W. E. Brittin (University of Colorado Press, Boulder, 1965), pp. 1-159. Lectures were delivered at the 1964 Boulder Summer Institute for Theoretical Physics; the volume appeared in 1965.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: The Rockefeller Institute, New York (as printed on the lectures)
items.venue: Lectures in Theoretical Physics, Vol. 7c, ed. W. E. Brittin, University of Colorado Press, Boulder, pp. 1-159

items.claim: Identifies the Yang-Lee edge — the endpoint of the arc of zeros on the unit circle above T_c — as a genuine critical point in its own right, with its own exponent sigma, and shows it is governed by a non-unitary i*phi-cubed field theory with upper critical dimension 6. The result that turns 'zeros on a circle' from a curiosity into a universality class.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: Direct experimental observation of Lee-Yang zeros, obtained by measuring the quantum coherence of a probe spin coupled to an Ising-type bath in an NMR system, which encodes the partition function at complex magnetic field. Cite this if the book wants to answer the objection that complex-field zeros are a purely formal device.
items.people: Xinhua Peng, Hui Zhou, Bo-Bo Wei, Jiangyu Cui, Jiangfeng Du, Ren-Bao Liu
items.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei; Chinese University of Hong Kong

items.claim: The first statement of the finite-size scaling idea: at a critical point the singular behaviour of a bounded system is rounded and shifted, and both the shift and the rounding are controlled by the ratio of the correlation length to the system size. The precursor to the 1972 Fisher-Barber paper.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher, Arthur E. Ferdinand
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: Exact solution for the specific heat of a FINITE two-dimensional Ising lattice (n by m, torus and other boundary conditions). This is the concrete demonstration that a finite Ising system has no singularity at all — the specific heat is a smooth, bounded, analytic function of temperature whose peak grows only as log(L) and sits at a shifted pseudo-critical temperature. The exact worked example a graduate reader can check against their own simulation.
items.people: Arthur E. Ferdinand, Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: THE canonical finite-size scaling citation. States the scaling theory with distinct exponents lambda for the critical-point shift and theta = 1/nu for the rounding, so that the width of the rounded region scales as L^(-1/nu) and the peak height as a power of L; verified against exact results for d-dimensional spherical models and ideal Bose fluids with various boundary conditions, and checked against Ising data and helium-film experiments. This is the standard citable statement that a finite system has no true singularity and that the rounding scales as a power of the system size. The book-length companion statement is M. N. Barber, 'Finite-size scaling', in Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena, Vol. 8, ed. C. Domb and J. L. Lebowitz (Academic Press, London, 1983), pp. 145-266 — no DOI located for that chapter.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher, Michael N. Barber
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: Introduces the fourth-order cumulant of the order-parameter block distribution — the Binder cumulant — whose curves for different L cross at T_c, giving the workhorse numerical method for locating a critical point from finite lattices without knowing the exponents in advance. Directly usable in an Ising-simulation chapter.
items.people: Kurt Binder
items.affiliation: Institut fuer Festkoerperforschung, Kernforschungsanlage Juelich
items.venue: Zeitschrift fuer Physik B Condensed Matter 43(2), 119-140

items.claim: Establishes that finite-size scaling functions and their amplitudes are themselves universal, given a fixed shape, boundary conditions and aspect ratio — the result that licenses quantitative collapse of data from different lattice sizes onto one curve. NOTE: Crossref misprints the first author as 'Valdimir Privman'; the correct spelling is Vladimir Privman.
items.people: Vladimir Privman, Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: Priority note for the Ginzburg criterion. Levanyuk, as sole author and a year before Ginzburg, gave the fluctuation-magnitude estimate that bounds the validity of Landau theory near a second-order transition, in the context of critical opalescence and light scattering. Because of this the criterion is more accurately called the Levanyuk-Ginzburg criterion. English translation Sov. Phys. JETP 9(3), 571 (September 1959); Russian original ZhETF 36(3), 810 (1959); received 8 July 1958. No DOI; the JETP archive hosts the scan at the URL given.
items.people: Anatoly P. Levanyuk
items.affiliation: USSR Academy of Sciences

items.claim: The Ginzburg criterion. States the self-consistency condition for mean-field (Landau) theory: the theory is valid only where fluctuations of the order parameter within a correlation volume are small compared with the order parameter itself. This bounds the reduced temperature outside which mean-field exponents hold and inside which they must fail, with the width of the critical (Ginzburg) region scaling as the inverse sixth power of the interaction range — which is why the region is unobservably narrow in conventional superconductors and ferroelectrics but wide in short-range magnets. Russian original: Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960). English translation: 'Some remarks on phase transitions of the second kind and the microscopic theory of ferroelectric materials', Sov. Phys. Solid State 2(9), 1824-1834; indexes disagree on whether the translation is dated 1960 or 1961. No DOI.
items.people: Vitaly Lazarevich Ginzburg
items.affiliation: P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute, Moscow
items.venue: Fizika Tverdogo Tela 2, 2031 (1960) [Soviet Physics Solid State 2(9), 1824-1834]

items.claim: The standard English-language pedagogical statement of the Ginzburg criterion, with the criterion derived explicitly and used to define the marginal (upper critical) dimensionality at which mean-field theory becomes self-consistent — namely d = 4 for short-range systems with a scalar order parameter. The most quotable single source for 'when is mean-field theory allowed to be right'.
items.people: Jens Als-Nielsen, Robert J. Birgeneau
items.affiliation: Risoe National Laboratory, Denmark; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

items.claim: The epsilon expansion. Computes critical exponents as a systematic series in epsilon = 4 - d, i.e. by perturbing around the upper critical dimension of the Ising universality class. The title itself ('Critical Exponents in 3.99 Dimensions') is the cleanest possible signal that d = 4 is the dimension where mean-field behaviour turns on.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson, Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: Rigorous proof that for d > 4 the continuum limit of the phi-fourth field theory is trivial (free/Gaussian) and that Ising models in more than four dimensions exhibit mean-field critical behaviour. This is the theorem behind the statement 'the upper critical dimension of the Ising universality class is 4'. The independent contemporaneous proof is J. Froehlich, Nuclear Physics B 200(2), 281-296 (1982), DOI 10.1016/0550-3213(82)90088-8.
items.people: Michael Aizenman
items.affiliation: Princeton University

items.claim: Closes the marginal case left open for forty years: proves that in exactly d = 4 the scaling limit of the critical Ising and lambda-phi-fourth models is also Gaussian, though the approach is only logarithmically slow. This is the precise sense in which d = 4 is the upper critical dimension rather than merely a boundary. Preprint arXiv:1912.07973 (2019); journal publication 2021.
items.people: Michael Aizenman, Hugo Duminil-Copin
items.affiliation: Princeton University; IHES and University of Geneva

openQuestions: Clapeyron 1834: I confirmed the citation (Journal de l'Ecole Royale Polytechnique, Tome XIV, 23e cahier, pp. 153-190) from multiple search results and a Gallica catalogue entry, but neither the Gallica facsimile nor the Notre Dame scan (https://academicweb.nd.edu/~powers/ame.20231/clapeyron1834.pdf, which does exist and downloaded as a 1.3 MB PDF) could be converted to readable text by my fetch tool. Someone should eyeball the title page before the citation goes to press. Note also that Clapeyron did NOT write it as dp/dT = L/(T*Delta V); that form is due to Clausius. If the book attributes the modern equation to Clapeyron alone it will be wrong.

Ginzburg 1960 translation year: the Russian original is Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960), but the English translation Sov. Phys. Solid State 2(9), 1824-1834 is dated 1961 by the ISI/HistCite record I fetched and 1960 by most physics bibliographies. Pick one convention and state both, e.g. 'Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960) [Sov. Phys. Solid State 2, 1824 (1960)]'. No DOI exists for either version; I could not fetch a scan of the original.

M. N. Barber, 'Finite-size scaling', Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena Vol. 8 (Domb and Lebowitz, eds., Academic Press, 1983), pp. 145-266 is the review a graduate reader should be sent to, and the page range is corroborated across several independent citing papers, but I found no DOI and no URL I could fetch for the chapter itself. I therefore folded it into the Fisher-Barber entry rather than listing it as a separately verified item. Worth a library check for the ISBN.

Fisher's 1965 Boulder lectures: I verified the citation form (Vol. 7c, ed. W. E. Brittin, University of Colorado Press, 1965, pp. 1-159) from a fetched bibliography (Dagstuhl LIPIcs.ITCS.2019.55) and the volume title from Google Books, which records the lectures as delivered at the 1964 Boulder Summer Institute. A scanned PDF is hosted at https://personal.rhul.ac.uk/UHAP/027/PH4211/PH4211_files/Fisher-1965.pdf but that host refused my connection, so I have not read the original. Be aware that some papers cite it as 'Vol. VIIC' and some as 'Lecture notes in Theoretical Physics'; both refer to the same volume.

Terminology to fix early in the chapter: 'Yang-Lee zeros' (complex fugacity or complex magnetic field) versus 'Fisher zeros' (complex temperature) are different objects, and the literature also uses 'Lee-Yang zeros' interchangeably with 'Yang-Lee zeros'. The circle theorem is specifically about the former. Bena, Droz and Lipowski (2005) is the reference that keeps them straight.

Not researched here, but adjacent and probably needed if the book quantifies the 3D Ising upper-critical-dimension story: modern conformal-bootstrap determinations of the 3D Ising exponents (Kos, Poland, Simmons-Duffin, Vichi and successors) would give the reader the numbers that mean-field theory fails to reproduce below d = 4. Ask if you want those verified too.

Also not researched: whether the book wants the rigorous first-order-transition analogue of finite-size scaling (Borgs-Kotecky) and the partition-function-zeros analysis at first-order points (Biskup, Borgs, Chayes, Kleinwaks, Kotecky, Comm. Math. Phys. 2004). Both surfaced in searches and would be the right citations if the chapter treats first-order as well as continuous transitions.

verdicts.claim: Clapeyron, 'Memoire sur la puissance motrice de la chaleur', Journal de l'Ecole Royale Polytechnique, Tome XIV (23e cahier), pp. 153-190 (1834); Gallica facsimile at ark:/12148/bpt6k3414331n. Affiliation given as 'Ecole des Ponts et Chaussees / Ecole Polytechnique, Paris'.
verdicts.correction: Citation and page range CONFIRMED: the BnF catalogue record cb40936143n (the record behind the Gallica ark in the dossier URL) describes 'Mémoire sur la puissance motrice de la chaleur' by Clapeyron as a facsimile of an extract from the Journal de l'École polytechnique (1834), 1 vol. (pp. 153-190) — matching Tome XIV, 23e cahier. Two corrections. (1) AFFILIATION IS ANACHRONISTIC: per MacTutor and concurring biographies, Clapeyron graduated from the École Polytechnique in 1818, trained at the École des Mines, spent 1820-1830 in Russia, and in 1834 was a railway engineer in Paris; he was appointed professor at the École des Ponts et Chaussées only in 1844. Do not print 'École des Ponts et Chaussées' as his 1834 affiliation. (2) Gallica itself returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, and the digitised object is the 2006 Jacques Gabay facsimile reprint (ISBN 978-2-87647-283-9), not a scan of the original 1834 printing — accurate to describe as 'facsimile', but nobody in this chain has read the original title page, so the exact journal title form ('Journal de l'École Royale Polytechnique' vs 'de l'École polytechnique') remains unverified. The dossier's own warning stands: the modern form dp/dT = L/(T·ΔV) is Clausius's, not Clapeyron's.

verdicts.claim: Clausius 1850, 'Ueber die bewegende Kraft der Waerme...', Annalen der Physik 155(3) 368-397 (Part I, DOI 10.1002/andp.18501550306) and 155(4) 500-524 (Part II, DOI 10.1002/andp.18501550403); affiliation Royal Artillery and Engineering School, Berlin.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns for 10.1002/andp.18501550306: R. Clausius, 'Ueber die bewegende Kraft der Wärme und die Gesetze, welche sich daraus für die Wärmelehre selbst ableiten lassen', Annalen der Physik 155(3), 368-397, 1850. For 10.1002/andp.18501550403: same title, 155(4), 500-524, 1850. Both parts, volume, issue, pages and year exactly as stated; the dossier URL resolves to Part I. Clausius's 1850 appointment to the Royal Artillery and Engineering School in Berlin is standard biography and not contradicted by anything I found.

verdicts.claim: Koutsoyiannis 2012, 'Clausius-Clapeyron equation and saturation vapour pressure: simple theory reconciled with practice', European Journal of Physics 33(2), 295-305, DOI 10.1088/0143-0807/33/2/295.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns exactly: Demetris Koutsoyiannis (sole author), that title, European Journal of Physics 33(2), 295-305, published 10 January 2012. Title itself supports the dossier's topical claim (the equation plus the practical approximations and where they break down). Affiliation NTUA is the author's standing affiliation.

verdicts.claim: Kardar 2007, Statistical Physics of Particles, CUP, DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511815898 — described as the 'standard graduate textbook source for the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and first-order coexistence'; companion Statistical Physics of Fields DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511815881 carries the Ginzburg criterion and upper critical dimension.
verdicts.correction: Bibliographic half is CONFIRMED: Crossref gives 10.1017/CBO9780511815898 = Mehran Kardar, 'Statistical Physics of Particles', Cambridge University Press, monograph, 2007, print ISBN 9780521873420 / electronic 9780511815898; and 10.1017/CBO9780511815881 = 'Statistical Physics of Fields', CUP 2007, print ISBN 9780521873413. TOPICAL CLAIM NOT VERIFIED: I could not confirm that 'Statistical Physics of Particles' actually treats the Clausius-Clapeyron relation. The Cambridge index PDF and the book's full table of contents were unreachable (assets.cambridge.org refused the connection; the Cambridge Higher Education page does not print the TOC), and targeted searches surfaced no Clausius-Clapeyron section or index entry — the book's phase-coexistence material is the van der Waals / Maxwell-construction treatment in the interacting-particles chapter. Check the index before citing Kardar for Clausius-Clapeyron specifically; Callen or Reichl is the conventional textbook home for it. The 'Fields' half of the claim (Ginzburg criterion, upper critical dimension d=4 in the Landau-Ginzburg chapter) is well corroborated.

verdicts.claim: Yang & Lee 1952 Part I, 'Statistical Theory of Equations of State and Phase Transitions. I. Theory of Condensation', Phys. Rev. 87(3), 404-409, author order Yang then Lee; affiliations 'Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton; Columbia University'.
verdicts.correction: Bibliography CONFIRMED by Crossref: 'C. N. Yang, T. D. Lee' in that order, Physical Review 87(3), 404-409, 1 August 1952; DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.87.404 resolves to it. The physics claim (finite-system polynomial with no positive-real zeros, analyticity in any zero-free region of the complex fugacity plane, transition at a pinch point) is a correct description of Part I. AFFILIATION IS WRONG: both papers carry a single affiliation, 'Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey', for both authors. T. D. Lee was at the Institute for Advanced Study 1951-1953 and did not join Columbia until 1953, so 'Columbia University' must not be printed against either 1952 paper.

verdicts.claim: Lee & Yang 1952 Part II, 'Statistical Theory of Equations of State and Phase Transitions. II. Lattice Gas and Ising Model', Phys. Rev. 87(3), 410-419, author order REVERSED (Lee then Yang); affiliations 'Columbia University; Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton'.
verdicts.correction: The load-bearing detail is CONFIRMED: Crossref returns 'T. D. Lee, C. N. Yang' in that order for 10.1103/PhysRev.87.410, Physical Review 87(3), 410-419, 1 August 1952 — the author-order flip between Parts I and II is real and correctly flagged. Lattice-gas/Ising equivalence and the circle theorem are indeed Part II. Same affiliation error as Part I: the printed affiliation is 'Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey' for both authors; Lee was not yet at Columbia in August 1952.

verdicts.claim: Lieb & Sokal 1981, 'A general Lee-Yang theorem for one-component and multicomponent ferromagnets', Comm. Math. Phys. 80(2), 153-179, DOI 10.1007/BF01213009; affiliations 'Princeton University; New York University (at time of publication)'.
