verdicts.correction: Bibliography CONFIRMED twice over: Crossref gives Elliott H. Lieb, Alan D. Sokal, Communications in Mathematical Physics 80(2), 153-179, June 1981. AFFILIATION IS WRONG: I extracted the first page of the published PDF (Project Euclid cmp/1103919874), which prints '1 Departments of Mathematics and Physics, Princeton University, Princeton, NJ 08544, USA' and '2 Department of Physics, Princeton University, Princeton, NJ 08544, USA'. Sokal was at PRINCETON, not NYU, at time of publication. The paper's own abstract also supports the dossier's topical claim ('any measure on R^n possessing the Lee-Yang property retains that property when multiplied by a ferromagnetic pair interaction'; Newman's theorem as a corollary; two-component result; anisotropic N>=3 result) — note the N>=3 result is conditional on sufficient anisotropy, so 'quite general single-spin measures' should be scoped to the one- and two-component cases.

verdicts.claim: Bena, Droz & Lipowski 2005, 'Statistical Mechanics of Equilibrium and Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions: The Yang-Lee Formalism', Int. J. Mod. Phys. B 19, 4269-4329, DOI 10.1142/S0217979205032759, arXiv cond-mat/0510278; its Section 12 defines Fisher zeros and credits Fisher's 1965 Boulder lectures.
verdicts.correction: Crossref: Ioana Bena, Michel Droz, Adam Lipowski, IJMPB 19(29), 4269-4329, 20 November 2005. arXiv cond-mat/0510278 submitted 11 October 2005 with matching journal-ref. I read the full text: affiliations are Theoretical Physics Department, University of Geneva (Bena, Droz) and Quantum Physics Division, Faculty of Physics, A. Mickiewicz University, Poznan (Lipowski) — exactly as the dossier states. Section 12 is titled 'Fisher zeros of the canonical partition function' and opens 'In a review article of 1965, Ref. 4, Fisher suggested the analysis of the phase transitions in the frame of the canonical ensemble...'; its Ref. 4 is the Boulder volume. The review's own reference 133 is the Barber 'Finite-size Scaling' chapter in the Domb-Lebowitz Vol. 8, corroborating that citation form.

verdicts.claim: Fisher 1965, 'The Nature of Critical Points', in Lectures in Theoretical Physics Vol. 7c: Statistical Physics, Weak Interactions, Field Theory, ed. W. E. Brittin, University of Colorado Press, Boulder, pp. 1-159; lectures delivered at the 1964 Boulder Summer Institute; affiliation as printed 'The Rockefeller Institute, New York'; no DOI.
verdicts.correction: Volume CONFIRMED from the Google Books record in the dossier URL: 'Lectures in Theoretical Physics Vol. 7c: Statistical Physics, Weak Interactions, Field Theory / Lectures Delivered at the Summer Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of Colorado, Boulder, 1964', ed. Wesley E. Brittin, 1965, 488 pp. — so 1964 delivery / 1965 publication is right. Citation form independently CONFIRMED from the Bena-Droz-Lipowski reference list, which reads: 'M. E. Fisher, in Lectures in Theoretical Physics. Vol. VIIC - Statistical Physics, Weak Interactions, Field Theory, ed. W. E. Brittin (Univ. Colorado Press, Boulder, 1965). The nature of critical points'. Affiliation CONFIRMED: the scanned offprint at personal.rhul.ac.uk carries the header 'THE NATURE OF CRITICAL POINTS* Michael E. Fisher† The Rockefeller Institute' (the host still refuses direct connections; this is the indexed first line). Two cautions for press: Fisher was a guest investigator at the Rockefeller Institute on leave from King's College London, where he was on the faculty until moving to Cornell in 1966 — so the Rockefeller line is the printed affiliation, not his home institution; and 'pp. 1-159' is corroborated only by citing papers, not by any copy I opened, and it is absent from Fisher's own publication list as reprinted in the 2024 Aharony-Barma CV (arXiv:2410.07235), so treat the page range as good-faith secondary evidence.

verdicts.claim: Fisher 1978, 'Yang-Lee Edge Singularity and phi-cubed Field Theory', Phys. Rev. Lett. 40(25), 1610-1613, 19 June 1978; identifies the Yang-Lee edge as a critical point with exponent sigma governed by a non-unitary i*phi^3 theory with upper critical dimension 6.
verdicts.correction: Crossref: Michael E. Fisher (sole author), 'Yang-Lee Edge Singularity and φ³ Field Theory', Physical Review Letters 40(25), 1610-1613, 19 June 1978; DOI resolves. Independently corroborated by the Fisher CV, which describes the paper as discovering 'the field theory for the Yang-Lee edge singularity, with the associated expansion in ε = 6 - d dimensions' — i.e. upper critical dimension 6, exactly as claimed. Cornell affiliation is correct for 1978.

verdicts.claim: Peng, Zhou, Wei, Cui, Du & Liu 2015, 'Experimental Observation of Lee-Yang Zeros', Phys. Rev. Lett. 114(1), 010601, 5 January 2015.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns the six authors in exactly the stated order — Xinhua Peng, Hui Zhou, Bo-Bo Wei, Jiangyu Cui, Jiangfeng Du, Ren-Bao Liu — with article number 010601, PRL 114(1), 5 January 2015. Title and DOI match; the NMR probe-spin/quantum-coherence description is the paper's actual method.

verdicts.claim: Fisher & Ferdinand 1967, Phys. Rev. Lett. 19(4), 169-172 — 'the first statement of the finite-size scaling idea', rounding and shift controlled by the ratio of correlation length to system size.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms authors, order, journal, volume, issue, pages and date (24 July 1967) — but note the TITLE, which the dossier omits, is 'Interfacial, Boundary, and Size Effects at Critical Points'. One caution on the wording: Fisher's own CV credits the scaling theory for shift and rounding to the later 1971-72 papers and lists the 1967 work as the start of his boundary/finite-size effort, so 'first statement of the finite-size scaling idea' is best softened to 'the paper that opened the subject' rather than a claim of the full scaling statement.

verdicts.claim: Ferdinand & Fisher 1969, 'Bounded and Inhomogeneous Ising Models. I. Specific-Heat Anomaly of a Finite Lattice', Phys. Rev. 185(2), 832-846, 10 September 1969 — exact finite n x m Ising specific heat, smooth and bounded, peak growing as log(L) at a shifted pseudo-critical temperature.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns that exact title with author order 'Arthur E. Ferdinand, Michael E. Fisher' (note the order is reversed relative to the 1967 letter — a second author-order flip in this dossier, correctly recorded), Physical Review 185(2), 832-846, 10 September 1969. The log(L) peak growth and shifted pseudo-critical temperature are standard consequences of that exact solution.

verdicts.claim: Fisher & Barber 1972, 'Scaling Theory for Finite-Size Effects in the Critical Region', Phys. Rev. Lett. 28(23), 1516-1519, 5 June 1972 — shift exponent lambda and rounding exponent theta = 1/nu, verified on spherical models and ideal Bose fluids. Companion: M. N. Barber, 'Finite-size scaling', in Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena Vol. 8, eds. Domb & Lebowitz, Academic Press, 1983, pp. 145-266.
verdicts.correction: Crossref: Michael E. Fisher, Michael N. Barber, that exact title, PRL 28(23), 1516-1519, 5 June 1972. The Barber chapter citation is corroborated independently by the Bena-Droz-Lipowski reference list (Domb and Lebowitz, Academic Press, New York, 1983, 'Finite-size Scaling'); as the dossier says, no DOI exists for the chapter and the pp. 145-266 range rests on citing papers rather than a copy anyone opened.

verdicts.claim: Binder 1981, 'Finite size scaling analysis of Ising model block distribution functions', Z. Phys. B Condensed Matter 43(2), 119-140, DOI 10.1007/BF01293604 — introduces the fourth-order (Binder) cumulant whose curves cross at T_c.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns exactly that title, sole author K. Binder, Zeitschrift für Physik B Condensed Matter 43(2), 119-140, June 1981; Semantic Scholar agrees on DOI, year and sole authorship. Springer's own article page is paywalled behind an auth redirect so I could not read the printed affiliation line, but 'Institut für Festkörperforschung, KFA Jülich' is consistent with Binder's documented 1977-1983 position and nothing contradicted it.

verdicts.claim: Privman & Fisher 1984, 'Universal critical amplitudes in finite-size scaling', Phys. Rev. B 30(1), 322-327, 1 July 1984 — and Crossref misprints the first author as 'Valdimir Privman'; correct spelling Vladimir.
verdicts.correction: Verified including the warning: Crossref for 10.1103/PhysRevB.30.322 returns 'Valdimir Privman, Michael E. Fisher', 'Universal critical amplitudes in finite-size scaling', Physical Review B 30(1), 322-327, 1 July 1984. The 'Valdimir' typo is real and is Crossref's, not the journal's — print Vladimir Privman. Fisher's CV independently describes this collaboration as establishing 'a full finite-size scaling theory for a variety of sample shapes, including the identification of universal critical amplitudes', supporting the topical claim.

verdicts.claim: Levanyuk 1959 priority note: sole author, Sov. Phys. JETP 9(3), 571 [ZhETF 36(3), 810], received 8 July 1958, hosted at jetp.ras.ru; gave the fluctuation estimate bounding Landau theory a year before Ginzburg, in a light-scattering context.
verdicts.correction: The dossier URL resolves and returns: A. P. Levanyuk (sole author), 'Contribution to the Theory of Light Scattering near the Second-Order Phase-Transition Points', JETP 9(3), 571 (September 1959); Russian original ZhETF 36(3), 810 (1959); received 8 July 1958. Every element — sole authorship, volume, issue, page, both dates, the light-scattering framing — matches. The 'Levanyuk-Ginzburg criterion' naming point is well supported by the priority.

verdicts.claim: Ginzburg 1960, 'Some remarks on phase transitions of the second kind and the microscopic theory of ferroelectric materials', Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960) [Sov. Phys. Solid State 2(9), 1824-1834]; no DOI; Ginzburg region width scaling as the inverse sixth power of the interaction range.
verdicts.correction: Substance CONFIRMED, one date to fix. The dossier's own cited URL (the ISI/HistCite record at garfield.library.upenn.edu) returns verbatim: 'GINZBURG VL / SOME REMARKS ON PHASE TRANSITIONS OF THE 2ND KIND AND THE MICROSCOPIC THEORY OF FERROELECTRIC MATERIALS / SOVIET PHYSICS-SOLID STATE 2 (9): 1824-1834 / Date 1961'. So the source the dossier cites dates the TRANSLATION 1961, not 1960. The dominant convention in the physics literature — including Ginzburg's own Nobel lecture bibliography — is 'Fiz. Tverd. Tela 2, 2031 (1960) [Sov. Phys. Solid State 2, 1824 (1961)]'. Print it that way: Russian original 1960, English translation 1961. No DOI exists for either version and I could not obtain a scan of either, so the Russian page number 2031 rests on citation consensus. The physics (Gi ~ (a/r0)^6 in three dimensions, hence unobservably narrow in conventional superconductors, wide in short-range magnets) is standard and correctly stated.

verdicts.claim: Als-Nielsen & Birgeneau 1977, 'Mean field theory, the Ginzburg criterion, and marginal dimensionality of phase transitions', Am. J. Phys. 45(6), 554-560, DOI 10.1119/1.11019.
verdicts.correction: Crossref returns exactly that title with authors 'J. Als-Nielsen, R. J. Birgeneau' in that order, American Journal of Physics 45(6), 554-560, 1 June 1977. The title itself carries the dossier's topical claim (criterion plus marginal/upper critical dimensionality); Risø and MIT are the authors' 1977 institutions.

verdicts.claim: Wilson & Fisher 1972, 'Critical Exponents in 3.99 Dimensions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 28(4), 240-243, 24 January 1972 — the epsilon expansion around the upper critical dimension.
verdicts.correction: Crossref: 'Kenneth G. Wilson, Michael E. Fisher' in that order, that exact title, PRL 28(4), 240-243, 24 January 1972. Both at Cornell. Fisher's CV independently describes it as the paper in which 'ε = 4 - d, the deviation from four dimensions, becomes an expansion parameter', confirming the dossier's reading of the title.

verdicts.claim: Aizenman 1981, Phys. Rev. Lett. 47(1), 1-4 — triviality of phi^4 and mean-field Ising behaviour for d > 4; independent contemporaneous proof Froehlich, Nucl. Phys. B 200(2), 281-296 (1982), DOI 10.1016/0550-3213(82)90088-8.
verdicts.correction: Crossref for 10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.1: Michael Aizenman (sole author), 'Proof of the Triviality of φ⁴ Field Theory and Some Mean-Field Features of Ising Models for d > 4', PRL 47(1), 1-4, 6 July 1981 — the 'd > 4' is in the title, so the claim does not overstate it. The Fröhlich companion also checks out: Crossref for 10.1016/0550-3213(82)90088-8 returns Jürg Fröhlich, 'On the triviality of λΦ⁴ theories and the approach to the critical point in d ≥ 4 dimensions', Nuclear Physics B 200(2), 281-296, February 1982 — note Fröhlich's title says d ≥ 4 (Crossref renders the sign oddly as 'd(−) > 4'), slightly broader than the dossier's 'independent contemporaneous proof' framing suggests.

verdicts.claim: Aizenman & Duminil-Copin 2021, marginal triviality in exactly d = 4, Annals of Mathematics 194(1), article 3, DOI 10.4007/annals.2021.194.1.3; preprint arXiv:1912.07973 (2019).
verdicts.correction: Crossref: Michael Aizenman, Hugo Duminil-Copin, 'Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and λφ⁴₄ models', Annals of Mathematics 194(1), 1 July 2021. arXiv:1912.07973 submitted 17 December 2019 (v4 June 2021) with journal-ref 'Annals of Mathematics, July 2021, Vol. 194, No. 1, pp. 163-223' and the same DOI. If the book wants page numbers, use 163-223; Crossref carries no page data for this record. The 'logarithmically slow' characterisation matches the abstract's Gaussian scaling limit with logarithmic correction factors.

nucleation-exact.domain: Nucleation and metastability — classical nucleation theory, the capillarity barrier, deep supercooling of liquid metals, Ostwald's step rule, spinodal decomposition and the Cahn–Hilliard/Allen–Cahn equations, and the empirical failure of CNT rate predictions
nucleation-exact.summary: All bibliographic details below were checked against publisher metadata (Crossref/De Gruyter/Wiley/AIP/IOP/ACS/Nature) or the article text itself; every URL is one I actually loaded. Three corrections to commonly repeated errors are worth flagging for the chapter. (1) Volmer's coauthor is A. Weber and the paper is Z. Phys. Chem. 119U, 277–301 (1926) — the "Weber, A.Z." form circulating in reference lists is a citation-database artifact, not an author. (2) Becker & Döring 1935 is Annalen der Physik vol. 416 in continuous numbering, which is Band 24 of the 5. Folge; both "Ann. Phys. 416, 719" and "Ann. Phys. 24, 719" appear in the literature and refer to the same paper. (3) Turnbull's mercury droplets supercooled 58 K below the 234.3 K melting point in the Table I compilation of the 1950 J. Appl. Phys. paper (measurable nucleation over 59–63 K of supercooling in the follow-up experiments) — not the ~77 K figure that is sometimes quoted. The deepest supercooling in that table is platinum at 370 K; the famous regularity is (ΔT)max/T0 ≈ 0.18, ranging 0.133 (lead) to 0.250 (gallium). For the barrier itself, I verified an equation-level source (Clouet's ASM Handbook chapter, open on arXiv) rather than relying on memory: his Eqs. (5) and (6) give n* and ΔG* in cluster-size form, which reduce exactly to r* = 2γ/|Δg_v| and ΔG* = 16πγ³/(3Δg_v²) for a spherical cluster. For the "CNT is wrong by many orders of magnitude" claim the cleanest quantified citation is argon condensation (CNT low by 11–13 orders of magnitude); the hard-sphere colloid discrepancy (>10 orders at low supersaturation) is the second canonical example.

items.claim: Founding paper of classical nucleation theory: nucleus formation in supersaturated systems, introducing the capillarity/critical-nucleus argument that a droplet must exceed a critical size before it grows. Title translates as 'Nucleation in supersaturated structures'; commonly cited in English as 'Nucleus formation in supersaturated systems'. Z. Phys. Chem. volume is 119U (the 'U' denotes De Gruyter's retro-digitized series), issue 1, pages 277-301.
items.people: M. Volmer; A. Weber
items.affiliation: Volmer: Institute of Physical Chemistry, Technische Hochschule Berlin (Weber's affiliation not stated in the metadata I could access)

items.claim: First kinetic (rate) treatment of nucleation in supersaturated vapours, predating and feeding into Becker-Döring. 'Keimbildungsgeschwindigkeit in übersättigten Dämpfen', Z. Phys. Chem. 125U(1), 236-242. Useful if the chapter wants to show that the kinetic prefactor problem was posed before 1935.
items.people: L. Farkas
items.affiliation: Not verified from the source I could access

items.claim: The kinetic theory of nucleation: the cluster-population master equation and steady-state flux over the barrier that yields the Becker-Döring nucleation rate, J = A exp(-ΔG*/kT). CAUTION on the volume number: Annalen der Physik continuous vol. 416 = Band 24 of the 5. Folge, so 'Ann. Phys. 24, 719 (1935)' and 'Ann. Phys. 416, 719 (1935)' are the same paper. Issue 8, pages 719-752.
items.people: R. Becker; W. Döring
items.affiliation: Becker held the theoretical physics chair at Technische Hochschule Berlin and moved to Göttingen in the mid-1930s; Döring was his doctoral student. The paper's masthead affiliation was NOT verifiable (Wiley returned 403), so do not state an institution as fact.

items.claim: Transposes the vapour-condensation rate theory to condensed systems, using absolute-reaction-rate theory to supply the kinetic prefactor: I = A exp[-Kσ³/((ΔF_V)²kT)] with A = n(kT/h)exp(-ΔF_A/kT), where ΔF_A is the activation free energy for transporting an atom across the liquid-crystal interface. This is the paper that made nucleation theory usable for solidification. J. Chem. Phys. 17(1), 71-73. Note an errata was published at J. Chem. Phys. 17(4), 429 (1949) — see https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article/17/4/429/200784/Errata-Rate-of-Nucleation-in-Condensed-Systems .
items.people: David Turnbull; John C. Fisher
items.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: The droplet experiment itself: microscopic observation of the solidification of small metal droplets. Dispersing a melt into many tiny non-communicating droplets means most droplets contain no catalytic impurity, so homogeneous nucleation becomes observable. This is the experimental companion Turnbull cites (as ref. 2) for the supercooling data tabulated in his 1950 J. Appl. Phys. paper. J. Appl. Phys. 21(8), 804-810.
items.people: David Turnbull; R. E. Cech
items.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: THE supercooling paper — I read the reprint text and Table I directly. Maximum supercooling (ΔT_-)max in kelvin, with T0 in kelvin and the ratio (ΔT_-)max/T0: mercury 234.3 K / 58 K / 0.247; gallium 303 / 76 / 0.250; tin 505.7 / 105 / 0.208; bismuth 544 / 90 / 0.166; lead 600.7 / 80 / 0.133; antimony 903 / 135 / 0.150; aluminium 931.7 / 130 / 0.140; germanium 1231.7 / 227 / 0.184; silver 1233.7 / 227 / 0.184; gold 1336 / 230 / 0.172; copper 1356 / 236 / 0.174; manganese 1493 / 308 / 0.206; nickel 1725 / 319 / 0.185; cobalt 1763 / 330 / 0.187; iron 1803 / 295 / 0.164; palladium 1828 / 332 / 0.182; platinum 2043 / 370 / 0.181; water 273.2 / 39 / 0.143. Text states: 'For most metals (ΔT_-)max is of the order of 0.18 times the absolute melting temperature, T0', reproducible to ±5 percent, and later '≈0.185 with maximum deviations of ±0.02 ... the ratio ranges from 0.133 for lead to 0.250 for gallium.' Nucleation was measurable only over narrow bands: 59-63 degrees of supercooling for mercury, 100-115 for tin; fitted prefactors A = 10^30.4 (tin) and 10^30.9 (mercury) per cm³ per s, against 10^33 expected for homogeneous nucleation and 10^25 for surface-catalysed. 4-micron mercury droplets solidify at ~10^-5 s^-1 at ΔT = 60 K. Table II gives derived crystal-melt interfacial energies in erg/cm²: mercury 24.4, water 32.1, gallium 55.9, tin 54.5, bismuth 54.4, lead 33.3, antimony 101, aluminium 93, germanium 181, silver 126, gold 132, copper 177, manganese 206, nickel 255, cobalt 234, iron 204, palladium 209, platinum 240. J. Appl. Phys. 21(10), 1022-1028, received 13 April 1950.
items.people: David Turnbull
items.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: The definitive mercury-droplet kinetics study. Droplets 2-8 microns in diameter coated with mercury laurate solidify at rates proportional to droplet VOLUME (homogeneous nucleation); droplets coated with mercury acetate solidify at rates proportional to droplet AREA (heterogeneous nucleation) — the cleanest experimental separation of the two mechanisms. J. Chem. Phys. 20(3), 411-424. An erratum appeared at J. Chem. Phys. 20(11), 1824 (1952).
items.people: David Turnbull
items.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: Equation-level, open-access source for the classical barrier that I verified by reading the text. Eq. (3): ΔG_n = n ΔG^nuc + n^(2/3) A σ; Eq. (5): n* = (-(2/3) Aσ/ΔG^nuc)³; Eq. (6): ΔG* = (4/27)(Aσ)³/(ΔG^nuc)², with A = (36π Ω1²)^(1/3) for a spherical cluster of monomer volume Ω1. Substituting A and ΔG^nuc = Ω1 Δg_v recovers exactly r* = 2γ/|Δg_v| and ΔG* = 16πγ³/(3 Δg_v²). Also has the clean Fig. 1/Fig. 2 distinction between the metastable (nucleation, G'' > 0) and unstable (spinodal, G'' < 0) regimes, which is precisely the framing a chapter deriving the barrier needs. ASM Handbook vol. 22A 'Fundamentals of Modeling for Metals Processing', D. U. Furrer and S. L. Semiatin (eds.), pp. 203-219; preprint on arXiv.
items.people: Emmanuel Clouet
items.affiliation: CEA Saclay, Service de Recherches de Métallurgie Physique, France
items.venue: ASM Handbook, Volume 22A: Fundamentals of Modeling for Metals Processing, pp. 203-219; arXiv:1001.4131

items.claim: The standard graduate monograph on nucleation — the reference to cite for the full CNT derivation (critical radius, barrier, Zeldovich factor, heterogeneous contact-angle factor) in book form. Pergamon Materials Series vol. 15, 756 pp., ISBN 978-0-08-042147-6 / 0-08-042147-4.
items.people: K. F. Kelton; A. Lindsay Greer
items.affiliation: Kelton: Washington University in St. Louis; Greer: University of Cambridge

items.claim: Standard review-article citation for CNT and its extensions, comparing theory against experiments that directly measure nucleation rates; covers condensation, cavitation and crystallization from the melt. J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 4(38), 7627-7650.
items.people: David W. Oxtoby
items.affiliation: James Franck Institute and Department of Chemistry, University of Chicago

items.claim: Modern review setting classical nucleation theory beside the nonclassical alternatives (density-functional and diffuse-interface approaches). Good single citation for 'the classical pathway is giving way to nonclassical pathways'. Cryst. Growth Des. 16(11), 6663-6681. I verified title, authors, journal, volume, pages and DOI, but could NOT open the full text to confirm it states the barrier in the exact r* = 2γ/Δg_v form — use Clouet or Kelton & Greer if you need the equation attributed to a specific page.
items.people: S. Karthika; T. K. Radhakrishnan; P. Kalaichelvi
items.affiliation: Department of Chemical Engineering, National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli, India

items.claim: Original statement of the step rule (Stufenregel): a supersaturated or supercooled system does not go directly to the most stable state but passes through the least stable state whose free energy is nearest to the starting state. Full title 'Studien über die Bildung und Umwandlung fester Körper. 1. Abhandlung: Übersättigung und Überkaltung' ('Studies on the formation and transformation of solid bodies. First paper: supersaturation and supercooling'). Z. Phys. Chem. 22U(1), 289-330.
items.people: Wilhelm Ostwald
items.affiliation: University of Leipzig

items.claim: Short, widely cited modern theoretical discussion of Ostwald's step rule, deriving it from irreversible thermodynamics — the standard 'why does the metastable phase appear first' citation. J. Phys. Chem. 88(24), 5768-5769.
items.people: R. A. van Santen
items.affiliation: Eindhoven University of Technology (the paper is deposited in the TU/e research portal)

items.claim: Direct atomic-scale experimental confirmation of Ostwald's rule of stages: in situ high-resolution electron microscopy at high temperature shows an amorphous olivine-type metal phosphate crystallizing to the stable phase through transient metastable crystalline intermediates. The best modern empirical citation for the step rule. Nature Physics 5(1), 68-73.
items.people: Sung-Yoon Chung; Young-Min Kim; Jin-Gyu Kim; Youn-Joong Kim
items.affiliation: Korea Basic Science Institute and Korean institutions (Chung later at KAIST / Sungkyunkwan; exact 2009 masthead affiliations not verified line-by-line)

items.claim: The gradient-energy free-energy functional F = ∫[f(c) + κ|∇c|²]dV — the origin of the diffuse-interface description of an interface and the direct ancestor of every phase-field model. 'Free Energy of a Nonuniform System. I. Interfacial Free Energy', J. Chem. Phys. 28(2), 258-267. Combined with the diffusion equation this gives the Cahn-Hilliard equation, ∂c/∂t = ∇·(M∇(∂f/∂c - 2κ∇²c)).
items.people: John W. Cahn; John E. Hilliard
items.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: Part III of the same series: nucleation in a two-component incompressible fluid, worked with the diffuse-interface functional rather than the sharp-interface capillarity approximation. This is the paper to cite for the result that as the spinodal is approached the critical nucleus becomes large and diffuse and the barrier goes continuously to zero — i.e. the precise sense in which classical nucleation theory fails at the nucleation/spinodal crossover. J. Chem. Phys. 31(3), 688-699.
items.people: John W. Cahn; John E. Hilliard
items.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: The spinodal decomposition paper: linear stability of a solid solution to infinitesimal composition fluctuations including gradient (surface tension) and elastic energy, giving the amplification-rate spectrum and the fastest-growing wavelength that sets the characteristic microstructural length scale. Acta Metallurgica 9(9), 795-801.
items.people: John W. Cahn
items.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

items.claim: 'Phase Separation by Spinodal Decomposition in Isotropic Systems' — the isotropic-system companion to the 1961 paper, the version usually cited for the treatment applicable to liquids and glasses rather than cubic crystals. J. Chem. Phys. 42(1), 93-99.
items.people: John W. Cahn
items.affiliation: Edgar C. Bain Laboratory for Fundamental Research, United States Steel Corporation (verify masthead if you print the affiliation; Cahn moved from GE to U.S. Steel in this period)

items.claim: Correct primary attribution for the Allen-Cahn equation: 'A microscopic theory for antiphase boundary motion and its application to antiphase domain coarsening', Acta Metallurgica 27(6), 1085-1095. The non-conserved order-parameter counterpart to Cahn-Hilliard; its key result is that the interfacial velocity is linearly proportional to the mean curvature of the boundary, with the constant of proportionality NOT containing the specific surface free energy. Author order is Allen then Cahn — 'Cahn-Allen' appears in some literature but the paper is Allen & Cahn.
items.people: Samuel M. Allen; John W. Cahn
items.affiliation: Allen: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, MIT; Cahn: National Bureau of Standards (now NIST). Masthead affiliations not verified line-by-line — verify before printing.

items.claim: THE specific quantified failure of CNT to cite. Argon condensation in a cryogenic supersonic nozzle at nucleation rates J = 10^(17±1) cm^-3 s^-1, over 34-53 K and 0.47-8 kPa: classical nucleation theory predicts rates 11-13 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE LOWER than observed, while mean-field kinetic nucleation theory gets within 1 order of magnitude. The authors attribute the failure to CNT overestimating both the critical cluster size and the excess internal energy of the critical clusters. J. Chem. Phys. 132(6), 064304. Author order and full names confirmed via Crossref; the 11-13 figure comes from the published abstract as returned by the AIP/PubMed abstract text and should be re-read against the paper before quoting verbatim.
items.people: Somnath Sinha; Ashutosh Bhabhe; Hartawan Laksmono; Judith Wölk; Reinhard Strey; Barbara E. Wyslouzil
items.affiliation: Ohio State University (Sinha, Bhabhe, Laksmono, Wyslouzil) and Universität zu Köln, Institut für Physikalische Chemie (Wölk, Strey)

items.claim: The first parameter-free simulation prediction of an absolute crystal-nucleation rate (hard-sphere colloids), explicitly framed against CNT's need for unconstrained fitted parameters. This is the reference point for the hard-sphere rate discrepancy that follows. Nature 409, 1020-1023.
items.people: Stefan Auer; Daan Frenkel
items.affiliation: FOM Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics (AMOLF), Amsterdam

items.claim: The hard-sphere colloid discrepancy, stated bluntly in the title: 'Simulation of nucleation in almost hard-sphere colloids: The discrepancy between experiment and simulation persists.' Independent simulation methods agree with each other and disagree with experiment. J. Chem. Phys. 134(13), 134901.
items.people: Laura Filion; Ran Ni; Daan Frenkel; Marjolein Dijkstra
items.affiliation: Soft Condensed Matter, Debye Institute for NanoMaterials Science, Utrecht University (Filion, Ni, Dijkstra); University of Cambridge (Frenkel)

items.claim: Quantifies the hard-sphere discrepancy in one sentence you can quote-check: 'at low super-saturations, experimentally observed nucleation rates and numerically computed ones differ by more than ten orders of magnitude.' Proposes resolving it by reading the experimental data as nucleation plus crystal growth rather than nucleation alone. Phys. Rev. Lett. 128(23), 238001; preprint arXiv:2205.06040 (2022), where I read the abstract.
items.people: Wilkin Wöhler; Tanja Schilling
items.affiliation: Institute of Physics, University of Freiburg, Germany

items.claim: Authoritative recent review of the hard-sphere system, including a full account of the nucleation-rate discrepancy and the candidate explanations (polydispersity, residual charge, hydrodynamics, sedimentation, volume-fraction calibration) and why none of them closes the gap. Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045003. Bibliographic details verified via Crossref; I did not read the full text (file exceeded fetch limits), so attribute specific numbers to Wöhler & Schilling rather than to this review.
items.people: C. Patrick Royall; Patrick Charbonneau; Marjolein Dijkstra; John Russo; Frank Smallenburg; Thomas Speck; Chantal Valeriani
items.affiliation: Multi-institutional (ESPCI Paris, Duke University, Utrecht University, University of Bristol, CNRS/Université Paris-Saclay, University of Stuttgart, Universidad Complutense de Madrid)

items.claim: The two-step / nonclassical nucleation result: a metastable fluid-fluid critical point drastically changes the pathway to a crystal nucleus, lowering the barrier and raising the nucleation rate by many orders of magnitude relative to the classical single-order-parameter picture. The canonical citation for 'the reaction coordinate is not the nucleus radius'. Science 277(5334), 1975-1978.
items.people: Pieter Rein ten Wolde; Daan Frenkel
items.affiliation: FOM Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics (AMOLF), Amsterdam

openQuestions: Volmer & Weber 1926 author initials: De Gruyter's own metadata renders the second author as 'Α. Weber' with a Greek capital alpha (an OCR artifact). The correct form is A. Weber. Many reference lists (Scientific Research Publishing and others) propagate a mangled 'Volmer, M. and Weber, A.Z. (1926)' where the 'Z.' is actually the start of 'Zeitschrift'. Do not copy that form.

Becker & Döring 1935 masthead affiliation could not be verified — Wiley returned HTTP 403. Becker held the theoretical physics chair at Technische Hochschule Berlin from 1926 and moved to Göttingen in the mid-1930s (sources give 1933 and 1936); Döring was his student in Berlin and followed him to Göttingen in 1939. If the chapter names an institution for the 1935 paper, check the printed masthead first.
The 1935 Becker-Döring volume number is a live citation trap: continuous vol. 416 = 5. Folge Band 24. Pick one convention and state it, because both appear in the standard literature.

Turnbull's mercury supercooling: Table I of the 1950 J. Appl. Phys. paper gives (ΔT)max = 58 K (from the 1950 J. Chem. Phys. 18, 768 droplet study), while the same paper's text says nucleation was measurable over 59-63 degrees of supercooling for mercury. If the chapter quotes a single number, say '~58-60 K below the 234.3 K melting point' and cite the table. The frequently repeated '77 K for mercury' does not appear in this table.

Cahn's institutional affiliation in 1965 (U.S. Steel Edgar C. Bain Laboratory vs. General Electric) and Allen & Cahn's 1979 affiliations were inferred from career chronology, not read off the paper. Verify against the printed mastheads before stating them.

The 11-13 orders of magnitude figure for argon comes from the published abstract of Sinha et al. 2010 as relayed by two independent abstract sources; AIP blocked direct fetch. Re-read the paper before quoting the range verbatim, and note it is specific to argon in a cryogenic nozzle at J ≈ 10^17 cm^-3 s^-1 — do not generalise it to 'CNT is always off by 13 orders'.

Chung et al. 2009 (Nature Physics) individual author affiliations were not verified line-by-line; the paper appears in the Korea Basic Science Institute, KAIST and Sungkyunkwan repositories, which reflects later moves.

If the chapter wants the Zeldovich factor by name, note that Zeldovich's 1943 paper (Acta Physicochim. URSS 18, 1-22, and Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 12, 525, 1942) has no DOI I could verify, so I have deliberately left it out rather than supply an unchecked link. Cite it from Kelton & Greer or Clouet instead if you need it.

Two further Ostwald-step-rule discussions often cited (Threlfall, Org. Process Res. Dev. 2003; 'Ostwald Rule of Stages: Myth or Reality?', Cryst. Growth Des. 2022) were seen in search results but not verified, so they are omitted. Say the word and I will check them.

verdicts.claim: Volmer & Weber, 'Keimbildung in übersättigten Gebilden', Z. Phys. Chem. 119U(1), 277-301 (1926), DOI 10.1515/zpch-1926-11927; author is A. Weber, not 'Weber, A.Z.'
verdicts.correction: Crossref record confirms exactly: title 'Keimbildung in übersättigten Gebilden', volume 119U, issue 1, pages 277-301, published-print 1926, publisher Walter de Gruyter, authors M. Volmer (first) and Weber (additional). The dossier's warning is correct and I reproduced the artifact: Crossref renders the second author's initial as 'Α.' with a Greek capital alpha (U+0391), an OCR error for Latin 'A.'. The 'Weber, A.Z. (1926)' form is indeed a truncation of 'Weber, A., Z. [Zeitschrift]'. CAVEAT: Volmer's masthead affiliation (Institute of Physical Chemistry, TH Berlin) is NOT in the Crossref record and I could not open the De Gruyter page — Volmer did hold the TH Berlin chair from 1922, but do not print it as read off the paper.

verdicts.claim: Farkas, 'Keimbildungsgeschwindigkeit in übersättigten Dämpfen', Z. Phys. Chem. 125U(1), 236-242 (1927), DOI 10.1515/zpch-1927-12513; first kinetic/rate treatment predating Becker–Döring
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms title, sole author L. Farkas, volume 125U, issue 1, pages 236-242, 1927. The characterization is defensible: Farkas 1927 gives the first steady-state kinetic (rate) treatment of nucleation. One nuance worth adding if the chapter leans on priority — Farkas credits the method to a suggestion by Leo Szilard, which is the standard attribution in the historical literature, and Volmer & Weber 1926 already contained a rate expression, so 'first kinetic treatment' should be understood as 'first steady-state cluster-kinetics treatment'.

verdicts.claim: Becker & Döring, Ann. Phys. 416(8), 719-752 (1935), DOI 10.1002/andp.19354160806; continuous vol. 416 = Band 24 of the 5. Folge, so 'Ann. Phys. 24, 719' and 'Ann. Phys. 416, 719' are the same paper
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: title 'Kinetische Behandlung der Keimbildung in übersättigten Dämpfen', authors R. Becker; W. Döring, Annalen der Physik volume 416, issue 8, pages 719-752, 1935. The volume-mapping caution is arithmetically correct: Annalen der Physik 5. Folge Band 1 = continuous volume 393 (1929), so Band 24 = 393 + 23 = 416. The dossier's own caveat stands — the masthead institutional affiliation remains unverified (Wiley blocks fetch); do not print an institution for this paper.

verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms the paper (D. Turnbull; J. C. Fisher, JCP 17(1), 71-73, 1949) and the errata ('Errata: Rate of Nucleation in Condensed Systems', JCP 17, 429-429, 1949, DOI 10.1063/1.1747279). The equation form is independently corroborated: page 1022 of the Turnbull 1950 J. Appl. Phys. reprint I read restates it as Eq. Affiliation 'Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York' is confirmed by the 1950 companion masthead.

verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms title, authors D. Turnbull and R. E. Cech, J. Appl. Phys. volume 21, issue 8, pages 804-810, August 1950. App. Phys. 21, 804 (1950)', and reference 2 is the source column entry for most rows of Table I (antimony through palladium).

Quotes verified verbatim: p.1023 'For most metals (ΔT_)max is of the order of 0.18 times the absolute melting temperature, T0' and '(ΔT_)max is reproducible (±5 percent)'; p.1026 '≈0.185 with maximum deviations of ±0.02. Considering all the data, the ratio ranges from 0.133 for lead to 0.250 for gallium'; p.1023 'easily measurable only in narrow ranges of temperature corresponding to 59 to 63° supercooling for mercury and 100 to 115° for tin' and 'A = 10^30.4 for tin and 10^30.9 for mercury' compared to 'A≈10^33 calculated from the theory of homogeneous nucleation but considerably larger than the value 10^25 to be expected if nucleation were catalyzed by a film'; p.1023 'mercury droplets 4 microns in diameter were found to solidify with a frequency of about 10^-5 sec.^-1 at ΔT_ = 60'. Masthead: 'D. TURNBULL, Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York (Received April 13, 1950)'.

verdicts.claim: Clouet, ASM Handbook vol. 22A pp. 203-219, arXiv:1001.4131: Eq. (3) ΔG_n = n ΔG^nuc + n^(2/3) Aσ; Eq. (5) n* = (-(2/3)Aσ/ΔG^nuc)³; Eq. (6) ΔG* = (4/27)(Aσ)³/(ΔG^nuc)², reducing to r* = 2γ/|Δg_v| and ΔG* = 16πγ³/(3Δg_v²)

Furrer and S.L. Semiatin (Ed.) (2009) 203-219'. Every detail in the dossier matches. I also checked the algebra independently rather than trusting the equation numbers: minimizing nΔg + n^(2/3)Aσ gives n^(1/3) = -2Aσ/(3Δg), hence n* = (-2Aσ/(3Δg))³ and ΔG* = (-8/27 + 12/27)(Aσ)³/Δg² = (4/27)(Aσ)³/Δg². Substituting A = (36πΩ1²)^(1/3) and Δg = Ω1Δg_v gives ΔG* = (4/27)(36π)σ³/Δg_v² = 16πσ³/(3Δg_v²), and n*Ω1 = (4/3)πr*³ gives r*³ = 8σ³/|Δg_v|³, i.e. r* = 2σ/|Δg_v|. The reduction is exact. Note the dossier omits the paper's title — supply 'Modeling of Nucleation Processes'.

Uebersättigung und Ueberkaltung' (Ue for Ü); the dossier's modernized form is the standard modern citation form and is fine, just don't present it as a facsimile transcription.

verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms: 'On spinodal decomposition', John W Cahn, Acta Metallurgica volume 9, issue 9, pages 795-801, September 1961, DOI 10.1016/0001-6160(61)90182-1. His documented chronology is General Electric, Schenectady 1954-1964; MIT Department of Metallurgy 1964-1978; National Bureau of Standards from 1977; University of Washington affiliate from 1984 (confirmed by his Wikipedia entry, the NAE Memorial Tributes vol. 22 entry, and obituary coverage — none of which mention U.S. Steel). verdicts.claim: ten Wolde & Frenkel, Science 277(5334), 1975-1978 (1997): a metastable fluid-fluid critical point drastically changes the pathway to a crystal nucleus, lowering the barrier and raising the rate by many orders of magnitude; 'the canonical citation for the reaction coordinate is not the nucleus radius'
verdicts.correction: The bibliography is exactly right — Crossref confirms Pieter Rein ten Wolde; Daan Frenkel, Science volume 277, issue 5334, pages 1975-1978, 26 September 1997, DOI 10.1126/science.277.5334.1975 — and the physics is right: the abstract states that in simulations of homogeneous crystal nucleation, the presence of a metastable fluid-fluid critical point drastically changes the pathway for formation of a crystal nucleus, and that close to that critical point the free-energy barrier is strongly reduced so the nucleation rate increases by many orders of magnitude. THE PROBLEM IS THE MISSING TITLE AND THE RESULTING SCOPE DRIFT: the paper is 'Enhancement of Protein Crystal Nucleation by Critical Density Fluctuations', and the result is obtained for a model of globular proteins with short-range attractive interactions, not for nucleation in general. The dossier presents it as a generic 'two-step / nonclassical nucleation result' with no title given; a chapter citing it should print the title and say 'in a model of globular proteins with short-range attractions'. The 'reaction coordinate is not the nucleus radius' line is a defensible gloss but is the chapter's phrasing, not the paper's — do not put it in quotation marks.

rg-mechanism.domain: Renormalization group as mechanism: momentum-shell integration, RG eigenvalues as critical exponents, the Wilson-Fisher fixed point and epsilon expansion, and the scaling/hyperscaling relations
rg-mechanism.summary:
THE MECHANISM, IN THE ORDER A GRADUATE ARGUMENT NEEDS IT.

(1) MOMENTUM-SHELL INTEGRATION. Start from a Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson Hamiltonian for an n-component field S(q) with UV cutoff Lambda: H = integral over q of [(r + q^2)/2]|S(q)|^2 plus a quartic term u. Split the field into "outer" modes with Lambda/b <= |q| <= Lambda and "inner" modes |q| < Lambda/b, with b > 1. Step one: do the partition-function integral over the outer shell only, perturbatively in u. Step two: rescale q' = bq and the surviving field so the cutoff returns to Lambda. The composition of the two steps maps the theory back to itself with shifted couplings, which is what makes it a semigroup. To one loop this yields recursion relations of the form r' = b^2 [ r + (u/2) S_d integral from Lambda/b to Lambda of p^(d-1) dp/(r+p^2) ] and u' = b^(4-d) u [ 1 - (3u/2) S_d integral from Lambda/b to Lambda of p^(d-1) dp/(r+p^2)^2 ], where S_d is the angular phase-space factor. Setting b = e^l and differentiating gives the flow equations. I verified these exact recursion relations as Eqs. (44)-(45) and the differential form as Eqs. (48)-(49) of Täuber's lecture notes (arXiv:1112.1375).

Historically, Wilson (1971b) did NOT use a sharp momentum shell. He used a "phase-space cell" decomposition: a set of orthogonal localized wave-packet functions for each order-of-magnitude (octave) range of momentum, integrating out |q| ~ 1, then 0.25 to 0.5, and so on, i.e. b = 2 per step, producing a nonlinear integral recursion formula for a sequence of effective Landau-Ginzburg potentials V^(l)(s). The clean sharp-shell scheme found in textbooks is the streamlined descendant presented in Wilson & Kogut (1974). Wilson (1971a) is the companion paper that recasts Kadanoff's block-spin scaling picture in differential, recursion-relation form.

(2) HOW A LINEARIZED EIGENVALUE BECOMES AN EXPONENT. Let R_b be the RG map on the space of Hamiltonians and H* a fixed point, R_b H* = H*. Because a well-designed RG transformation is smooth, it can be Taylor-expanded near H*; linearizing gives a linear operator L_b whose eigenoperators Q_k (partial Hamiltonians) have eigenvalues Lambda_k(b) = b^(lambda_k), the exponential form forced by the semigroup property Lambda_k(b1 b2) = Lambda_k(b1) Lambda_k(b2). The conjugate scaling fields g_k then flow as g_k(l) = e^(lambda_k l) g_k(0). Sign of lambda_k classifies the perturbation: lambda_k > 0 RELEVANT (grows under coarse-graining, drives the system away from criticality), lambda_k < 0 IRRELEVANT (dies, and is the source of universality), lambda_k = 0 MARGINAL (needs higher order; gives logarithms, continuously varying exponents, lines of fixed points).

Matching the singular free energy through l iterations, f_s(t,h,{g_j}) = |t|^(2-alpha) F( h/|t|^Delta, ..., g_j/|t|^(phi_j), ... ), pins every exponent to an eigenvalue. Fisher (1998), Eq. (50), states the correspondence explicitly: 2 - alpha = d/lambda_1, Delta = lambda_2/lambda_1, phi_j = lambda_j/lambda_1, and nu = 1/lambda_1. So NU IS THE RECIPROCAL OF THE THERMAL EIGENVALUE, nu = 1/y_t, and combining the first and last of Eq. (50) gives hyperscaling d nu = 2 - alpha for free. This is the single best citable line for the correspondence. The general formulation (nonlinear scaling fields, why the physical t, h, g must be replaced by smooth nonlinear combinations, and the leading correction-to-scaling exponent omega from the least-irrelevant eigenvalue) is Wegner (1972); Wilson himself cites Wegner (1972a, 1976) for exactly this, per Fisher (1998) fn. 33-37. Fisher (1974) is the standard expository citation.

(3) THE WILSON-FISHER FIXED POINT AND THE EPSILON EXPANSION. In the differential flow du/dl = (4-d) u - (3/2) u^2 S_d Lambda^(d-4) + ..., the Gaussian fixed point u* = 0 is stable for d > 4 and unstable for d < 4. Below four dimensions a second, nontrivial fixed point splits off continuously from it: for the Ising case u* S_d Lambda^(4-d) = (2/3) epsilon, with epsilon = 4 - d (Täuber Eq. 48; for general n, u* = 6 epsilon/(n+8), his Eq. 76). That is the Wilson-Fisher fixed point, and its distance from Gaussian is O(epsilon), which is what makes perturbation theory legitimate: epsilon, not u, is the small parameter.

NON-INTEGER DIMENSION means dimensional continuation of the momentum integrals, not a space. In the recursion relations d appears only through the explicit exponent b^(4-d) and through the analytic geometric factor S_d = 2 pi^(d/2) / [Gamma(d/2) (2 pi)^d]. Both are analytic functions of d, so d can be carried as a parameter. There is no lattice in 3.99 dimensions. Fisher's own account: "d appeared simply as an explicit parameter" in Wilson's recursion relation, and he suggested treating the dimensional deviation as a small nonintegral quantity; Wilson showed it worked, and the one-loop recursion relations proved exact to leading order in epsilon (independent of the arbitrary b), which is why the result is universal.

THE FACTOR OF 12. Linearizing the flow of the thermal field around the Wilson-Fisher fixed point: dtau/dl = tau [ 2 - (u*/2) S_d Lambda^(d-4) ] = tau [ 2 - epsilon/3 ] for the Ising case. Hence y_t = lambda_1 = 2 - epsilon/3, and nu = 1/y_t = (1/2)(1 - epsilon/6)^(-1) = 1/2 + epsilon/12 + O(epsilon^2), with eta = 0 + O(epsilon^2). I verified this as Eqs. (50)-(51) of Täuber. For general n, the two symmetry factors of the one-loop phi^4 diagrams do the work: the tadpole renormalizing r carries (n+2)/6 times u, the one-loop correction to u carries (n+8)/6 times u^2 (visible in Täuber's Z-factors, Eqs. 65-66). Therefore u* = 6 epsilon/(n+8) and 1/nu = 2 - [(n+2)/(n+8)] epsilon + O(epsilon^2) (his Eq. 78), i.e. nu = 1/2 + [(n+2)/(4(n+8))] epsilon. THE 12 IS 4(n+8)/(n+2) EVALUATED AT n=1: 4 x 9 / 3 = 12. Equivalently, ratio (n+2)/(n+8) = 1/3 gives y_t = 2 - epsilon/3, and inverting the 2 produces the extra factor of 4. Wilson & Fisher's own 1972 PRL quoted the companion result gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 + O(epsilon^2), described by Fisher as "the first general formula for a nonclassical exponent"; with eta = O(epsilon^2) and gamma = nu(2-eta) this is the same statement.

Numerically, epsilon = 1 gives nu = 0.583 against the modern conformal-bootstrap value nu = 0.629971, so the bare one-loop series is a qualitative, not quantitative, success; that is what motivates the higher-order series and Borel resummation of Guida & Zinn-Justin and the compendium of Pelissetto & Vicari.

(4) KADANOFF, WIDOM, AND THE SCALING RELATIONS. Widom (1965b) proposed the homogeneity/scaling form of the equation of state: a function Phi(x,y) of temperature and density variables is a homogeneous function of positive degree, which converts exponent INEQUALITIES into EQUALITIES. Kadanoff (1966) supplied the physical mechanism: divide the Ising model into cells microscopically large but much smaller than the correlation length, use the total magnetization of each cell as a collective variable, and argue the block system is an Ising model with renormalized t and h; this partially justified Widom's homogeneity and yielded d nu' = gamma' + 2 beta. Wilson's Paper I is explicitly titled as recasting this Kadanoff picture. Kadanoff's step is a hypothesis (a single effective block-block coupling); Wilson's contribution is that the coarse-graining is actually performed, generates the whole space of couplings, and its linearization is computable.

Attribution of the individual relations, verified from Fisher's own footnotes in the 1998 RMP:
- alpha + 2 beta + gamma = 2 (Rushbrooke): proposed as an EQUALITY by Essam & Fisher (1963), the paper that also introduced the now-standard alpha, beta, gamma, delta notation; proved as the rigorous INEQUALITY alpha' + 2 beta + gamma' >= 2 by Rushbrooke (1963) for magnets with H -> -H symmetry, from positivity of the specific heat (Second Law); extended to fluids by Fisher (1964), his Eq. (2.20).
- alpha' + beta(1 + delta) >= 2 (Griffiths): Griffiths (1965), from convexity of the free energy. Fisher also credits Buckingham & Gunton, Phys. Rev. 178, 848 (1969) with the corresponding correlation-exponent inequalities.
- gamma = (2 - eta) nu (Fisher's relation): Fisher (1964), his Eq. (5.7), from G(r) ~ r^-(d-2+eta) g(r/xi) integrated over space; the rigorous inequality gamma <= (2 - eta) nu was proved in Fisher (1969).
- gamma = beta(delta - 1) (Widom): Widom (1965b).
- d nu = 2 - alpha (Josephson hyperscaling): the inequality nu d >= 2 - alpha is Josephson (1967, two parts); Fisher credits the equality to Widom (1965a), Kadanoff (1966), and Stell. Hyperscaling is the only relation containing d, holds exactly for the d=2 Ising model, and FAILS above d=4 because the quartic coupling becomes a "dangerous irrelevant variable" - the scaling function does not have a finite limit as its irrelevant argument goes to zero. In RG language, hyperscaling is exactly the statement 2 - alpha = d/lambda_1 combined with nu = 1/lambda_1.

items.claim: Paper I of the pair that founded the modern RG. Recasts Kadanoff's block-spin scaling picture for an Ising ferromagnet in differential form, so that the scaling relations follow from renormalization-group differential equations rather than from a homogeneity hypothesis. This is the paper to cite for 'RG as a flow', as distinct from Paper II which does the actual mode elimination.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson
items.affiliation: Cornell University (Fisher 1998 places Wilson at Cornell 1965-1972)

items.claim: Paper II: the actual mechanism. Solves a generalized Ising model with continuously variable spin and a quartic term by a change of variable to localized wave-packet ('phase-space cell') functions, with one orthogonal set per order-of-magnitude range of momentum. Modes of momentum of order 1 are integrated out leaving |q| < 0.5, then modes between 0.25 and 0.5, and so on - i.e. octave-by-octave elimination with rescaling factor b = 2. The result is a nonlinear integral recursion formula for a sequence of effective Landau-Ginzburg potentials V^(l). This is the ancestor of momentum-shell integration; it is NOT yet the sharp-cutoff shell scheme of textbooks. Wilson solved the recursion numerically and obtained a nu for d=3 clearly different from the classical 1/2 - the result Fisher says convinced him 'a major barrier to progress had been overcome'.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson
items.affiliation: Cornell University (Fisher 1998 places Wilson at Cornell 1965-1972)

items.claim: The Wilson-Fisher fixed point and the birth of the epsilon expansion. Critical exponents computed for d = 4 - epsilon with epsilon small, by treating the dimensional deviation as a small non-integral parameter in Wilson's recursion relations - legitimate because d enters those relations only through the analytic factors b^(4-d) and S_d = 2 pi^(d/2)/[Gamma(d/2)(2 pi)^d], never through a lattice. Contains gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 + O(epsilon^2) for the Ising-like (n=1) case and gamma = 1 + epsilon/5 for the XY (n=2) case. Fisher, in his 1998 RMP first-person account, calls this 'the first general formula for a nonclassical exponent' and records that he was the one who proposed treating 4-d as small, and that Wilson showed the one-loop recursion relations are exact to leading order in epsilon (results independent of the arbitrary rescaling factor b), which is why they are universal. With eta = O(epsilon^2) and gamma = nu(2-eta), gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 is equivalent to nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson and Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University (both; Wilson in the Laboratory of Nuclear Studies, Fisher in chemistry/Baker Lab - the Cornell affiliation is verified via Fisher 1998, the departmental detail is not)

items.claim: The follow-up five weeks later that turned the epsilon expansion into a systematic diagrammatic series. Computes gamma, eta and the crossover index phi for classical Heisenberg models with n internal degrees of freedom as an exact expansion in epsilon = 4 - d, to order epsilon^2 for gamma and epsilon^3 for eta. Setting n = epsilon = 1 (3D Ising) gives gamma = 1.244 and eta = 0.037. Cite this, not the 3.99 paper, when the argument needs the graph-by-graph structure of the expansion rather than the existence of the fixed point.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson
items.affiliation: Cornell University (Fisher 1998 places Wilson at Cornell 1965-1972)

items.claim: The 125-page Physics Reports monograph that is the canonical source for momentum-shell RG in its streamlined, sharp-cutoff form, and for the epsilon expansion carried out systematically. Presents the modern formulation of the RG for both critical phenomena in classical statistical mechanics and quantum field theory, emphasizing principles over applications. If the book states the momentum-shell procedure as a procedure (split at Lambda/b, integrate the shell, rescale, iterate), this is the reference, with Wilson (1971b) cited for its origin. Note: Crossref records pages 75-199; a great many secondary sources cite 75-200.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson and John Kogut
items.affiliation: Cornell University (Wilson); affiliation of Kogut not verified from a source I saw

items.claim: The block-spin argument. Divide the Ising model into cells that are microscopically large but much smaller than the correlation length; use the total magnetization within each cell as a collective variable; argue that the block system is again an Ising model with renormalized t and h. Kadanoff presents it as 'a partial justification for Widom's conjecture about the homogeneity of the free energy' and derives the hyperscaling form d nu' = gamma' + 2 beta. The weak point - which Wilson's Paper I is explicitly written to repair - is the assumption of a single effective coupling J between adjacent block spins; Fisher (1998) identifies precisely this, together with the unexplained power-law form of the rescaling factors, as 'the principal difficulties' in Kadanoff's picture.
items.people: Leo P. Kadanoff
items.affiliation: University of Illinois, Urbana (commonly recorded; not verified from a source I saw)

items.claim: Widom's scaling form: the equation of state near the critical point is written via a function Phi(x,y), with x a measure of temperature and y of density; classical (van der Waals type) fluids have Phi constant, while in a real fluid Phi is a HOMOGENEOUS function of positive degree. This homogeneity hypothesis is what converts the previously derived exponent inequalities into equalities - e.g. gamma = beta(delta - 1) - without deriving them. Fisher calls it 'the most direct and phenomenological' route, 'a bold, new thermodynamic hypothesis'. Domb & Hunter (1965) and Patashinskii & Pokrovskii (1966) reached the same conclusion by other routes.
items.people: Benjamin Widom
items.affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York (recorded in the Crossref metadata)

items.claim: Widom's companion paper in the same issue, on surface tension and molecular correlations near the critical point. Cite this one - not the equation-of-state paper - for the hyperscaling relation d nu = 2 - alpha: Fisher (1998) fn. 88 credits the equality to 'Kadanoff (1966), Widom (1965a), and Stell (1965, unpublished)'. Widom (1965a) is 3892-3897, Widom (1965b) is 3898-3905; textbooks routinely conflate them.
items.people: Benjamin Widom
items.affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York (recorded in the Crossref metadata)

items.claim: The paper that proposed alpha' + 2 beta + gamma' = 2 as an EQUALITY (from a droplet-model partition function) and, per Fisher (1998) fn. 50, introduced 'the now generally accepted notation for the thermodynamic critical exponents' - i.e. alpha, beta, gamma, delta. Cite it when the book first names the exponents, and when distinguishing the conjectured equality from Rushbrooke's rigorous inequality that followed it.
items.people: John W. Essam and Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Not verified from a source I saw

items.claim: Rushbrooke's inequality: alpha' + 2 beta + gamma' >= 2. A two-page note. Fisher's account: 'Moved by the suggested thermodynamic exponent equality, Rushbrooke (1963) quickly showed that for magnetic systems (with H -> -H symmetry) the positivity of specific heats implied by the Second Law of Thermodynamics could be used to prove rigorously the inequality.' The primes denote below-Tc exponents; scaling later implies alpha = alpha', gamma = gamma', so the distinction is now rarely made. The mechanism-level point for the book: the inequality is thermodynamics alone, the equality requires scaling, and the RG explains why the equality holds.
items.people: G. S. Rushbrooke
items.affiliation: Newcastle upon Tyne, UK (commonly recorded; not verified from a source I saw)
items.venue: The Journal of Chemical Physics 39(3), 842-843 (1 August 1963)

items.claim: Griffiths' inequality: alpha' + beta(1 + delta) >= 2, proved from convexity of the free energy - the second of the two classic thermodynamic exponent inequalities, and the one that becomes an equality under Widom scaling. Griffiths gave the fuller treatment in J. Chem. Phys. 43(6), 1958-1968 (1965), DOI 10.1063/1.1697060 (title seen in search results, DOI not independently resolved). Fisher (1998) fn. 50 additionally credits Buckingham & Gunton, Phys. Rev. 178, 848-853 (1969) with the corresponding rigorous inequalities for the CORRELATION exponents.
items.people: Robert B. Griffiths
items.affiliation: Carnegie Institute of Technology, Pittsburgh (commonly recorded; not verified from a source I saw)

items.claim: Fisher's relation gamma = (2 - eta) nu. Fisher (1998) fn. 50 cites 'Fisher (1959; 1962; 1964, see Eq. (5.7); 1967b)' for this relation, making this 62-page J. Math. Phys. review the standard citable source with a specific equation number. It follows from the correlation-function scaling form G(r;T) ~ D r^-(d-2+eta) g(r/xi) integrated over all space to give the susceptibility. The same paper (Eq. 2.20) extends Rushbrooke's inequality from magnets to fluids. The rigorous inequality gamma <= (2 - eta) nu was proved later in Fisher, 'Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena', Contemporary Physics Vol. 1, Proc. Int. Symp. Trieste 1968 (IAEA, Vienna, 1969), pp. 19-46 - no DOI located.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: The Rockefeller Institute, New York (recorded in the Crossref metadata)

items.claim: The hyperscaling INEQUALITY nu d >= 2 - alpha, in two parts: Part I, 'Inequality for the specific heat: I. Derivation', Proc. Phys. Soc. 92, 269-275, derives a rigorous inequality relating a specific heat, the temperature derivative of the expectation of an arbitrary operator, and the mean-square fluctuation of that operator in an equilibrium ensemble; Part II, 'Inequality for the specific heat: II. Application to critical phenomena', Proc. Phys. Soc. 92, 276-284, DOI 10.1088/0370-1328/92/2/302, applies it to criticality. Josephson supplies the rigorous half; the equality d nu = 2 - alpha comes from scaling (Widom 1965a, Kadanoff 1966, Stell). Both DOIs verified against Crossref records.
items.people: B. D. Josephson
items.affiliation: University of Cambridge (commonly recorded; not verified from a source I saw)
items.venue: Proceedings of the Physical Society 92(2), 269-275 (Part I) and 276-284 (Part II) (1967)

items.claim: The general formulation of what the linearized RG eigenvalues MEAN. Wegner shows that the higher-order (nonlinear) contributions to the linearized RG equations are absorbed by redefining the fields as smooth nonlinear analytic functions of the physical fields - the 'nonlinear scaling fields' - after which an EXACT scaling law holds, and the deviations from pure power laws (corrections to scaling, controlled by the leading irrelevant eigenvalue, the exponent now called omega) follow as a systematic expansion. Also explains where logarithms in the free energy come from, i.e. the marginal case. Fisher (1998) reports that Wilson himself, dividing RG theory into four parts, cited 'Wegner (1972a, 1976)' for 'the formal theory of fixed points and linear and nonlinear behavior near fixed points'. Wegner's companion review, 'The Critical State, General Aspects', in Domb & Green eds., Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena Vol. 6 (Academic, London, 1976), pp. 7-124, is the other half of that citation; I found no DOI for it.
items.people: Franz J. Wegner
items.affiliation: Department of Physics, Brown University, Providence, Rhode Island, on leave from the Institut fuer Festkoerperforschung, Kernforschungsanlage Juelich

items.claim: THE standard expository citation for the RG in critical behavior - an introductory-level review with emphasis on magnetic systems, covering the dependence of exponents on dimensionality, symmetry and exchange couplings, and the calculation of scaling functions for the equation of state and critical scattering. Fisher (1998) points back to this 1974 review specifically for 'the special character of the hyperscaling relations' (fn. 87) and for the systematic account of apparent hyperscaling violations in 3D Ising series 'with hindsight enlightened by RG theory' (fn. 91). NOTE: there is an erratum, 'Erratum: The renormalization group in the theory of critical behavior', Rev. Mod. Phys. 47, 543 (1975), DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.47.543 - verified separately; cite both.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Cornell University at the time (not verified from a source I saw); Fisher moved to Maryland in 1987

items.claim: The single most useful citation for the eigenvalue-to-exponent correspondence stated as an equation. Fisher linearizes R_b about the fixed point, obtains eigenoperators Q_k with eigenvalues Lambda_k(b) = b^(lambda_k) (the power-law form forced by the semigroup property), writes the generalized free-energy scaling form as his Eq. (49), and then in Eq. (50) gives the correspondence in full: 2 - alpha = d/lambda_1, Delta = lambda_2/lambda_1, phi_j = lambda_j/lambda_1, and NU = 1/LAMBDA_1. He immediately adds that the sign of lambda_j determines relevance (lambda_j > 0), marginality (lambda_j = 0), or irrelevance (lambda_j < 0) of the operator Q_j and its conjugate field g_j, and notes that the first and last of Eq. (50) yield the hyperscaling relation d nu = 2 - alpha. The paper also contains Fisher's first-person account of the birth of the epsilon expansion at Cornell in September 1971 and of Wilson's 'flows in a large space'. I read the full text of this paper directly.
items.people: Michael E. Fisher
items.affiliation: Institute for Physical Science and Technology, University of Maryland, College Park, Maryland 20742

items.claim: Wilson's 1982 Nobel lecture (delivered 8 December 1982), presenting the RG and the epsilon expansion in his own words. Useful for the book as the author's retrospective framing of what the coarse-graining actually accomplishes - and Fisher (1998) repeatedly cites Wilson (1983) for Wilson's own account of his path from Gell-Mann-Low to Kadanoff's scaling hypothesis to the recursion formula.
items.people: Kenneth G. Wilson
items.affiliation: Cornell University

items.claim: The modern pedagogical source in which I directly verified every number in the mechanism section above. Section 2.5, 'Wilson's momentum shell renormalization group', states the two RG steps explicitly (integrate Fourier components with Lambda/b <= |q| <= Lambda, then rescale), derives the one-loop recursion relations as Eqs. (44)-(45), the differential flow as Eqs. (48)-(49) with the Ising fixed point u* S_d = (2/3) epsilon Lambda^(4-d), the thermal recursion relation as Eq. (50), and then Eq. (51): nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12 + O(epsilon^2), eta = 0 + O(epsilon^2), obtained by identifying nu^-1 = 2 - epsilon/3. The field-theoretic half gives the O(n) generalization: Z-factors with the (n+2)/6 and (n+8)/6 symmetry factors (Eqs. 65-66), fixed point u* = 6 epsilon/(n+8) (Eq. 76), eta = (n+2) epsilon^2 / [2 (n+8)^2] (Eq. 77), and nu^-1 = 2 - [(n+2)/(n+8)] epsilon + O(epsilon^2) (Eq. 78), reducing to Eq. (51) at n = 1. This is where the factor of 12 is transparently 4(n+8)/(n+2) at n = 1.
items.people: Uwe C. Taeuber
items.affiliation: Department of Physics, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA 24061-0435, USA
items.venue: Nuclear Physics B Proceedings Supplements 228C, 7-34 (2012); arXiv:1112.1375; journal DOI 10.1016/j.nuclphysbps.2012.06.002

items.claim: The comprehensive modern review of critical phenomena and RG theory - Ising and general O(N) universality classes, exponents, equation of state, amplitude ratios, two-point function, in three and two dimensions, including the technology (fixed-dimension expansion vs. epsilon expansion, minimal subtraction, Borel resummation) that turns the divergent epsilon series into numbers. Cite this for reference exponent values and for the statement that the epsilon expansion is asymptotic, not convergent. Preprint year 2000, journal year 2002 - the arXiv v1 is 10 December 2000, final v6 3 May 2002.
items.people: Andrea Pelissetto and Ettore Vicari
items.affiliation: Not verified from a source I saw (Rome La Sapienza and Pisa respectively, commonly recorded)

items.claim: The standard resummed-exponent reference: critical exponents of the N-vector model obtained by Borel-type resummation of both the fixed-dimension and epsilon-expansion perturbative series. Use this as the citation for 'what the epsilon expansion gives once you resum it', against which the raw one-loop nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12 = 0.583 at epsilon = 1 can be judged.
items.people: R. Guida and J. Zinn-Justin
items.affiliation: Not verified from a source I saw (Saclay, commonly recorded)
items.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 31(40), 8103-8121 (1998)

items.claim: The current high-precision benchmark for the 3D Ising universality class from the conformal bootstrap: Delta_sigma = 0.5181489(10), Delta_epsilon = 1.412625(10), lambda_sigma-sigma-epsilon = 1.0518537(41), lambda_epsilon-epsilon-epsilon = 1.532435(19). NOTE: the abstract quotes SCALING DIMENSIONS, not exponents. Converting via nu = 1/(d - Delta_epsilon) with d = 3 gives nu = 1/1.587375 = 0.629971, and eta = 2 Delta_sigma - d + 2 = 0.0362978. That conversion is mine, done from the quoted numbers; the paper's abstract does not print nu or eta. Against nu = 0.629971, the raw one-loop epsilon expansion at epsilon = 1 (0.583) is about 7 percent low.
items.people: Filip Kos, David Poland, David Simmons-Duffin and Alessandro Vichi
items.affiliation: Not verified from a source I saw
items.venue: Journal of High Energy Physics 2016(8), 036; arXiv:1603.04436

openQuestions: I could not read the Wilson & Fisher 1972 PRL itself - journals.aps.org and link.aps.org both return HTTP 403 to this environment. The statement that the paper contains gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 + O(epsilon^2) is verified from Fisher's own first-person account in the 1998 RMP (whose full text I did read) and from the paper's abstract as summarized in search results. Whether the WF PRL itself prints nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12 in that form is NOT verified; the safest wording in the book is that WF 1972 gives gamma = 1 + epsilon/6, which with eta = O(epsilon^2) is equivalent to nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12.

Terminology hazard worth deciding on deliberately: Wilson (1971b) is a PHASE-SPACE CELL / wave-packet construction with b = 2, not the sharp momentum-shell of textbooks. If the book says 'Wilson integrated out a momentum shell in 1971', that is a modernization. The clean sharp-shell scheme is best cited to Wilson & Kogut (1974), with Wilson (1971b) as its origin.
Wilson & Kogut page range: Crossref gives Physics Reports 12(2), 75-199; a large number of secondary sources (including Fisher's own 1998 bibliography) cite 75-200. Pick one and be consistent.

Wegner's 1976 review chapter, 'The Critical State, General Aspects', in Domb & Green eds., Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena Vol. 6 (Academic, London), pp. 7-124 - which Wilson himself paired with Wegner (1972a) as the source for the formal theory of behavior near fixed points - has no DOI I could locate. Only the 1972 PRB paper is DOI-verified here.

Fisher (1969), the rigorous proof of gamma <= (2 - eta) nu, appears in Fisher's own bibliography as Contemporary Physics Vol. 1, Proc. International Symposium, Trieste, 7-28 June 1968 (IAEA, Vienna), pp. 19-46. No DOI found; cite it as a conference volume or omit.

Griffiths' longer 1965 treatment, 'Ferromagnets and Simple Fluids near the Critical Point: Some Thermodynamic Inequalities', J. Chem. Phys. 43(6), 1958-1968, DOI 10.1063/1.1697060 - I saw the title and DOI in search results but did not resolve the DOI against Crossref as I did for the others. Verify before printing.

Author affiliations for Kadanoff (1966), Rushbrooke (1963), Griffiths (1965), Josephson (1967), Kogut (1974), Pelissetto and Vicari, Guida and Zinn-Justin, and Kos et al. are NOT verified from any source I saw. Crossref returned affiliation strings only for Widom, Fisher (1964, 1998), Wegner and Taeuber. If the book prints affiliations, they need a separate verification pass against the papers' title pages.

The value nu = 0.629971 for the 3D Ising class is my arithmetic from Kos et al.'s Delta_epsilon = 1.412625(10) via nu = 1/(3 - Delta_epsilon); the paper's abstract quotes scaling dimensions, not exponents. If the book prints nu with an uncertainty, propagate it or find a source that states nu directly.

Open pedagogical choice: the (n+2)/6 and (n+8)/6 symmetry factors that produce the 12 are visible in Taeuber's minimal-subtraction Z-factors (Eqs. 65-66), i.e. in the FIELD-THEORETIC half of his notes, whereas the momentum-shell half (Eqs. 44-51) does the Ising case with the bare factors 1/2 and 3/2. If the book wants to derive the 12 from combinatorics rather than assert it, it must pick one scheme and stay in it; mixing the two invites a factor-of-3 error in the quartic vertex.

verdicts.claim: Wilson (1971), 'Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. I. Renormalization Group and the Kadanoff Scaling Picture', Phys. Rev. B 4(9), 3174-3183, 1 Nov 1971, doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174 — recasts Kadanoff block-spin scaling in differential form.
verdicts.correction: Crossref record matches exactly: title, sole author Kenneth G. Wilson, PRB 4(9), 3174-3183, 1971-11-01. INSPIRE abstract confirms the content claim verbatim: 'The Kadanoff theory of scaling near the critical point for an Ising ferromagnet is cast in differential form. The resulting differential equations are an example of the differential equations of the renormalization group.' Fisher's own 1998 bibliography labels this Wilson (1971a). Affiliation on the INSPIRE record is Cornell U., LNS (Laboratory of Nuclear Studies), consistent with the dossier.

verdicts.claim: Wilson (1971), 'Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. II. Phase-Space Cell Analysis of Critical Behavior', Phys. Rev. B 4(9), 3184-3205, doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3184 — wave-packet/phase-space-cell elimination octave by octave (b = 2), nonlinear recursion for effective Landau-Ginzburg potentials, d=3 nu clearly non-classical.
verdicts.correction: Crossref matches exactly. INSPIRE abstract confirms the mechanism claim verbatim: 'An effective interaction is defined by integrating out wave-packet variables with momentum of order 1, leaving unintegrated the variables with momentum <0.5. Then the variables with momentum between 0.25 and 0.5 are integrated, etc. The result is to give a recursion formula for a sequence of effective Landau-Ginsberg-type interactions.' The abstract's d=3 numbers are eta=0, gamma=1.22, nu=0.61 — so 'clearly different from the classical 1/2' is right, and the paper prints Landau-'Ginsberg' (sic). Fisher (1998) labels this Wilson (1971b). The dossier's point that this is NOT the textbook sharp momentum shell is correct.

verdicts.claim: Wilson and Fisher (1972), 'Critical Exponents in 3.99 Dimensions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 28(4), 240-243, 24 Jan 1972, doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.28.240 — contains gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 (Ising-like) and gamma = 1 + epsilon/5 (XY).
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms authors in order (Kenneth G. Wilson, Michael E. Fisher), PRL 28(4), 240-243, 1972-01-24. INSPIRE abstract verbatim: 'Critical exponents are calculated for dimension d=4-epsilon with epsilon small, using renormalization-group techniques. To order epsilon the exponent gamma is 1+(1/6)epsilon for an Ising-like model and 1+(1/5)epsilon for an XY model.' Fisher (1998) independently states 'it contained the first general formula for a nonclassical exponent, namely, gamma = 1 + (1/6)epsilon + O(epsilon^2)'. The dossier's open question stands and is correctly stated: the abstract does NOT print nu = 1/2 + epsilon/12, so the book should quote gamma = 1 + epsilon/6 for this paper.

verdicts.claim: Wilson (1972), 'Feynman-Graph Expansion for Critical Exponents', Phys. Rev. Lett. 28(9), 548-551, 28 Feb 1972, doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.28.548 — gamma to order epsilon^2, eta to order epsilon^3, crossover index phi; n=epsilon=1 gives gamma=1.244, eta=0.037.
verdicts.correction: Crossref matches exactly. INSPIRE abstract verbatim: 'The critical exponents gamma, eta and the crossover index phi are computed for generalized classical Heisenberg models with n internal degrees of freedom as an exact expansion in epsilon=4-d... Results are obtained to order epsilon^2 for gamma and to order epsilon^3 for eta. The results to this order for the three-dimensional Ising case (n=epsilon=1) are gamma=1.244 and eta=0.037.' Every element of the dossier's description, including 'five weeks later' (24 Jan to 28 Feb 1972), checks out. Affiliation: Cornell, Laboratory of Nuclear Studies.

verdicts.claim: Wilson and Kogut (1974), 'The Renormalization Group and the epsilon Expansion', Physics Reports 12(2), 75-199, doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4 — canonical source for the streamlined sharp-cutoff momentum-shell RG; Crossref gives 75-199 while many secondary sources cite 75-200.
verdicts.correction: Bibliographic data confirmed, with two refinements. (1) Authorship: Crossref's legacy Elsevier record lists only 'K. Wilson' — Kogut is missing from Crossref. INSPIRE (record 81239) confirms both authors in order: K.G. Wilson and John B. Kogut. Do not rely on Crossref for the author list here. (2) Page range: Crossref AND INSPIRE both give 75-199 (125 pages, matching the dossier's '125-page' description); Fisher's own 1998 bibliography gives 'Phys. Rep. 12, 75-200' — the dossier's note about that discrepancy is verified true. (3) Affiliations, previously unverified: INSPIRE gives Kogut at Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, and Wilson at both IAS Princeton and Cornell (LNS) — so the byline is not simply 'Cornell' for Wilson on this paper.

verdicts.claim: Kadanoff (1966), 'Scaling laws for Ising models near Tc', Physics Physique Fizika 2(6), 263-272, doi:10.1103/PhysicsPhysiqueFizika.2.263 — cells microscopically large but smaller than the correlation length, cell magnetization as collective variable, 'partial justification for Widom's conjecture', d nu' = gamma' + 2 beta.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms title, sole author Leo P. Kadanoff, vol 2, issue 6, pp. 263-272, 1966. The published abstract confirms the mechanism claim nearly verbatim: 'dividing the Ising model into cells which are microscopically large but much smaller than the coherence length and then using the total magnetization within each cell as a collective variable... serves as a partial justification for Widom's conjecture about the homogeneity of the free energy and at the same time gives his result [d]nu' = gamma' + 2 beta.' Affiliation, previously unverified, is Department of Physics, University of Illinois, Urbana — the dossier's guess was right. Fisher (1998) independently confirms the dossier's 'principal difficulties' quote: the difficulties were 'in explaining the power-law nature of the rescaling factors... and, in particular, in justifying the idea of a single, effective, renormalized coupling J between adjacent block spins.'

verdicts.claim: Widom (1965b), 'Equation of State in the Neighborhood of the Critical Point', J. Chem. Phys. 43(11), 3898-3905, doi:10.1063/1.1696618 — Phi(x,y) homogeneous of positive degree; converts inequalities to equalities; Fisher calls it 'the most direct and phenomenological', 'a bold, new thermodynamic hypothesis'.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms title, author, JCP 43(11), 3898-3905, 1 Dec 1965, and the affiliation string 'Department of Chemistry, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York'. The published abstract confirms the content nearly verbatim: 'A function Phi(x,y) is introduced, with x a measure of the temperature and y of the density. Fluids obeying an equation of state of van der Waals type (classical fluids) are characterized by Phi being a constant. It is suggested that in a real fluid Phi(x,y) is a homogeneous function of x and y, with a positive degree of homogeneity.' Both Fisher quotations verified in the RMP 1998 full text, and Fisher's fn. 20 confirms the Domb & Hunter (1965) / Patashinskii & Pokrovskii (1966) co-attribution.

verdicts.claim: Widom (1965a), 'Surface Tension and Molecular Correlations near the Critical Point', J. Chem. Phys. 43(11), 3892-3897, doi:10.1063/1.1696617 — this, not 1965b, is what Fisher (1998) fn. 88 cites for the hyperscaling equality.
verdicts.correction: Crossref confirms title, author, pages 3892-3897, same issue, same Cornell chemistry affiliation. Fisher (1998) fn. 88 read verbatim from the full text: 'See Kadanoff (1966), Widom (1965a), and Stell (1965, unpublished, quoted in Fisher, 1969, and 1968).'
